P0342.crumb: Amazon raises FBA fees about 3% and cuts…
P0342.title: Amazon raises FBA fees about 3% and cuts some referral fees, effective February 18
P0342.alt: A brass hanging balance scale tips with a stack of coins on one pan and a twine-tied parcel on the other.
P0342.ttag: Amazon raises FBA fees about 3% and cuts some referral fees, effective February 18 | Kwontified
P0342.desc: Amazon told US sellers on December 23, 2019 that its 2020 fee changes take effect on February 18, 2020: fulfillment fees rise by about 3%, select referral…
P0342.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 24, 2019. 2-minute read.
P0342.body:
Amazon told US sellers on December 23, 2019 that its 2020 fee changes take effect on February 18, 2020: fulfillment fees rise by about 3%, select referral fees fall, and storage for standard-size items costs more from January to September, according to Amazon’s notice to sellers. Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) fees are charged by the date a shipment leaves Amazon’s fulfillment center, so orders placed before February 18 that ship afterwards pay the new rates, Feedvisor reported the same day.

What happened

Fulfillment costs more. Amazon described “moderate increases (about 3%)” in fulfillment fees. Per-unit fees rise for small standard, large standard and medium oversize products. Clothing loses its separate $0.40 per-unit surcharge, but its standard-size fees rise, and oversize clothing moves onto the core FBA rates.

Some referral fees fall, a few rise. The share of the price above $75 on shoes, handbags and sunglasses drops from 18% to 15%. Outdoor furniture joins Furniture, paying 10% rather than 15% on the portion above $200. Personal care appliances priced at $10 or less move to the Health & Personal Care rate of 8%, from 15%. Activewear moves the other way, from the 15% Sports & Outdoors rate to the 17% Clothing & Accessories rate, and Amazon Business drops its separate tiered rates for orders above $1,000.

Storage and services change too. Monthly storage for standard-size items rises by $0.06 per cubic foot for January to September, first billed in April for March storage; October to December rates and oversize storage do not change. The FBA label service rises from $0.20 to $0.30 per unit, removal fees fall for standard-size items, and disposal fees rise.

Why it matters for brands

The changes work in opposite directions by price. Referral fees are a share of the price, while fulfillment and storage fees are fixed per unit, so the cuts help expensive items and the increases weigh most on cheap, slow-selling ones.

Apparel brands get two answers at once. Higher-priced shoes and bags gain three points of margin on the portion above $75, while activewear loses two points across its whole price.

What to do now

  1. Recalculate the margin on every Amazon product with the February 18 fees, sorted by price.
  2. Check which activewear, footwear and bag products sit near the $75 line, where the rate now changes.
  3. Lower the advertising budget per sale for any product whose margin falls, before the new fees apply.

P0369.crumb: Amazon limits FBA inbound shipments to…
P0369.title: Amazon limits FBA inbound shipments to household staples, medical supplies and other high-demand products until April 5
P0369.alt: A shrink-wrapped pallet of cardboard boxes beside a yellow pallet jack against a gray wall.
P0369.ttag: Amazon limits FBA inbound shipments to household staples, medical supplies and other high-demand products until April 5 | Kwontified
P0369.desc: Amazon told sellers on March 17, 2020 that its US and European fulfillment centers are “temporarily prioritizing household staples, medical supplies and…
P0369.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 18, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0369.body:
Amazon told sellers on March 17, 2020 that its US and European fulfillment centers are “temporarily prioritizing household staples, medical supplies and other high-demand products,” and that new shipments of other products will be delayed while the change lasts, expected until April 5, CNBC reported, citing a document it obtained. A spokesperson said the change is meant to let Amazon “more quickly receive, restock and ship these products to customers.”

What happened

The restriction covers new inbound shipments. Amazon will keep shipping the inventory already in its warehouses and will receive shipments created before March 17. It applies to third-party sellers and vendors in the US and EU marketplaces.

Some categories are still accepted. Besides household staples and medical supplies, the notice lists baby products, health and household, beauty and personal care, grocery, industrial and scientific, and pet supplies as priority categories.

Demand is the stated reason. The spokesperson said surges in online shopping had left some staples and medical supplies out of stock; on Saturday, March 14, Amazon had already reported shortages and longer-than-usual delivery promises. Sellers of other products can still sell through Fulfilled by Merchant, shipping orders from their own warehouses.

Why it matters for brands

Your FBA stock is now a fixed quantity. For products outside the priority categories, what is in Amazon’s warehouses today is all that can sell through FBA until the change lifts, expected on April 5, so every unit sold brings the stockout date closer. Merchant-fulfilled offers can fill the gap only where a brand has its own stock and shipping.

Advertising spends the fixed stock faster. Ads that keep running on a product that cannot be replenished will sell it out sooner, and once it is out of stock its Sponsored Products ads stop serving and shoppers see it as unavailable.

The priority list is broad, not just essentials. Beauty and personal care, grocery, baby and pet products are on it, so brands in those categories can keep sending stock, but they will compete with the highest-demand items for receiving capacity.

What to do now

  1. Count weeks of cover for every FBA product outside the priority categories, using the last two weeks of sales, and flag any that run out before April 5.
  2. For those products, cut ad budgets and consider pausing promotions so stock lasts, and set up merchant-fulfilled offers from your own warehouse where you can ship to Amazon’s standards.
  3. For products in priority categories, create inbound shipments now and expect slower receiving than usual.

P0381.title: Amazon will let more non-essential products into FBA this week, in capped quantities
P0381.alt: An open cardboard box spilling kraft packing paper beside a roll of tape on a sunlit wooden bench.
P0381.ttag: Amazon will let more non-essential products into FBA this week, in capped quantities | Kwontified
P0381.desc: Amazon said on April 13, 2020 that it will let more products into its fulfillment centers later this week, easing the March limit that kept most…
P0381.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 14, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0381.body:
Amazon said on April 13, 2020 that it will let more products into its fulfillment centers later this week, easing the March limit that kept most non-essential items out of FBA, with quantities capped, Engadget reported from the company’s statement to The Wall Street Journal. The same day, Amazon said it had hired 100,000 people in four weeks and will hire 75,000 more, TechCrunch reported.

What happened

The door reopens, partly. “Later this week, we will allow more products into our fulfillment centers,” an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that “products will be limited by quantity” so Amazon can keep prioritizing essential items and protecting employees. Sellers of items outside health, wellness and cleaning can again send inventory, The Motley Fool reported, citing the Journal. Amazon has not said what the caps are or exactly which day the change starts.

The March rule ran longer than planned. On March 17, Amazon stopped creating new inbound shipments for FBA sellers and vendors outside six categories (baby, health and household, beauty and personal care, grocery, industrial and scientific, and pet supplies), and set April 5 as a tentative end date, TechCrunch reported. April 5 passed without a change.

Capacity is growing. Amazon said it has filled the 100,000 jobs it announced on March 16 and is adding 75,000 more, and that its spending on higher pay and related costs now tops $500 million.

Why it matters for brands

Restocking returns before full stock does. With a cap per product, a brand that sold out of a best seller in March may be able to send only part of what it needs, so the stockout shortens rather than ends.

The first units in will set the next weeks of sales. Inventory that arrives this month competes with shoppers’ extended delivery estimates, which reached 30 days on some items in late March, so products that reach FBA first regain the Prime badge and the faster promise first.

Ad plans built around stockouts need a second look. Campaigns paused or restructured while products were out of stock can come back as stock lands, but only for the products and quantities Amazon actually accepts.

What to do now

  1. Rank every out-of-stock FBA product by margin and sales rate, and decide which ones get the first, limited shipments.
  2. Check Seller Central daily this week for which products are open for new shipments and at what quantity, and create shipments as soon as they are allowed.
  3. Restart advertising product by product as each shipment is received, not when the shipment is created.

P0397.title: Facebook launches Shops, one free storefront across Facebook and Instagram
P0397.alt: A phone on a small flexible tripod beside white canvas sneakers on a white block against a pink wall.
P0397.ttag: Facebook launches Shops, one free storefront across Facebook and Instagram | Kwontified
P0397.desc: Facebook launched Facebook Shops on May 19, 2020, letting a business set up one online store that shoppers can reach from its Facebook Page and its…
P0397.kicker: News. Creative and conversion. Instagram Shop
P0397.byline: By Kwontified. Published May 20, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0397.body:
Facebook launched Facebook Shops on May 19, 2020, letting a business set up one online store that shoppers can reach from its Facebook Page and its Instagram profile, as well as through stories and ads, according to Facebook’s announcement. Mark Zuckerberg presented Shops in a livestream as a way for small businesses closed by the lockdowns to keep an income, The Next Web reported.

What happened

Setting up a Shop is free. A business chooses products from its catalog and adds a cover image and accent colors to match its brand, Facebook said. Shoppers can complete the order on the business’s own website or, in the US, inside the app where the business has turned on Checkout.

Messaging is part of the store. Shoppers can ask questions, get support and track deliveries through WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram Direct, and Facebook said it plans to let them buy inside those chats in the future.

Commerce platforms are the on-ramp. Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, ChannelAdvisor, CedCommerce, Cafe24, Tienda Nube and Feedonomics will help businesses build and manage their Shops. Rollout began on May 19 and will widen “in the coming months.”

Instagram gets its own storefront. Instagram Shop, a shopping section in Explore with curated collections and category filters, is coming to the US this summer, and Facebook is testing product tags in live video.

Why it matters for brands

Social profiles become storefronts. A brand’s Facebook Page and Instagram profile can now carry a full catalog instead of a link in the bio.

The product catalog does double duty. The same catalog that feeds a brand’s Facebook and Instagram ads will now also stock its Shop, so errors in titles, images or prices show up in both places at once.

Checkout decides who keeps the customer. A shopper who checks out inside the app buys without leaving Facebook or Instagram, while one sent to the brand’s website buys there. Which option a brand enables shapes what it learns about the buyer and where the next purchase begins.

What to do now

  1. Audit the product catalog connected to your Facebook and Instagram accounts: titles, images, prices and stock status.
  2. Decide whether orders should finish in the app or on your site, based on what you need from the customer relationship.
  3. Ask your commerce platform when its Facebook Shops integration will be available for your account.

P0398.crumb: Walmart will discontinue Jet.com as US…
P0398.title: Walmart will discontinue Jet.com as US e-commerce sales rise 74%
P0398.alt: A blue shopping basket of bread, apples, milk, and a bottle on a yellow stool against a bright blue wall.
P0398.ttag: Walmart will discontinue Jet.com as US e-commerce sales rise 74% | Kwontified
P0398.desc: Walmart said on May 19, 2020 that it will discontinue Jet.com, the online retailer it bought in 2016 for $3.3 billion, as it reported a 74% rise in US…
P0398.byline: By Kwontified. Published May 20, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0398.body:
Walmart said on May 19, 2020 that it will discontinue Jet.com, the online retailer it bought in 2016 for $3.3 billion, as it reported a 74% rise in US e-commerce sales for its first quarter. “One decision we’ve made is to discontinue Jet.com,” chief executive Doug McMillon said, Supermarket News reported.

What happened

The Walmart brand won the internal contest. McMillon said the company’s resources, people and financials have gone to the Walmart brand “because it has so much traction,” and that the Jet name “may still be used in the future,” according to Supermarket News. He credited the Jet acquisition with jump-starting Walmart’s e-commerce progress and said he did not expect a significant accounting charge.

The wind-down was already under way. Walmart had been unwinding the Jet unit for about 18 months, and most Jet employees had already moved into Walmart.com operations, Talk Business & Politics reported.

Walmart.com is where the growth is. US e-commerce sales rose 74% in the quarter, and Walmart US comparable sales rose 10%, its best performance in almost 20 years, Fortune reported. McMillon said the number of new customers trying pickup and delivery had increased four times since mid-March, and that marketplace growth outpaced the overall business.

Why it matters for brands

One Walmart storefront to manage. Brands that sold on Jet kept a second Walmart-owned channel with its own listings and pricing. Walmart has now told the market that Walmart.com is the brand it will invest in.

Marketplace is the growth line. With marketplace sales outpacing the business and the number of new pickup and delivery customers up fourfold since mid-March, the Walmart.com product page is where Walmart’s online shoppers will meet a brand this year.

Content and pricing on Walmart.com carry more weight. A brand whose Walmart.com listings were set up by a reseller, or never set up at all, has less reason than ever to leave them that way.

What to do now

  1. If you sell on Jet.com, contact your Walmart or Jet partner team to confirm how and when your listings and open orders will be handled.
  2. Review your Walmart.com listings for titles, images, price and stock, and check who is selling your products there.
  3. Decide whether to sell on Walmart Marketplace directly if you rely today on wholesale to Walmart or on resellers.

P0409.title: Walmart opens its marketplace to Shopify merchants and expects 1,200 to join this year
P0409.alt: Trestle table with wooden crates, ceramic bowls, folded towels and woven baskets against a sunlit terracotta wall.
P0409.ttag: Walmart opens its marketplace to Shopify merchants and expects 1,200 to join this year | Kwontified
P0409.desc: Walmart and Shopify said on June 15, 2020 that US merchants on Shopify can now apply to sell on Walmart.com through a new sales channel inside Shopify,…
P0409.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 16, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0409.body:
Walmart and Shopify said on June 15, 2020 that US merchants on Shopify can now apply to sell on Walmart.com through a new sales channel inside Shopify, making Shopify the first commerce platform Walmart has partnered with to bring small and medium-sized businesses onto its marketplace, according to Shopify’s announcement. Walmart expects to add 1,200 Shopify sellers in 2020, Walmart Marketplace vice president Jeff Clementz told Talk Business & Politics.

What happened

Shopify merchants get a direct route in. Approved merchants connect their Shopify store to a Walmart seller account, and Shopify keeps product listings synced with Walmart.com while orders, inventory and fulfillment are tracked inside Shopify, the announcement said. Listing information, including variants, can be added in bulk.

The fees stay the same. Walmart charges marketplace sellers no monthly fee to list products and takes a referral fee only when an item sells. Shopify put Walmart.com’s audience at more than 120 million Americans a month.

Walmart is growing the marketplace on purpose. “Growing our Marketplace is a strategic priority, and we are going to be smart as we grow,” Clementz said, adding that Walmart would “start integrating new sellers now.”

The move follows a strong quarter online. Walmart’s US e-commerce sales rose 74% in the three months to April 30, the company said on May 19, Supermarket News reported. In February Walmart also opened a fulfillment service that stores and ships marketplace sellers’ goods for a fee and tags them for two-day delivery, Modern Retail reported.

Why it matters for brands

More sellers will list on the same items. Shopify merchants include resellers and small retailers as well as brands, so some of the 1,200 new sellers will offer products that a brand already sells on Walmart.com, on the same item page and at prices the brand does not set.

The route to Walmart got shorter for direct-to-consumer brands. A brand that runs its own site on Shopify can now manage a Walmart listing from the same catalog and inventory, which lowers the cost of testing the marketplace.

Walmart is choosing who gets in. Sellers must be approved, and the target of 1,200 is small next to the more than one million small businesses Shopify serves, so early entrants will compete with fewer rivals than they would on Amazon.

What to do now

  1. Search Walmart.com for your top 20 items this week and record which sellers appear on each page and at what price, so new sellers can be spotted as they arrive.
  2. If your own store runs on Shopify, apply for the Walmart channel and compare Walmart’s referral fees with your margin on each item before listing.
  3. Make sure the brand’s own content on Walmart.com, from titles and images to descriptions, is complete, since new sellers will list against the page you have.

P0422.crumb: Instagram opens a Shop in Explore, with…
P0422.title: Instagram opens a Shop in Explore, with in-app checkout through Facebook Pay
P0422.alt: A phone on a small flexible tripod beside white canvas sneakers on a white block against a pink wall.
P0422.ttag: Instagram opens a Shop in Explore, with in-app checkout through Facebook Pay | Kwontified
P0422.desc: Instagram began rolling out a redesigned Instagram Shop in the US on July 16, 2020, a shopping destination inside the app’s Explore section where people…
P0422.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 17, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0422.body:
Instagram began rolling out a redesigned Instagram Shop in the US on July 16, 2020, a shopping destination inside the app’s Explore section where people can browse products from brands and creators and, for some sellers, check out without leaving the app, paying with Facebook Pay, TechCrunch reported. Instagram had also begun testing, in early July, a navigation bar that replaces the Activity tab with a dedicated Shop tab.

What happened

Shopping gets its own place in the app. Instagram Shop sits in Explore and shows rows of favorite brands and creators, collections curated by Instagram’s own @shop account, category filters such as beauty and home, and a “Suggested For You” section, according to TechCrunch. Until the Shop tab reaches everyone, shoppers reach it through Explore.

Checkout runs on Facebook Pay. US users can pay for purchases inside Instagram with Facebook Pay, which Facebook introduced in November 2019 to handle payments across its apps. Sellers that use Instagram’s own Checkout pay a selling fee; TechCrunch linked to Facebook’s help page for the amount but did not state it.

It builds on two earlier steps. Instagram Checkout opened as a closed beta with about 20 brands in March 2019, Tubefilter reported, and Facebook announced free Shops for Facebook and Instagram on May 19, 2020. Instagram Shop is where those storefronts and products now gather for shoppers.

Why it matters for brands

Instagram now has a shelf, not just a feed. Until now a product reached an Instagram shopper mostly through a post or an ad the shopper happened to see. A browsable destination with categories and recommendations means a brand’s product catalog can be found by people who were not looking for the brand, much as a marketplace search would find it.

The catalog becomes the merchandising. What appears in Instagram Shop comes from the products a brand has tagged and the catalog behind them, so product names, images and prices maintained for Instagram now do the work a store planogram does.

Instagram, not the brand, holds the checkout. When a purchase completes inside the app, the payment and the transaction data pass through Facebook Pay, and the brand pays a selling fee on the sale. Brands weighing in-app checkout are trading some control of the customer relationship for less friction at the moment of purchase.

What to do now

  1. Check that every product in your Instagram catalog has a current image, price and stock status, since the catalog now feeds a browsable shop.
  2. Decide whether to use in-app checkout or send shoppers to your own site, and find out the current selling fee before you decide.
  3. Open Explore in the Instagram app each week and look at which brands and collections appear in your categories.

P0445.title: Walmart launches Walmart+ on September 15: free same-day delivery from stores for $98 a year
P0445.alt: A blue shopping basket of bread, apples, milk, and a bottle on a yellow stool against a bright blue wall.
P0445.ttag: Walmart launches Walmart+ on September 15: free same-day delivery from stores for $98 a year | Kwontified
P0445.desc: Walmart announced Walmart+ on September 1, 2020, a membership that will cost $98 a year or $12.95 a month and opens to all US customers on September 15,…
P0445.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 2, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0445.body:
Walmart announced Walmart+ on September 1, 2020, a membership that will cost $98 a year or $12.95 a month and opens to all US customers on September 15, TechCrunch reported. Members get free same-day delivery from stores, a fuel discount and checkout-free shopping in stores, with a 15-day free trial. The program replaces Delivery Unlimited, Walmart’s existing $98 grocery delivery subscription, whose members move into Walmart+ automatically.

What happened

Delivery from the store is the core benefit. Members pay no delivery fee on orders of $35 or more, picked by store staff and delivered by partners such as Postmates, DoorDash and Roadie. More than 160,000 items are eligible at launch, from groceries to toys and electronics, and about 2,700 of Walmart’s 4,700-plus US stores offer delivery, according to TechCrunch.

Two benefits are about the store visit itself. Members save up to 5 cents a gallon at nearly 2,000 Walmart, Murphy USA and Murphy Express fuel stations, with Sam’s Club stations to follow. They can also use Scan & Go: scan items with the Walmart app while shopping and pay with Walmart Pay, without a checkout line.

Walmart did not add new shipping benefits for Walmart.com orders. Free one- or two-day shipping on orders of $35 or more is already open to every customer, membership or not. Janey Whiteside, Walmart’s chief customer officer, called the program “the ultimate life hack” for customers, Talk Business & Politics reported. Amazon Prime costs $119 a year by comparison.

Why it matters for brands

Walmart+ is built around the store shelf. The products members can get the same day are the ones a Walmart store carries, so a brand’s store assortment and store in-stock rate decide whether it is part of the member’s routine order. Items sold only on Walmart.com, including those listed by marketplace sellers, sit outside the headline benefit.

The membership gives Walmart a list of its most frequent customers. Every member’s fuel stop, store trip and delivery order runs through the Walmart app, which tells Walmart more about who shops it most and how. That is information a retailer with an advertising business, Walmart Media Group, can put to use over time.

It also raises the stakes on basket size. A $35 minimum per free delivery rewards brands whose products are added to a weekly grocery basket, and makes a single low-priced item ordered on its own less likely.

What to do now

  1. List which of your items are carried in Walmart stores near your largest customer areas and check their store in-stock rates, since those are the items members can order the same day.
  2. Review your Walmart.com item pages for the products shoppers add to a grocery basket, and make sure images and titles work on the app.
  3. Ask your Walmart contacts how Walmart+ members will be identified in reporting and media options once the program launches on September 15.

P0454.title: Amazon Accelerate 2020: Brand Follow, repeat-purchase data and $100 million to promote small sellers
P0454.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
P0454.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2020: Brand Follow, repeat-purchase data and $100 million to promote small sellers | Kwontified
P0454.desc: Amazon opened Amazon Accelerate, a new virtual conference for US sellers, on September 1, 2020 with two tools for brand owners and a promise to spend an…
P0454.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 4, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0454.body:
Amazon opened Amazon Accelerate, a new virtual conference for US sellers, on September 1, 2020 with two tools for brand owners and a promise to spend an extra $100 million promoting small businesses around Prime Day and the holidays, Amazon said. The free three-day event ran from September 1 to 3, with more than 25,000 entrepreneurs and brand owners expected to attend.

What happened

Amazon introduced Brand Follow, which it described as an investment in customer relationship management tools. It lets sellers reach shoppers who have shown interest in their brand, through features such as personalized posts on the Amazon homepage. Alongside it, Repeat Purchase Behavior gives sellers data on how customers come back to their brands.

The company said it is on course to invest $18 billion in 2020 to help independent businesses sell, has released more than 135 tools and services for sellers this year, and will provide guidance and support to more than 500,000 US small and medium-sized sellers over the next twelve months while bringing on 100,000 new ones. The additional $100 million will promote small businesses during Prime Day and the holiday season, with details closer to Prime Day, whose 2020 date Amazon has not announced. Third-party sellers passed $2 billion in global sales during Prime Day 2019, according to the release.

Jeff Wilke, chief executive of Amazon’s worldwide consumer business, opened the event in conversation with Dharmesh Mehta, who leads customer trust and partner support. Other sessions covered building a brand in Amazon’s store, with Amazon Fashion president Christine Beauchamp, and the future of Fulfillment by Amazon, Amazon said when it announced the program. US small and medium-sized sellers sold more than 3.4 billion products in the twelve months to May, with average sales of $160,000, up from about $100,000.

Why it matters for brands

Amazon is giving brands a way to talk to their own customers again. Until now, a shopper who bought a brand’s product on Amazon was Amazon’s customer, reachable mainly through paid ads. Brand Follow and Repeat Purchase Behavior are first steps toward letting the brand see and reach its returning buyers inside Amazon.

The $100 million is promotion Amazon will place, not cash for sellers. Brands that qualify as small businesses may get extra visibility around Prime Day, on terms Amazon has not yet published.

What to do now

  1. Confirm your brand is enrolled in Brand Registry and that the right people can see Brand Analytics, where repeat purchase data is likely to live.
  2. Start publishing Posts and keep your Store current, since followers will see what you post.
  3. Ask your Amazon contacts how a brand qualifies for the small-business promotion before Prime Day planning closes.

P0458.crumb: Amazon sets Prime Day 2020 for October…
P0458.title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2020 for October 13-14, with a $10 credit for buying from small businesses first
P0458.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
P0458.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Day 2020 for October 13-14, with a $10 credit for buying from small businesses first | Kwontified
P0458.desc: Amazon will hold Prime Day 2020 on October 13 and 14, starting at midnight Pacific time on the Tuesday, the company announced on September 28, 2020, CBS…
P0458.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 29, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0458.body:
Amazon will hold Prime Day 2020 on October 13 and 14, starting at midnight Pacific time on the Tuesday, the company announced on September 28, 2020, CBS News and the AP reported. It is the first Prime Day held in the fall, moved from its usual July slot because of the pandemic, and it runs in 19 countries, including Brazil and Turkey for the first time.

What happened

The event now sits in the fourth quarter, two weeks after Amazon’s announcement and about six weeks before Black Friday. Jeff Wilke, chief executive of Amazon’s worldwide consumer business, said October “is the perfect opportunity for Prime members to get their holiday shopping done early from the comfort of their homes.” Amazon said Prime members would see more than a million deals.

Small businesses get a promotion that starts immediately. From September 28 through October 12, Prime members who spend $10 on items sold by select small businesses in Amazon’s store receive a $10 credit to use on Prime Day, fully funded by Amazon, Pulse 2.0 reported. Wilke said Amazon was committed to making this “the most successful Prime Day ever for our small businesses.” Amazon had said at its Accelerate seller conference on September 1 that it would spend an extra $100 million promoting small businesses during Prime Day and the holiday season.

Other retailers are already moving. Target and Walmart said they would launch holiday discounts earlier than usual, and Walmart said 87% of its customers planned to look for deals before Black Friday, Retail Dive reported. AlixPartners included October in its holiday sales projections for the first time.

Why it matters for brands

Two weeks is a short runway. Brands that waited for a date now have about 14 days to settle deal depth, ad budgets and the inventory that has to be checked in at Amazon’s warehouses before the event starts. Deals already submitted for later in the season may need to move.

The holiday season now opens in mid-October. With Target and Walmart pulling their own deals forward, Prime Day becomes the first of several overlapping events rather than a summer peak of its own, and some shoppers who buy on October 13 would otherwise have bought in late November.

Small sellers have a reason to run ads before the event, not only during it. The $10 credit rewards shoppers for buying from small businesses between now and October 12, so a small brand’s traffic and ad returns may rise in the two weeks before Prime Day.

What to do now

  1. Confirm today which products will carry Prime Day deals and check that their stock will be checked in at Amazon’s warehouses before October 13.
  2. Set the event ad budget as part of the fourth-quarter total, with a share held back for Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
  3. If your brand qualifies as a small business on Amazon, plan advertising for the September 28 to October 12 window when the $10 credit applies.

P0475.crumb: Amazon’s second AdCon ran online and…
P0475.title: Amazon’s second AdCon ran online and steered brands toward streaming TV and video ads
P0475.alt: Empty wooden picture frame and a twine-tied cardboard parcel leaning against a sunlit mustard-yellow wall.
P0475.ttag: Amazon’s second AdCon ran online and steered brands toward streaming TV and video ads | Kwontified
P0475.desc: Amazon Advertising opened AdCon 2020, its second annual conference for advertisers, online on September 30, 2020, and used it to push brands beyond search…
P0475.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 1, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0475.body:
Amazon Advertising opened AdCon 2020, its second annual conference for advertisers, online on September 30, 2020, and used it to push brands beyond search ads toward streaming TV, video and brand-building formats. In a recap posted the same day, five Amazon Ads leaders each named what advertisers should take away, and the one figure Amazon offered was its own: a 22% increase in new-to-brand customers for ad campaigns run since March 1, compared with the previous six months, Amazon said.

What happened

The conference moved online. Amazon had planned AdCon 2020 as a two-day, invitation-only event on September 30 and October 1 and held it online because of COVID-19, Business Insider reported in August, when the event site opened with a September 28 registration deadline and no published agenda. The first AdCon, in 2019, was a smaller gathering of several hundred brands and agencies.

The advice pointed up the funnel. Amazon’s recap told advertisers to experiment. It described streaming TV ads (OTT) as affordable, measurable and able to reach scale, against linear TV, which it said had required significant budgets. And it paired Amazon’s free brand tools (Posts, Stores, Follow and Amazon Live) with paid formats, Sponsored Brands video and Streaming TV ads, as the way to extend a brand’s story to new customers and turn them into loyal ones.

The timing is not subtle. The conference ran two weeks before Prime Day, which Amazon set for October 13 and 14 in an announcement on September 28, with early deals already running. Amazon’s “other” revenue line, which mainly holds advertising, reached $4.22 billion in the second quarter, up 41% from a year earlier, according to its second-quarter results.

Why it matters for brands

Amazon is selling reach, not only clicks. Sponsored Products answer a shopper who is already searching. Streaming TV and video ask a brand to pay to be remembered before the search, which is the budget that brand and media teams have traditionally held.

The 22% figure needs reading with care. It is Amazon’s own aggregate, it compares the pandemic months, when shoppers who were stuck at home moved their buying online, with the six months before, and it does not say how much of the gain the ads caused. Brands should expect their own new-to-brand numbers to look better in 2020 for reasons that have little to do with ad format.

What to do now

  1. Check new-to-brand share in your Sponsored Brands reporting for March through September against the six months before, so you know your own baseline before anyone quotes Amazon’s.
  2. If you test Sponsored Brands video or Streaming TV ads before the holidays, fix the measurement first: a defined budget, a set period and a comparison against products or weeks without the ads.
  3. Keep Prime Day budgets in Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands, where the October 13–14 demand will show up, and treat upper-funnel tests as a separate line.

P0467.body:
Amazon’s first October Prime Day ended at midnight Pacific time on October 14, 2020, after 48 hours of deals in 19 countries. Amazon had not published any results by the close. The only public data so far are early readings from a shopper panel, so everything below is preliminary and will be revised when Amazon and outside analysts report.

What happened

The event ran on the dates Amazon set on September 28: from midnight PT on October 13 through October 14, with more than one million deals and, for the first time, shoppers in Turkey and Brazil, according to Amazon’s announcement. Amazon put more than $100 million into Prime Day and holiday promotions, including a $10 credit for members who spent $10 with selected small businesses beforehand.

Early panel data showed steady ordering. Numerator, which tracks purchases from a panel of shoppers, had logged more than 2,200 verified Prime Day orders by 2:15 p.m. Eastern on October 13, with an average order of $45.19, later updated to $45.83, and two in five participating households had already placed two or more orders, Digital Commerce 360 reported. These are first-day figures from one panel and do not measure total sales.

The forecast to beat is large. eMarketer expected Prime Day 2020 to bring in $9.91 billion worldwide and $6.17 billion in the US, against $6.93 billion and $4.32 billion in 2019, TechCrunch reported on October 6.

Rivals ran alongside. Target held its Deal Days on the same two days and Walmart’s Big Save event runs through October 15. On October 14, Walmart also said its Black Friday would become three events starting online on November 4, November 11 and November 25, the Associated Press reported.

Why it matters for brands

Prime Day 2020 is the first holiday-season Prime Day, so its results will be read as the opening of Q4, not as a summer event. Total sales figures, when Amazon releases them, will not show how much was pulled forward from November, and that matters more this year than any headline number.

What to do now

  1. Pull your own Prime Day sales by product and compare them with the plan before reading anyone else’s numbers.
  2. Recalculate weeks of cover through December and book inbound shipments for the products that sold through.
  3. Treat outside estimates as preliminary until Amazon reports, and keep this week’s figures out of November budgets until the post-event weeks are in.

P0479.crumb: Amazon sets Black Friday Deals Week for…
P0479.title: Amazon sets Black Friday Deals Week for November 20 to 27, weeks after Walmart and Target opened theirs
P0479.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
P0479.ttag: Amazon sets Black Friday Deals Week for November 20 to 27, weeks after Walmart and Target opened theirs | Kwontified
P0479.desc: Amazon will run its US Black Friday Deals Week from Friday, November 20 through Black Friday, November 27, releasing tens of thousands of deals with new…
P0479.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 17, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0479.body:
Amazon will run its US Black Friday Deals Week from Friday, November 20 through Black Friday, November 27, releasing tens of thousands of deals with new ones added daily and many lasting only 24 hours, Amazon announced on November 16. The release names no Amazon-wide Cyber Monday event; Cyber Monday falls on November 30.

What happened

Amazon set out the week’s mechanics: deals at amazon.com/blackfriday, a “Black Friday Deal” badge on top offers, and Alexa-exclusive deals for shoppers who ask for them. Small Business Holiday Deals run from November 26 to 30. Most items shipped between October 1 and December 31 can be returned until January 31, 2021, and Prime members get free one-day delivery on more than 10 million eligible items.

Amazon is the last of the big three to fix its dates. Walmart said on October 14 that its Black Friday would be three events, starting online on November 4, November 11 and November 25, the Associated Press reported. Target is running a new set of “Black Friday Now” deals each week of November, with price adjustments through December 24, Target said on October 29. Adobe expects $56 billion of US online sales between November 1 and 22, before any of Thanksgiving week, and $12.7 billion on Cyber Monday alone, in its forecast.

Why it matters for brands

Amazon’s peak is an eight-day window that opens this Friday, while Walmart and Target shoppers have been seeing Black Friday prices since the first week of November. A brand selling on all three now has its holiday price on display somewhere for most of the month, and a shopper comparing tabs will find the lowest one.

Deals that last 24 hours concentrate traffic into single days. A product’s best day of the week will be the day its deal runs, so ad budgets and bids need to be set by day, not for the week.

The extended return window also moves risk into January: gifts bought in late November can come back for two months.

What to do now

  1. Confirm by Thursday which products have Black Friday deals on Amazon and on which days, and set daily ad budgets for those days rather than spreading a weekly budget evenly.
  2. Check that your Amazon deal price is not above the price Walmart or Target is showing for the same item that week.
  3. Keep a budget reserve for Cyber Monday, November 30, which Amazon has not yet scheduled and Adobe expects to be the largest online day of the year.
  4. Plan January replenishment net of returns, given the January 31 return deadline.

P0491.crumb: Early read: Cyber Week 2020 sets online…
P0491.title: Early read: Cyber Week 2020 sets online records on Thanksgiving and Black Friday, below Adobe’s October forecast (preliminary)
P0491.alt: Blue, red and orange paper shopping bags lined up on a weathered wooden bench against a sunlit cream wall.
P0491.ttag: Early read: Cyber Week 2020 sets online records on Thanksgiving and Black Friday, below Adobe’s October forecast (preliminary) | Kwontified
P0491.desc: US shoppers spent a record $9 billion online on Black Friday, November 27, up 21.6% on 2019, and $5.1 billion on Thanksgiving Day, according to Adobe…
P0491.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 1, 2020. 2-minute read.
P0491.body:
US shoppers spent a record $9 billion online on Black Friday, November 27, up 21.6% on 2019, and $5.1 billion on Thanksgiving Day, according to Adobe Analytics data reported by TechCrunch on November 28. Both are records for those days. Black Friday still landed below the $10 billion, 39% growth, that Adobe had forecast on October 28. This early read covers Thanksgiving through Black Friday only. Cyber Monday totals and Amazon’s own figures were not out when it was written, so treat it as preliminary.

What happened

Adobe, which tracks spending on large US retail sites, said Black Friday was the second-biggest online shopping day in US history, behind Cyber Monday 2019. Online spending passed $3 billion on each day of the week before Thanksgiving. Purchases on smartphones reached $3.6 billion on Black Friday, up 25.3%, about 40% of the day’s online sales, and orders collected in store or at the curb rose 52% on 2019. The result sat inside a later Adobe range of $8.9 billion to $9.6 billion for the day. Adobe expects Cyber Monday to bring in $10.8 billion to $12.7 billion, up 15% to 35%, CNBC reported.

Stores told the other half of the story. Shopper visits to physical stores fell 52.1% on Black Friday and 94.9% on Thanksgiving Day, when many large chains stayed closed, according to preliminary Sensormatic Solutions counts reported by CNBC.

The comparison with Adobe’s October forecast matters more than the record. Adobe expected the season, November 1 to December 31, to reach $189 billion online, up 33%, with discounts arriving early in November. Retailers did spread the event out: Walmart ran three Black Friday events starting online on November 4, the Associated Press reported in October, and Black Friday growth came in at roughly half the rate Adobe had forecast for the day.

Why it matters for brands

A record that falls short of its forecast suggests the demand moved rather than disappeared. Shoppers who were offered Black Friday prices for most of November bought across the month, so Black Friday itself carried a smaller share of the season. Brands that judge the weekend against 2019’s single-day peaks will read their results as weaker than they are.

The store numbers also explain why curbside and in-store pickup grew so fast. For brands sold through big-box retailers, the same unit now moves through an online order even when it leaves a store shelf.

What to do now

  1. Measure Cyber Week 2020 from November 1, not from Thanksgiving, and compare it with the same weeks of 2019 in total.
  2. Check stock on every product that sold through over the weekend before raising December ad budgets.
  3. Hold judgment on Cyber Monday until Adobe and Amazon publish their own figures this week, and update this read when they do.

A0005.crumb: Walmart renames its ad business Walmart…
A0005.title: Walmart renames its ad business Walmart Connect and plans a DSP with The Trade Desk
A0005.alt: Metal and wood shelving of amber, green, white and black bottles with blank labels and kraft boxes against a blue wall
A0005.ttag: Walmart renames its ad business Walmart Connect and plans a DSP with The Trade Desk | Kwontified
A0005.desc: On January 28, 2021, Walmart renamed its media business, previously Walmart Media Group, as Walmart Connect and set out plans to become one of the top ten…
A0005.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jan 29, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0005.body:
On January 28, 2021, Walmart renamed its media business, previously Walmart Media Group, as Walmart Connect and set out plans to become one of the top ten advertising platforms in the United States, according to Walmart’s announcement.

What Walmart announced

Walmart described three areas of growth. On its own site, app and pickup and delivery service, Walmart Connect sells search and display media; Walmart said this part of the business nearly doubled its revenue and more than doubled its number of advertisers in its last fiscal year. In stores, advertisers can now buy placements on in-store TV walls and self-checkout screens, nearly 170,000 digital screens across more than 4,500 stores. Off Walmart’s properties, Walmart announced a partnership with The Trade Desk to launch a demand-side platform (DSP) for suppliers and their agencies in time for the 2021 holiday season, using Walmart’s shopping data to target and measure ads elsewhere on the internet.

Walmart tied the plan to its wider strategy: Walmart+ to build loyal customers and shopper data, and a growing marketplace to add more sellers who can advertise.

Why it matters for brands

Walmart is telling brands it wants to be judged as a media company, not only as a store. Brands that sell at Walmart will be asked for budget across three places at once, on the site, in the stores and across the web, and the pitch will rest on closed-loop measurement: ads connected to Walmart purchase data. That claim deserves the same scrutiny brands give Amazon’s: attributed sales are not the same as sales the ads caused.

The DSP matters most for planning. Until now, a brand’s Walmart advertising has largely stayed on Walmart’s own properties. A DSP built on Walmart’s data would compete for budgets currently spent on Amazon DSP and on general programmatic buying.

What to do now

  1. Ask your Walmart Connect contact what measurement will be available for in-store screens and for the DSP, and when.
  2. Decide which budget would fund Walmart off-site media in the 2021 holiday season, before the sales conversation starts.
  3. Treat Walmart’s attributed results as a starting point and plan a holdout test for any new spend.

A0014.crumb: Jeff Bezos to hand Amazon’s CEO role to…
A0014.title: Jeff Bezos to hand Amazon’s CEO role to Andy Jassy in the third quarter
A0014.alt: An open cardboard box spilling kraft packing paper beside a roll of tape on a sunlit wooden bench.
A0014.ttag: Jeff Bezos to hand Amazon’s CEO role to Andy Jassy in the third quarter | Kwontified
A0014.desc: On February 2, 2021, Amazon said founder Jeff Bezos will become executive chair in the third quarter of 2021 and Andy Jassy, who leads Amazon Web…
A0014.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 3, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0014.body:
On February 2, 2021, Amazon said founder Jeff Bezos will become executive chair in the third quarter of 2021 and Andy Jassy, who leads Amazon Web Services, will become chief executive at that time, in its fourth-quarter results release.

What Amazon announced

The leadership change came with Amazon’s largest quarter on record. Net sales rose 44% to $125.6 billion in the fourth quarter of 2020. The “other” revenue line, which Amazon says is mostly advertising, grew 66% to $7.95 billion. Third-party seller services grew 57% to $27.3 billion, and sellers accounted for 55% of paid units.

Amazon said independent sellers had their best holiday season ever, with worldwide sales up more than 50% and more than $4.8 billion in sales from Black Friday through Cyber Monday. It also repeated that it had postponed its annual selling fee adjustments until June 2021.

Why it matters for brands

For brands, the change of chief executive is less important in the short term than the numbers released alongside it. Advertising grew faster than any other major line in the quarter, and sellers now account for most of what Amazon sells. Both trends mean more competition for the same shoppers in 2021.

The longer-term question is how Amazon’s priorities shift under a leader whose career has been in cloud computing rather than retail. Bezos will stay as executive chair, and Amazon described the move as a transition rather than a departure. Brands should not expect sudden changes to the marketplace, its fees or its advertising.

What to do now

  1. Plan for continued growth in Amazon advertising costs in 2021, given that advertising grew faster than units sold in the fourth quarter.
  2. Keep modeling the fee changes Amazon has scheduled for June 2021.
  3. Watch Amazon’s first-quarter results, due in the spring, for any change in how it reports advertising or seller services.

A0050.title: Apple’s App Tracking Transparency goes live with iOS 14.5
A0050.alt: Trestle table with wooden crates, ceramic bowls, folded towels and woven baskets against a sunlit terracotta wall.
A0050.ttag: Apple’s App Tracking Transparency goes live with iOS 14.5 | Kwontified
A0050.desc: On April 26, 2021, Apple released iOS 14.5, which requires apps to ask iPhone and iPad users for permission before tracking their activity across other…
A0050.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 27, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0050.body:
On April 26, 2021, Apple released iOS 14.5, which requires apps to ask iPhone and iPad users for permission before tracking their activity across other companies’ apps and websites, the PA news agency reported.

What Apple released

The feature, called App Tracking Transparency, shows users a prompt asking whether an app may track them outside the app, with a short explanation from the developer of why it wants to. Apple’s chief privacy officer told PA earlier in April that users should have transparency about how their data is used and control over whether it is used for tracking.

Apple had told developers on April 20 that all apps must use the App Tracking Transparency framework to request permission to track users or to access the device’s advertising identifier once iOS 14.5 was released, MacRumors reported.

Facebook has argued against the change for months. In December, it said in newspaper ads and a blog post that small business advertisers saw a cut of over 60% in sales for every dollar spent when they could not use personalized ads, according to its own studies, CNBC reported.

Why it matters for brands

For brands that find customers through social advertising, two things change. Targeting on iPhones becomes less precise for users who decline tracking, and the platforms can see fewer of the purchases their ads lead to on a brand’s website. The second change affects reports immediately; the first affects results more gradually.

Brands should expect reported conversions from social campaigns to fall in the coming weeks. That fall will include sales that still happened but were no longer counted, so it is not a reliable guide to how much the ads lost.

What to do now

  1. Record your social campaigns’ reported conversions and your total sales for the weeks before April 26, so you have a baseline.
  2. Watch total sales by channel, not only platform reports, before cutting social budgets.
  3. Plan a regional holdout test on your largest social campaign to measure what it contributes after the change.

A0053.title: Amazon’s first-quarter sales rise 44% as it moves Prime Day into the second quarter
A0053.alt: Red hand cart stacked with taped cardboard shipping boxes against a weathered blue wall.
A0053.ttag: Amazon’s first-quarter sales rise 44% as it moves Prime Day into the second quarter | Kwontified
A0053.desc: On April 29, 2021, Amazon reported net sales of $108.5 billion for the first quarter, up 44% from a year earlier, and said it would hold Prime Day during…
A0053.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 30, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0053.body:
On April 29, 2021, Amazon reported net sales of $108.5 billion for the first quarter, up 44% from a year earlier, and said it would hold Prime Day during the second quarter, the Associated Press reported.

What Amazon announced

Amazon’s “other” revenue line, which is mostly advertising, grew 77% to $6.9 billion from $3.9 billion a year earlier, the fastest growth of any segment by percentage, GeekWire reported. Third-party seller services revenue grew 64% to $23.7 billion.

On the earnings call, Amazon said third-party sellers accounted for 55% of paid units in the quarter, up from 52% a year earlier, and that Prime Day would be a two-day event in the second quarter, with dates to be announced later, according to the call transcript. The chief financial officer told reporters the event would fall in June, GeekWire reported. Amazon guided to second-quarter net sales of $110 billion to $116 billion, assuming Prime Day takes place in the quarter.

Why it matters for brands

Prime Day moving from October in 2020 to June in 2021 shifts the year’s biggest member event by about four months. Brands that planned inventory, budgets and promotions around an autumn Prime Day need to bring that work forward, with only weeks to prepare.

Advertising again grew faster than Amazon’s overall sales, and sellers took a larger share of units. Both mean more competition for the same shoppers during the event.

What to do now

  1. Confirm stock levels for your Prime Day products now, allowing for inbound delays to Amazon’s warehouses.
  2. Set Prime Day advertising budgets for June and decide which products will carry deals.
  3. Plan for higher costs per click during the event, and set targets by period rather than for the quarter as a whole.

A0059.crumb: Amazon removes Aukey and Mpow listings…
A0059.title: Amazon removes Aukey and Mpow listings after a fake-review leak
A0059.alt: Clear corked bottle on a white paper backdrop with color swatch cards, a tape measure and a round mirror.
A0059.ttag: Amazon removes Aukey and Mpow listings after a fake-review leak | Kwontified
A0059.desc: Most products from Aukey and Mpow, two popular brands of phone chargers, headphones and other electronics accessories, disappeared from Amazon around May…
A0059.byline: By Kwontified. Published May 12, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0059.body:
Most products from Aukey and Mpow, two popular brands of phone chargers, headphones and other electronics accessories, disappeared from Amazon around May 10, 2021, shortly after an investigation reported a leaked database of companies paying for fake reviews, Android Authority reported.

What happened

The removals followed a report by the review site SafetyDetectives, which said it had found an exposed database linked to a scheme in which sellers gave shoppers free products in exchange for positive reviews, according to Android Authority. Neither brand had commented on the removals when it reported on May 10.

Amazon would not confirm or deny whether either company was involved in the scheme, Droid Life reported on May 11, citing a statement Amazon gave to The Verge.

Why it matters for brands

Aukey and Mpow were well-known brands, not obscure sellers. If the removals are linked to reviews, as their timing suggests, they show that a familiar name does not protect a seller whose reviews Amazon believes were manipulated.

For brands that compete with sellers like these, the removals may open space in crowded categories. For every brand, they are a reminder that reviews are only an asset if they were earned within Amazon’s rules. Any program that offers shoppers products, refunds or payment in exchange for reviews puts the whole account at risk, not just the listing.

What to do now

  1. Review every program that touches customer reviews, including agencies and third-party services, and end any that offer shoppers an incentive tied to a review.
  2. Check your categories for listings that have disappeared, and review advertising and stock plans for products that may now face less competition.
  3. Use only Amazon’s own programs, such as Vine where eligible, to request reviews on new products.

A0070.alt: Stacked cardboard boxes topped with a striped towel beside potted red geraniums on a stone step by a blue wall.
A0070.ttag: Amazon announces Prime Day 2021 for June 21 and 22 | Kwontified
A0070.desc: On June 2, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021 will run on June 21 and 22, with more than 2 million deals, according to its press release .
A0070.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 3, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0070.body:
On June 2, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021 will run on June 21 and 22, with more than 2 million deals, according to its press release.

What Amazon announced

The two-day event is open to Prime members. Amazon said it would spend more than $100 million for the rest of 2021 to support small businesses selling in its store, including promotions that encourage customers to buy from them.

As part of that, members who spend $10 on items sold by select small businesses from June 7 to June 20 will receive a $10 credit to use on Prime Day. More than 300,000 sellers are eligible, more than twice as many as in 2020, Amazon said.

The 2021 event comes earlier in the year than the last two. The 2020 event ran on October 13 and 14, after the pandemic pushed it out of the summer, and the 2019 event ran on July 15 and 16.

Why it matters for brands

Brands now have under three weeks to finalize stock, deals and advertising. Products that are not already in Amazon’s warehouses or on their way may not arrive in time.

The small-business promotion also changes the shape of the event. It runs for two weeks before Prime Day, which means shoppers will be buying from eligible sellers in the run-up, and some demand may arrive earlier than brands expect.

What to do now

  1. Confirm stock levels and inbound shipments for every product you plan to promote on June 21 and 22.
  2. Set advertising budgets for the run-up from June 7 as well as for the two event days.
  3. If you are a small business seller, check whether your products are eligible for the Spend $10, Get $10 promotion.

A0079.desc: On June 23, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021, held June 21 and 22, was the biggest two-day period ever for its third-party sellers, whose sales grew…
A0079.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 24, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0079.body:
On June 23, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021, held June 21 and 22, was the biggest two-day period ever for its third-party sellers, whose sales grew faster than Amazon’s own retail business, GeekWire reported. These are preliminary figures from public sources.

What Amazon and outside data show

Prime members in 20 countries bought more than 250 million items, Amazon said. Unlike in 2020, when it said third-party sellers sold more than $3.5 billion during the event, Amazon gave no dollar figure for sales.

Amazon also said shoppers spent more than $1.9 billion on more than 70 million products from small businesses during its “Spend $10, Get $10” promotion in the two weeks before the event, double the comparable promotion in October 2020, according to Amazon.

Total US online spending across all retailers on June 21 and 22 passed $11 billion, up 6.1% from Prime Day in October 2020, according to the Adobe Digital Economy Index, GeekWire reported. That included about $5.6 billion on the first day and $5.4 billion on the second, Investing.com reported. The figure covers all US online retailers, not Amazon alone, and it exceeded the $10.9 billion spent online on Cyber Monday 2020.

Why it matters for brands

The headline numbers say more about the industry than about any single brand. Growth of 6.1% across US online retail is modest against an October 2020 event that fell during the pandemic and the start of holiday shopping. Brands should judge their own results against the ranges they set before the event, not against Amazon’s description of a record.

What to do now

  1. Pull your Prime Day sales, advertising spend and stock-outs by product while the data is fresh.
  2. Compare results with your pre-event forecast range, and note which products landed above or below it and why.
  3. Check sales on Walmart and Target during the same days, since both ran competing events.

A0081.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 25, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0081.body:
On June 24, 2021, Google said it would delay its plan to phase out third-party cookies in its Chrome browser, which advertisers use to track people across websites, because it needs more time to develop a replacement, the Associated Press reported.

What Google announced

Google had planned to end support for third-party cookies in Chrome by early 2022. It now expects to have its replacement technologies, part of an effort it calls the Privacy Sandbox, deployed by late 2022, and then to phase out third-party cookies over three months ending in late 2023, Mobile Marketing reported. The new timeline is subject to Google’s engagement with the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority.

“We need to move at a responsible pace,” Vinay Goel, Chrome’s privacy engineering director, wrote in a blog post, according to the AP.

Why it matters for brands

The delay gives advertisers more time, but it does not change the direction. Apple’s App Tracking Transparency prompt, introduced in April, is already limiting how apps track iPhone users, and Apple has announced a Mail feature that will hide email opens. Brands that rely on third-party cookies to target and measure advertising on the open web will still need an alternative by late 2023.

Retail media networks are less affected, because retailers such as Amazon, Walmart and Target measure sales with their own first-party data rather than third-party cookies.

What to do now

  1. List which parts of your advertising and measurement depend on third-party cookies.
  2. Use the extra time to build first-party data, such as email lists and customer accounts, that does not depend on cookies.
  3. Give more weight to channels that measure sales with their own customer data, such as retail media networks.

A0085.title: Andy Jassy becomes Amazon’s chief executive as Jeff Bezos moves to executive chair
A0085.alt: An open cardboard box spilling kraft packing paper beside a roll of tape on a sunlit wooden table.
A0085.ttag: Andy Jassy becomes Amazon’s chief executive as Jeff Bezos moves to executive chair | Kwontified
A0085.desc: On July 5, 2021, Andy Jassy officially became chief executive of Amazon, taking over from founder Jeff Bezos, who now holds the title of executive…
A0085.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 6, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0085.body:
On July 5, 2021, Andy Jassy officially became chief executive of Amazon, taking over from founder Jeff Bezos, who now holds the title of executive chairman, SiliconANGLE reported.

What changed

Jassy previously ran Amazon Web Services, the company’s cloud computing business, which he helped build. Amazon said in May that former Tableau Software chief executive Adam Selipsky would succeed Jassy as head of AWS, SiliconANGLE reported on May 26.

Bezos chose July 5 because it is the date Amazon was incorporated in 1994, he told shareholders at the company’s annual meeting in May. Amazon said in a regulatory filing that it would grant Jassy 61,000 shares of stock, vesting over 10 years, on his first day as chief executive.

As executive chair, Bezos has said he will stay engaged in important Amazon initiatives while focusing more time on other projects.

Why it matters for brands

Amazon’s policies for sellers, vendors and advertisers are not expected to change overnight. But a new chief executive sets priorities, and Jassy comes from the part of Amazon built on selling services to businesses. Brands should watch for changes in how Amazon treats its marketplace sellers, its advertising business and the tools it offers partners over the coming year.

What to do now

  1. Note any changes in Amazon’s seller, vendor or advertising policies announced in the coming months, and judge them against your own plans.
  2. Keep your holiday planning on its current course; the leadership change does not alter Amazon’s near-term calendar.
  3. Watch Amazon’s next quarterly results for early signs of the new chief executive’s priorities.

A0107.title: TikTok tests in-app shopping with Shopify merchants
A0107.alt: A ring light with a phone clamp stands beside a wooden stool holding amber skincare bottles against a teal wall.
A0107.ttag: TikTok tests in-app shopping with Shopify merchants | Kwontified
A0107.desc: On August 24, 2021, TikTok and Shopify announced an expanded partnership that lets Shopify merchants add a shopping tab to their TikTok profiles, Shopify…
A0107.byline: By Kwontified. Published Aug 25, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0107.body:
On August 24, 2021, TikTok and Shopify announced an expanded partnership that lets Shopify merchants add a shopping tab to their TikTok profiles, Shopify said in an announcement.

What was announced

Shopify merchants with a TikTok For Business account will be able to sync their product catalogs to create a mini-storefront on their TikTok profile, linking to their online store for checkout. Merchants will also be able to tag products in organic TikTok posts using product links. The TikTok Shopping pilot is available to Shopify merchants in the US and UK, with a select group in Canada joining in the coming weeks, Shopify said.

Purchases are completed on the merchant’s own website, not inside TikTok, and TikTok plans to pilot the features with hundreds of Shopify merchants before a wider launch, TechCrunch reported.

Shopify said installs across its social commerce channels rose 76% from February 2020 to February 2021.

Why it matters for brands

TikTok has been a place where products are discovered, often without a direct way to buy. The pilot gives shoppers a shorter path from a video to a product page, and gives brands a way to sell from content they already post. Because checkout stays on the brand’s own site, the brand keeps the customer relationship and the order data, unlike some in-app checkout models.

The pilot is limited to Shopify merchants, so brands on other e-commerce platforms cannot use it yet.

What to do now

  1. If you sell through Shopify and have a TikTok For Business account, consider requesting access to the pilot through Shopify’s TikTok channel.
  2. Review which of your products already get attention on TikTok, and make sure their product pages are ready for traffic from short videos.
  3. Set up tracking for TikTok visits and sales on your own site before you start, so you can judge the results.

On September 8, 2021, Amazon opened registration for Accelerate 2021, a free virtual conference for its third-party sellers to be held on October 20 and 21, Amazon said in an announcement.

What was announced

This is the second annual Accelerate conference. Amazon said the event will include new product and service announcements, seller presentations and more than 30 sessions for current and aspiring sellers. Attendees will hear from Amazon chief executive Andy Jassy and Worldwide Consumer chief executive Dave Clark about Amazon’s focus on its selling partners.

Amazon also said entrepreneurs interested in becoming sellers can now get personalized account registration support and a new Start Selling on Amazon toolkit.

Why it matters for brands

Amazon has said the event will include new product and service announcements, and it falls just before the holiday season, when brands are finalizing their fourth-quarter plans. Announcements on advertising, analytics, inventory or fees could affect those plans. It is also the first Accelerate since Jassy became chief executive in July, so it may signal his priorities for Amazon’s selling partners.

What to do now

  1. Register through Amazon’s Accelerate page, and identify the sessions most relevant to your team.
  2. Plan to review any announcements against your holiday advertising and inventory plans before Black Friday.

A0137.title: Amazon Accelerate 2021: the announcements that matter for brands
A0137.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0137.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2021: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0137.desc: At its Accelerate 2021 conference for third-party sellers on October 20, 2021, Amazon announced new tools for product research and brand building, and…
A0137.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 22, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0137.body:
At its Accelerate 2021 conference for third-party sellers on October 20, 2021, Amazon announced new tools for product research and brand building, and said more than 100,000 brands had started selling in its U.S. store so far in 2021, according to its announcement.

What was announced

Amazon said sales by brands in its U.S. store grew by almost 60% in the 12 months ending June 30, 2021. It announced four tools and benefits for brands enrolled in Brand Registry:

  • Amazon Brand Referral Bonus. Brands that send shoppers to Amazon from their own websites or other non-Amazon marketing earn a bonus of, on average, 10% of the purchase price. The bonus covers the promoted product and any of the brand’s other products the shopper buys over the following two weeks.
  • Amazon Customer Engagement. A tool for sending email campaigns about new products to shoppers. Amazon said it had sent more than 6 million emails on brands’ behalf since the beta began in May. It will stay in beta into early 2022.
  • A+ Story Cards. Visual modules on the product page that tell the brand’s story and link to its other products.
  • Customer Review Resolution. A tool that lets brands offer support and a courtesy refund to a customer who leaves a negative review.

Amazon also announced Product Opportunity Explorer, a tool showing what shoppers search for, click on and buy, with search volume, sales history and pricing trends, in a separate announcement the same day. It is in beta through the end of 2021 and will be available to all sellers in 2022 at no charge. The same announcement noted that Amazon Vine can help Brand Registry sellers build reviews on new products for as little as $200 per enrolled product.

Why it matters for brands

Several of the new tools reward brands for bringing their own customers and marketing to Amazon. The Brand Referral Bonus effectively lowers the cost of off-Amazon advertising that sends shoppers to Amazon, which changes how brands should compare that spending with Amazon’s own advertising. Customer Engagement gives brands a direct line to shoppers who follow them.

The research tools matter for planning. Product Opportunity Explorer puts Amazon’s own search and sales data behind decisions about which products to launch, data that brands have previously had to estimate from third-party tools.

What to do now

  1. Confirm your brands are enrolled in Brand Registry, which most of the new tools require.
  2. Set up Brand Referral Bonus tracking for any off-Amazon campaigns that send traffic to Amazon, and recalculate their return with the bonus included.
  3. Request access to Product Opportunity Explorer and use it in your 2022 product launch planning.

A0139.title: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2021: the announcements that matter for brands
A0139.alt: A spotlight on a stand aimed at a plain white box on a white plinth against a navy blue wall.
A0139.ttag: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2021: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0139.desc: On October 26, 2021, the first day of its virtual unBoxed conference, Amazon Ads announced eight advertising and measurement solutions, including a new…
A0139.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 27, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0139.body:
On October 26, 2021, the first day of its virtual unBoxed conference, Amazon Ads announced eight advertising and measurement solutions, including a new Brand Metrics tool in beta and Sponsored Display ads inside Twitch livestreams, according to its announcement.

What was announced

  • Brand Metrics (beta). A measurement tool that counts how many shoppers are in the awareness and consideration stages for a brand. It measures all shopping engagement with the brand on Amazon, not just engagement attributed to ads, Amazon Ads said. It is available in the US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Spain.
  • Amazon Brand Lift. A tool that lets Amazon DSP advertisers run studies measuring the effect of brand campaigns, sent to a panel of opted-in Amazon shoppers, Modern Retail reported.
  • Sponsored Display in Twitch livestreams. Sponsored Display ads already ran on Twitch’s browse and directory pages. They will now also appear inside livestreams.
  • Amazon Marketing Cloud updates. Amazon is expanding access to Amazon Marketing Cloud, its analytics service for custom, cross-media measurement, to all of its DSP customers, Modern Retail reported.

Why it matters for brands

Most of the announcements are about measurement beyond the last click. Brand Metrics and Brand Lift give brands ways to see whether advertising builds awareness and consideration, not only whether it produces an attributed sale. That makes it easier to justify spending on upper-funnel formats such as Sponsored Display, video and DSP, which often look weak on return on ad spend alone.

The Twitch expansion widens Sponsored Display’s reach well beyond Amazon’s own store, to an audience that is not necessarily shopping when it sees the ad.

What to do now

  1. Check whether your brands are eligible for Brand Metrics, and record a baseline before changing upper-funnel budgets.
  2. If you run Amazon DSP, ask about Amazon Marketing Cloud access and Brand Lift studies for your holiday campaigns.
  3. Test Sponsored Display on Twitch only where your audience overlaps with Twitch viewers, and judge it on reach and consideration rather than immediate sales.

A0141.crumb: Facebook renames its parent company Meta
A0141.title: Facebook renames its parent company Meta
A0141.alt: A phone on a small flexible tripod beside white canvas sneakers on a white block against a pink wall.
A0141.ttag: Facebook renames its parent company Meta | Kwontified
A0141.desc: On October 28, 2021, at its Connect conference, Facebook announced that its parent company is now called Meta, bringing its apps and technologies under…
A0141.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 29, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0141.body:
On October 28, 2021, at its Connect conference, Facebook announced that its parent company is now called Meta, bringing its apps and technologies under one new company brand, according to the company’s announcement. The company said its apps and brands, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, are not changing their names.

What was announced

The company changed its corporate name from Facebook, Inc. to Meta Platforms, Inc., and said it expects its shares to begin trading under the new ticker MVRS on December 1, 2021, according to its regulatory filing. The company said it plans to report its results in two segments, Family of Apps and Reality Labs, starting with the fourth quarter of 2021, and that the change does not affect how it uses or shares data.

The new name reflects the company’s focus on building the metaverse, a set of shared virtual spaces, which chief executive Mark Zuckerberg described as the next stage of social technology.

Why it matters for brands

Little changes for brands in the short term. Facebook and Instagram keep their names, their ad products and their shopping tools, including Facebook Shops and Instagram Shopping. Business accounts, ad accounts and catalogs are unaffected by the corporate rename.

The new reporting split will matter more over time. Separating the apps business from Reality Labs will show how much the company is investing in the metaverse, and how much its advertising business is earning to pay for it. For brands that rely on Facebook and Instagram for advertising and social commerce, that investment is worth watching as a signal of where the company’s attention, and its product development, will go.

What to do now

  1. No action is needed on your ad accounts, Shops or catalogs; the apps and their business tools keep their names.
  2. Update internal documents and vendor references to the parent company’s new name where relevant.
  3. Keep your social commerce plans focused on the products that exist today, Shops and Instagram Shopping, rather than on future metaverse formats.
