A0146.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
A0146.ttag: Amazon sets a 48-hour Black Friday event for November 25 and 26 | Kwontified
A0146.desc: On November 15, 2021, Amazon announced that more Black Friday deals than ever before will be available during a 48-hour event starting on Thursday,…
A0146.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 16, 2021. 1-minute read.
A0146.body:
On November 15, 2021, Amazon announced that more Black Friday deals than ever before will be available during a 48-hour event starting on Thursday, November 25, Thanksgiving Day, and running through November 26, RTTNews reported.

What was announced

Amazon said shoppers will find deep discounts on top products during the event. In its Canadian announcement the same day, it said Prime members get 30-minute early access to select Lightning Deals throughout the holiday season, according to the release.

The event caps a season that started early. Amazon began offering “Black Friday-worthy” deals on October 4, Fortune reported. Walmart is running three Black Friday Deals for Days events in November, the first two starting online on November 3 and November 10, with early access for paying Walmart+ members, according to Walmart’s announcement.

Adobe expects Cyber Monday, November 29, to remain the biggest online shopping day of the year at $11.3 billion, up 4%, and Black Friday to reach $9.5 billion, up 5%, according to its forecast.

Why it matters for brands

The 48-hour event concentrates Amazon’s own promotion on Thanksgiving and Black Friday, after six weeks of earlier deals. Brands with deals in the event will compete for attention with a large number of others, and advertising costs typically rise as the event approaches.

The early-access benefits for Prime and Walmart+ members mean some of the most valuable shoppers will buy before the general public. Brands should make sure deal products are live, in stock and advertised from the start of each member window.

What to do now

  1. Confirm that your deal products are live, priced and in stock at Amazon’s warehouses for November 25 and 26.
  2. Set advertising budgets for Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, with room to move spend toward the days that convert best.
  3. Check deal eligibility and stock for Walmart’s remaining Black Friday event alongside Amazon’s.

A0156.title: Early read: Black Friday 2021 online sales slip as the season spreads out
A0156.alt: Blue, red and orange paper shopping bags lined up on a weathered wooden bench against a sunlit cream wall.
A0156.ttag: Early read: Black Friday 2021 online sales slip as the season spreads out | Kwontified
A0156.desc: Online spending on Black Friday, November 26, 2021, fell to $8.9 billion from about $9 billion a year earlier, the first time Adobe has recorded a…
A0156.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 30, 2021. 2-minute read.
A0156.body:
Online spending on Black Friday, November 26, 2021, fell to $8.9 billion from about $9 billion a year earlier, the first time Adobe has recorded a decline, while Thanksgiving was flat at $5.1 billion, CNBC reported on November 27. These are preliminary figures from public sources; Cyber Monday results were not yet available.

What the early data shows

Adobe said shoppers had shifted spending earlier in the season, responding to deals that began in October, ABC News reported. U.S. online spending from November 1 to November 28 reached $99.1 billion, up 13.6% from a year earlier, Fox Business reported. Adobe also found out-of-stock messages up 16% on November 27 and 28 from the prior weekend, Search Engine Land reported.

Stores saw more visitors than in 2020 but fewer than before the pandemic. Black Friday store traffic rose 47.5% from 2020 but was 28% below 2019, according to Sensormatic, CNBC reported. Many large retailers, including Walmart and Target, kept stores closed on Thanksgiving.

Adobe expected Cyber Monday, November 29, to bring $10.2 billion to $11.3 billion in online sales, which could fall short of 2020’s $10.8 billion, CNBC and ABC News reported.

Why it matters for brands

The early numbers fit the pattern forecast in October: a record season online, with weaker growth on the biggest days. Brands that judge their results against Black Friday 2020 alone will misread them. A flat or lower Black Friday can sit inside a strong November if the brand sold well in October and early November events.

Rising out-of-stock messages also matter. Brands that ran short during the weekend lost sales they will not recover, and may have handed trial to competitors.

What to do now

  1. Compare your Black Friday and Thanksgiving results with your November baseline and with your planning ranges, not only with 2020.
  2. Check which products ran out of stock over the weekend, and restock or pause advertising on them for December.
  3. Review results by day across the whole of November before setting budgets for the rest of the season.

A0185.crumb: Amazon raises the US Prime fee and…
A0185.title: Amazon raises the US Prime fee and reports advertising revenue as its own line
A0185.alt: Empty wooden picture frame and a twine-tied cardboard parcel leaning against a sunlit mustard-yellow wall.
A0185.ttag: Amazon raises the US Prime fee and reports advertising revenue as its own line | Kwontified
A0185.desc: Amazon is raising the price of an annual U.S.
A0185.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 4, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0185.body:
Amazon is raising the price of an annual U.S. Prime membership from $119 to $139, its first increase since 2018, and for the first time reported advertising revenue separately: $31.2 billion in 2021, with fourth-quarter sales up 32% to $9.7 billion, according to Amazon’s February 3 results and CNBC.

What happened

The monthly Prime fee rises from $12.99 to $14.99. New members pay the higher price from February 18 and existing members from their first renewal after March 25, MediaPost reported. Amazon cited expanded member benefits and higher wages and transportation costs, Variety reported.

Amazon previously included advertising in a line labeled “other.” Its advertising business is now larger than Microsoft’s, which passed $10 billion over the past year, and larger than the total revenue of Snap or Pinterest, CNBC reported. Advertising made up about 7% of Amazon’s fourth-quarter revenue. Amazon did not report the business’s operating income.

The rest of the retail business grew more slowly. Sales from Amazon’s own online stores fell 1% in the quarter, while third-party seller services grew 11%, according to a Raymond James note cited by MediaPost. Amazon expects first-quarter sales to grow 3% to 8%.

Why it matters for brands

The ad figure confirms what brands have felt in their costs. Advertising grew far faster than Amazon’s own retail sales in the fourth quarter, which means more ad spending competing for each sale. Brands should expect click prices to keep rising in 2022.

The Prime increase is a small cost for most shoppers, but it may make some members shop more deliberately, and it could raise expectations of value from brands that sell to them.

What to do now

  1. Set 2022 Amazon advertising budgets from late-2021 click prices, not the full-year average.
  2. Track cost per order and units per ad dollar alongside return on ad spend each month.
  3. Watch conversion after February 18 for any change in Prime members’ buying.

A0218.crumb: Amazon launches Buy with Prime for…
A0218.title: Amazon launches Buy with Prime for merchants’ own sites
A0218.alt: An open cardboard box overflowing with crumpled kraft paper beside a roll of packing tape on a sunlit bench.
A0218.ttag: Amazon launches Buy with Prime for merchants’ own sites | Kwontified
A0218.desc: On April 21, 2022, Amazon introduced Buy with Prime, which lets merchants offer Prime shopping benefits on their own websites, Retail TouchPoints reported…
A0218.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 22, 2022. 2-minute read.
A0218.body:
On April 21, 2022, Amazon introduced Buy with Prime, which lets merchants offer Prime shopping benefits on their own websites, Retail TouchPoints reported. Prime members shopping on those sites can check out with the payment and shipping details stored in their Amazon account and receive Prime delivery and free returns.

What was announced

Buy with Prime is available by invitation only through 2022, at first to merchants that use Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA), since their stock is already in Amazon’s warehouses, Chain Store Age reported. Amazon plans to extend it later to merchants that do not sell on its marketplace or use FBA.

Merchants can show the Prime logo and the expected delivery date on eligible products in their own online stores, and add the checkout through a widget that works with most online stores. Pricing combines a service fee, a payment processing fee, and fulfillment and storage fees charged per unit, Chain Store Age reported.

The launch follows Amazon’s announcement on April 13 of a 5% fuel and inflation surcharge on FBA fulfillment fees, which takes effect on April 28.

Why it matters for brands

Buy with Prime lets a brand sell to Prime members on its own site with the delivery promise they trust on Amazon. That could lift conversion for brands whose own sites lose shoppers at checkout or on shipping costs. Amazon has not released conversion figures for the service.

It also extends Amazon’s role. Orders on the brand’s own site would ship from Amazon’s warehouses, be paid through Amazon’s checkout and carry Amazon’s fees. Brands need to know which customer data they keep, and how the fees compare with their current fulfillment and payment costs.

What to do now

  1. If you use FBA, ask Amazon about an invitation and request the full fee schedule.
  2. Compare Buy with Prime fees with your own site’s current fulfillment, payment and shipping costs per order.
  3. Confirm which customer details, such as email addresses, your business would receive for each order.

A0222.desc: From April 28, 2022, Amazon is adding a 5% fuel and inflation surcharge to the per-unit fulfillment fees paid by U.S.
A0222.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 28, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0222.body:
From April 28, 2022, Amazon is adding a 5% fuel and inflation surcharge to the per-unit fulfillment fees paid by U.S. sellers who use Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA), the first such surcharge in its history, Bloomberg reported when Amazon announced it on April 13.

What happened

The surcharge applies on top of current FBA fulfillment fee rates, and Amazon said it is subject to change, UPI reported. It works out to about 24 cents per unit on average, below the fuel surcharges that UPS and FedEx were charging as of March 21, at 42 and 49 cents per unit respectively, UPI reported.

Amazon described the surcharge as an alternative to a permanent fee increase, Fox Business reported. It comes three months after Amazon’s annual fee changes took effect on January 18, which raised fulfillment fees by an average of 5.2%, EcommerceBytes reported.

The surcharge applies only to sellers using Amazon’s fulfillment service. Sellers that ship orders themselves are not affected.

Why it matters for brands

For a typical small, light product, the surcharge adds a few cents per unit. Across a large catalog, and on top of January’s increase, it adds up. Because Amazon has not said how long it will last, brands cannot treat it as a one-off.

It also changes comparisons. Brands weighing Amazon’s logistics against their own or a third party’s should include the surcharge, and those considering Buy with Prime, announced on April 21, should ask whether it applies to that program’s per-unit fulfillment fees.

What to do now

  1. Add the 5% surcharge to your per-unit Amazon cost model for every product.
  2. Review prices and advertising budgets for low-priced products, where the surcharge takes the largest share of margin.
  3. Compare FBA with merchant fulfillment for slow-moving or bulky products where the surcharge tips the balance.

A0243.crumb: Amazon sets Prime Day 2022 for July 12…
A0243.title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2022 for July 12 and 13
A0243.alt: Stacked cardboard boxes topped with a striped towel beside potted red geraniums on a stone step by a blue wall.
A0243.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Day 2022 for July 12 and 13 | Kwontified
A0243.desc: Amazon will hold Prime Day 2022 on July 12 and 13, starting at 3 a.m. Eastern time, the company announced on Thursday, June 16, Fortune reported .
A0243.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 17, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0243.body:
Amazon will hold Prime Day 2022 on July 12 and 13, starting at 3 a.m. Eastern time, the company announced on Thursday, June 16, Fortune reported. Early deals for Prime members begin on June 21.

What happened

The two-day event will run in 20 countries and, for the first time, in Poland and Sweden, Fox Business reported. Amazon had told investors in April that Prime Day would take place in July, but had not named the dates until now.

Members can earn a $10 credit toward Prime Day purchases by using other Prime services, such as streaming Prime Video or borrowing a Kindle book, Fortune reported.

It is the first Prime Day since Amazon raised the price of a U.S. Prime membership from $119 to $139 a year in February, according to its fourth-quarter results.

Why it matters for brands

The dates fix the planning calendar. Stock now has less than four weeks to reach Amazon’s warehouses, and advertising budgets need to cover the days before the event as well as the two days themselves, as competitors start bidding early.

The early deals starting June 21 stretch the event across three weeks. Shoppers who see a deal in late June may buy then, or wait for a deeper one in July. Brands should decide in advance whether to run early deals, or to hold their best offer for the event itself.

Prime Day 2022 also arrives in a weaker market for goods. Large retailers reported swollen inventories in May, so brands should expect heavy discounting around the same days, both on Amazon and at its rivals.

What to do now

  1. Confirm that inbound shipments for your Prime Day products will arrive before July 12.
  2. Decide which products, if any, should run early deals from June 21.
  3. Set advertising budgets for the days before and during the event, and agree how you will judge the result.

A0256.crumb: Early read on Prime Day 2022: shoppers…
A0256.title: Early read on Prime Day 2022: shoppers spent more per order, and hunted for value
A0256.alt: Red hand cart stacked with taped cardboard shipping boxes against a weathered blue wall.
A0256.ttag: Early read on Prime Day 2022: shoppers spent more per order, and hunted for value | Kwontified
A0256.desc: Preliminary figures from the first day of Prime Day 2022, which ran on July 12 and 13, show U.S.
A0256.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 14, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0256.body:
Preliminary figures from the first day of Prime Day 2022, which ran on July 12 and 13, show U.S. online spending of $6.0 billion across all retailers, the biggest online shopping day of 2022 so far, Adobe said in a statement to Total Retail on July 13. These are early readings, not final results.

What happened

Numerator, which tracks verified orders, said the average Prime Day order was $53.14 as of the morning of July 13, up from $47.14 at the same point in 2021, according to its release that day. It found that 42% of orders were $20 or less and 13% were above $100.

Shoppers were clearly hunting for value. In Numerator’s survey, 33% of Prime Day buyers said they had waited for the event to buy a specific item at a discount, and 20% said inflation led them to check prices outside Amazon first, Total Retail reported. The event fell on the day U.S. consumer prices were reported 9.1% higher in June than a year earlier.

Why it matters for brands

The early data fits a deal-driven event. Shoppers bought, but many bought what they had planned and compared prices before they did. Brands with strong deals on items people were waiting for are likely to see the biggest lift. Brands relying on impulse purchases may see less.

Order values rose, but so did prices. Some of the higher average order reflects inflation rather than larger baskets, so brands should judge their own results in units as well as revenue.

What to do now

  1. Record units, revenue, click costs and the share of sales sold on deal for both days, before the numbers blur into July.
  2. Compare the result against your forecast cases, and note which assumptions held.
  3. Watch whether sales fall below normal in the days after the event, a sign that some purchases were pulled forward.

A0260.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0260.ttag: Amazon opens registration for Accelerate 2022, its seller conference | Kwontified
A0260.desc: Amazon opened registration on July 20 for Accelerate 2022, its annual conference for sellers, which will run on September 14 and 15 at the Seattle…
A0260.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 21, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0260.body:
Amazon opened registration on July 20 for Accelerate 2022, its annual conference for sellers, which will run on September 14 and 15 at the Seattle Convention Center and, for the first time, online as well as in person, according to its announcement.

What happened

It is the third Accelerate conference. Amazon said the event will feature its largest seller announcements of the year, a fireside chat with Doug Herrington, the new chief executive of Worldwide Amazon Stores, and a session with tennis champion Venus Williams, GuruFocus reported, carrying the release.

Amazon described the conference as a personalized event, with sessions, live support, networking and access to solution providers, designed around each seller’s stage of growth.

Why it matters for brands

Accelerate is where Amazon tends to announce changes to its seller tools, fees and programs for the coming year. Announcements in September can shape how sellers prepare for the fourth quarter, when most brands are setting their holiday plans and budgets.

The timing is pointed. Amazon’s fulfillment fees rose with a 5% fuel and inflation surcharge in April, UPI reported, and sellers are planning a holiday season with higher costs and more cautious shoppers. Any changes to tools, fees or programs announced in Seattle will land just as those plans are being finalized.

What to do now

  1. Decide whether anyone from your team will attend in person or online, and register while places are open.
  2. List the questions your team most needs answered, from fees to advertising tools, before the agenda is published.
  3. Leave room in your fourth-quarter plan to adjust after the September announcements.

A0278.title: Pinduoduo quietly launches Temu, its first U.S. shopping site
A0278.alt: Gray plastic crate overflowing with orange poly mailer bags against a sunlit orange wall.
A0278.ttag: Pinduoduo quietly launches Temu, its first U.S. shopping site | Kwontified
A0278.desc: Pinduoduo, the Chinese e-commerce company, launched Temu, a shopping site and app for U.S.
A0278.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 6, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0278.body:
Pinduoduo, the Chinese e-commerce company, launched Temu, a shopping site and app for U.S. customers, on Thursday, September 1, without a public announcement, Nikkei Asia reported on September 2. It is the company’s first expansion outside China.

What happened

Temu sells clothing, electronics and other goods at relatively low prices, with a layout similar to that of the fast-fashion retailer Shein, though with a far smaller selection than its larger rivals, Nikkei reported. A Chinese vendor who sells on Amazon told Nikkei that Temu would run a trial from September 1 to September 15 before full operations begin, and that Pinduoduo prefers first vendors with cross-border experience on Amazon or Shein.

Pinduoduo did not comment on the launch. On a call with analysts days earlier, its chief executive said overseas business was an opportunity worth trying, without mentioning the United States. The company reported second-quarter revenue of 31.44 billion yuan, about $4.55 billion, up 36% from a year earlier.

Why it matters for brands

Temu enters the U.S. market as another low-price, China-sourced competitor, alongside Shein, which Nikkei noted had recently passed Amazon as the most downloaded shopping app in the United States. Its early vendors are the same cross-border sellers who already compete with brands on Amazon.

For brands, the effect will show first in price perception. Shoppers who see very low prices for look-alike products on a new app may compare them with prices on Amazon, Walmart and brand sites, particularly in categories such as accessories, home goods and small electronics. Pinduoduo’s backing is likely to give Temu room to spend on promotion while it builds an audience.

What to do now

  1. Search Temu for your category and note the prices and products shoppers will find there.
  2. Check whether your own products, or copies of them, are listed, and record anything that misuses your brand.
  3. Watch whether Temu begins advertising heavily in the United States, which would bring its prices in front of your shoppers.

A0287.title: Amazon Accelerate 2022: email for brands and new ways to test listings
A0287.alt: Clear corked bottle on a white paper backdrop with color swatch cards, a tape measure and a round mirror.
A0287.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2022: email for brands and new ways to test listings | Kwontified
A0287.desc: Amazon used its Accelerate seller conference in Seattle on September 14 and 15 to announce free email marketing for brands and new tools for testing and…
A0287.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 16, 2022. 2-minute read.
A0287.body:
Amazon used its Accelerate seller conference in Seattle on September 14 and 15 to announce free email marketing for brands and new tools for testing and analyzing product listings, according to its September 14 announcement.

What happened

On September 14, Amazon introduced Tailored Audiences, three new audience types in its Customer Engagement tool that let brands email their repeat, recent and high-spend customers at no cost. Amazon sends the emails on the brand’s behalf. The tool is in beta, and Amazon plans to make it available to all U.S. sellers in early 2023, CNN reported. Amazon also made Premium A+ Content available to all eligible brands, saying it can increase sales by up to 20%.

On September 15, Amazon said brands can now use Manage Your Experiments to test bullet points and descriptions, not only titles, main images and A+ content, and can choose to publish winning versions automatically, according to its release. Amazon said the tool can increase sales by up to 25%. Brands can also download Search Query and Catalog Performance data from the Search Analytics Dashboard for the first time, and the Product Opportunity Explorer adds a Customer Reviews Insight feature.

Why it matters for brands

The email tool changes who a brand can reach. Until now, brands could message shoppers who chose to follow them. Tailored Audiences reaches customers who have bought, and shoppers will have to opt out rather than opt in, The Spokesman-Review reported. For brands that rely on repeat purchases, that is a free channel to bring customers back without paying for advertising.

The testing and data tools matter for the same reason. Downloadable search data lets brands combine Amazon’s figures with their own, and testing more of the listing makes it easier to find what lifts conversion before the holiday season.

What to do now

  1. Check whether your brand is in the Tailored Audiences beta, and plan a few emails to repeat and recent customers.
  2. Start tests on bullet points and descriptions in Manage Your Experiments for your best sellers.
  3. Download Search Query Performance data and compare it with your own sales and advertising reports.

A0288.title: Amazon confirms its October Prime event: Prime Early Access Sale, October 11–12
A0288.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0288.ttag: Amazon confirms its October Prime event: Prime Early Access Sale, October 11–12 | Kwontified
A0288.desc: Amazon announced on September 26 a new two-day shopping event for Prime members, the Prime Early Access Sale, which begins on October 11 at 12 a.m.
A0288.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 27, 2022. 2-minute read.
A0288.body:
Amazon announced on September 26 a new two-day shopping event for Prime members, the Prime Early Access Sale, which begins on October 11 at 12 a.m. Pacific time and runs through October 12, according to its announcement. It is the first time Amazon will hold two Prime-exclusive shopping events in the same year.

What happened

The event will run in 15 countries, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and much of Europe, EcommerceBytes reported. Amazon said it will introduce its first Top 100 list, a curated selection of popular and giftable deals from brands including Hasbro, iRobot, KitchenAid and Samsung.

Deals will cover categories including electronics, fashion, home, kitchen, pets, toys and Amazon devices, with new deals released throughout the event, PYMNTS reported. Amazon has been preparing sellers for months: in June, it asked some to submit Lightning Deals by July 22 for a fourth-quarter Prime event, CNBC reported at the time.

Why it matters for brands

The confirmation settles the date brands have been planning around without certainty. With two weeks to go, most of the decisions about deals and stock have already been made, so the remaining choices are about advertising budgets and which products to promote.

The timing has a cost advantage. The event ends on October 12, three days before Amazon’s new holiday peak fulfillment fee, averaging 35 cents per item, takes effect on October 15, the Associated Press reported in August. Orders during the event should carry the normal fee.

The open question is how much extra demand a second event will create so close to the holidays, and how much it will pull forward from November.

What to do now

  1. Confirm which of your products have deals approved, and check their stock in Amazon’s network.
  2. Set an event advertising budget with a base and a reserve, and decide in advance what results release the reserve.
  3. Plan to measure the event against a normal October week, including the week after, to see how much of the lift was pulled forward.

A0300.crumb: Early read: Prime Early Access Sale 2022…
A0300.title: Early read: Prime Early Access Sale 2022, from public sources (preliminary)
A0300.alt: Red hand cart stacked with taped cardboard shipping boxes against a weathered blue wall.
A0300.ttag: Early read: Prime Early Access Sale 2022, from public sources (preliminary) | Kwontified
A0300.desc: Amazon said on October 13 that tens of millions of Prime members shopped its first Prime Early Access Sale on October 11 and 12, according to its…
A0300.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 14, 2022. 2-minute read.
A0300.body:
Amazon said on October 13 that tens of millions of Prime members shopped its first Prime Early Access Sale on October 11 and 12, according to its announcement. This is a preliminary read from the figures public so far; Amazon did not disclose total sales, and fuller data will follow.

What happened

Amazon said members ordered more than 100 million items from independent sellers during the event, with top-selling categories including apparel, home, toys and Amazon devices. For comparison, Amazon said members bought more than 300 million items worldwide during July’s Prime Day, GeekWire reported. The two figures are not directly comparable, since one counts only independent sellers’ items.

Shoppers appear to have bought smaller baskets. In the first 30 hours, the average order was $45.90, and 44% of orders were for $20 or less, Numerator reported on October 12. Toys rose as a share of purchases: 24% of shoppers it surveyed bought toys and games, compared with 15% on July’s Prime Day. And 43% had also shopped other early holiday events, including Target’s Deal Days and Walmart’s Rollbacks and More sale.

Why it matters for brands

The early signs point to an event smaller than July’s, with more gift buying and more comparison across retailers. That matches the planning case for a second members’ event held weeks before the holidays.

The figures that matter most for brands are not public yet: how much each brand sold above a normal October week, and whether sales dip in the weeks that follow. A lower average order is not a failure if units rose, and a large unit count is not a success if it was pulled forward from November.

What to do now

  1. Compare each product’s event sales with a normal October week, not with July’s Prime Day.
  2. Watch sales for the next two weeks to see how much of the lift was pulled forward.
  3. Hold judgment on budgets for Black Friday until those two weeks of data are in.

A0309.title: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2022: the announcements that matter for brands
A0309.alt: A spotlight on a stand aimed at a plain white box on a white plinth against a navy blue wall.
A0309.ttag: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2022: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0309.desc: Amazon Ads announced a set of new advertising tools at its unBoxed conference in New York on October 26, centered on video, measurement and new places to…
A0309.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 28, 2022. 2-minute read.
A0309.body:
Amazon Ads announced a set of new advertising tools at its unBoxed conference in New York on October 26, centered on video, measurement and new places to advertise, according to Amazon Ads.

What happened

Video was the largest theme. Sponsored Display video creative is now available worldwide, letting advertisers of all sizes run video in the self-service display product, and Amazon expanded a public beta of Video Builder, which offers templates for making Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display videos, Amazon Ads said. Sponsored Brands videos can now link to a brand’s Store as well as to a product page, MediaPost reported.

For new products, Sponsored Products campaigns with presets now appear in the ads console for U.S. advertisers, recommending daily budgets and bidding strategies, Amazon Ads said.

Measurement and reach also grew. Amazon Marketing Cloud, Amazon’s clean room for advertising analysis, added Sponsored Display events, more pre-built queries and the ability to manage DSP audiences, and its active customers have quadrupled in a year, MediaPost reported. From November, eligible U.S. advertisers will be able to buy digital signage ads in Amazon Fresh stores through Amazon DSP. And Sponsored Display is opening to brands that do not sell on Amazon, in a closed U.S. beta on Twitch.

Why it matters for brands

Most of these changes lower the cost of formats that used to need agencies or large budgets. Video in Sponsored Display and templates in Video Builder make video practical for smaller brands, and presets give new products a starting point.

The larger shift is measurement. Amazon Marketing Cloud is becoming the place where Amazon expects serious advertisers to analyze performance across channels. Brands that do not use it will see less of what their advertising does than competitors who do.

What to do now

  1. Test Sponsored Display video on a few products with existing video, against your current display creative.
  2. Use presets as a starting point for new products, then adjust bids from your own results.
  3. If you spend on Amazon DSP, plan how you will use Amazon Marketing Cloud before 2023 budgets are set.

A0313.crumb: Amazon sets a 48-hour Black Friday event…
A0313.title: Amazon sets a 48-hour Black Friday event for November 24 and 25
A0313.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
A0313.ttag: Amazon sets a 48-hour Black Friday event for November 24 and 25 | Kwontified
A0313.desc: Amazon announced on November 14, 2022 that millions of deals will be available during a 48-hour Black Friday event starting on Thursday, November 24, with…
A0313.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 15, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0313.body:
Amazon announced on November 14, 2022 that millions of deals will be available during a 48-hour Black Friday event starting on Thursday, November 24, with limited deals available before then, according to Amazon.

What happened

The event runs on Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, November 24 and 25. Amazon said surprise deals will drop every 30 minutes during select periods of the two days, from brands including Samsung, HP, Hasbro, adidas and Calvin Klein. It listed discounts of up to 50% on some fashion lines and up to 30% on categories including premium hair care, beauty, toys, small appliances and drinkware.

Shopping started before the event. Amazon said customers can buy early deals now, including daily deals, and can set alerts that notify them when items they have searched for or viewed go on sale during the event.

The announcement comes as other retailers spread their sales across the month. Walmart is running three “Deals for Days” events beginning on Mondays in November, the second of them starting on November 14, Progressive Grocer reported.

Why it matters for brands

A 48-hour event with deal drops every 30 minutes concentrates attention into short windows. Brands with deals in those windows will see sharp spikes in traffic, and advertising competition will be highest when the drops happen.

Deal alerts change who sees a discount. Shoppers who viewed a product before the event can be told when it goes on sale, which rewards brands that built traffic in early November.

What to do now

  1. Confirm stock for any product in a Black Friday deal, and add a margin for the spikes during deal drops.
  2. Keep advertising running through the week before the event, so shoppers view your products and qualify for alerts.
  3. Set bid caps for November 24 and 25 in advance, and check them during the deal windows.

A0323.crumb: Early read: Cyber Week 2022 from public…
A0323.title: Early read: Cyber Week 2022 from public sources, labeled preliminary
A0323.alt: Blue, red and orange paper shopping bags lined up on a weathered wooden bench against a sunlit cream wall.
A0323.ttag: Early read: Cyber Week 2022 from public sources, labeled preliminary | Kwontified
A0323.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 30, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0323.body:
U.S. shoppers spent $35.3 billion online from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday 2022, up 4% from 2021, with Cyber Monday the largest online shopping day on record at $11.3 billion, Adobe reported on November 29. These are early figures, and this read will be updated as fuller data arrives.

What happened

Adobe said Cyber Monday spending grew 5.8%, Black Friday reached $9.12 billion, up 2.3%, and Thanksgiving $5.29 billion, up 2.9%. Buy now, pay later orders rose 85% compared with the previous week. Adobe raised its forecast for the full holiday season to $210.1 billion, up 2.75%, after spending of $107.7 billion from November 1 to 28.

Shoppers came out in person too. A record 196.7 million people shopped in stores or online over the five days, with in-store shoppers up 17% to 122.7 million and online shoppers up 2% to 130.2 million, the National Retail Federation reported. Shoppers said they had completed 47% of their holiday shopping.

Amazon had not reported its own results at the time of writing.

Why it matters for brands

The week beat the cautious forecasts. In October, Adobe expected Cyber Week to grow 2.8%; it grew 4%. Heavy discounting drove the result, so the growth came at a cost to margin.

The figures are in dollars and not adjusted for inflation, and they do not show how much demand was pulled forward from December or back from October. Those answers come in the weeks ahead.

What to do now

  1. Record your own Cyber Week sales, click prices and share of units sold on deal while the data is fresh.
  2. Compare them with your plan, and with an average day in the four weeks before.
  3. Keep stock and advertising steady into December, since shoppers report more than half their holiday buying still to do.

A0325.title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a conversational AI model, as a free preview
A0325.alt: A white six-wheeled delivery robot with its lid open carries a cardboard parcel on a sidewalk by a lilac wall.
A0325.ttag: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a conversational AI model, as a free preview | Kwontified
A0325.desc: OpenAI released ChatGPT on November 30, 2022, a model that interacts in a conversational way and is free to use during a research preview, according to…
A0325.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 1, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0325.body:
OpenAI released ChatGPT on November 30, 2022, a model that interacts in a conversational way and is free to use during a research preview, according to OpenAI.

What happened

OpenAI said the dialogue format lets ChatGPT answer follow-up questions, admit its mistakes, challenge incorrect premises and reject inappropriate requests. It described ChatGPT as a sibling model to InstructGPT, which is trained to follow an instruction in a prompt and give a detailed response, and said ChatGPT was fine-tuned from a model in its GPT-3.5 series that finished training in early 2022.

The model was trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback, in which human trainers wrote and ranked responses. OpenAI said it is releasing ChatGPT to learn about its strengths and weaknesses from users, and that limitations remain, including answers that can sound plausible but be wrong.

Why it matters for brands

ChatGPT is not a shopping tool, and it does not search the web or link to products. But it shows a different way of asking for information: a conversation that refines a question over several turns, instead of a list of keywords and a page of results.

If shoppers come to expect that kind of answer, the way products are discovered could change. A shopper might describe a need and receive a recommendation, rather than type a search term and compare listings. The brands that are described clearly and accurately in public sources would be better placed for that change.

The model’s limits matter as much as its abilities. It can state wrong information confidently, so anything it says about a product, a price or a policy should not be treated as reliable.

What to do now

  1. Try ChatGPT with the questions your customers ask, and note how it describes your category.
  2. Review whether your product descriptions answer those questions clearly in plain language.
  3. Treat any AI-generated claim about your products as unverified until checked.

A0338.crumb: INFORM Consumers Act signed into law…
A0338.title: INFORM Consumers Act signed into law; marketplace seller rules take effect in June 2023
A0338.alt: Five colorful mailboxes on a lilac wall above a string-tied brown paper parcel on the sidewalk.
A0338.ttag: INFORM Consumers Act signed into law; marketplace seller rules take effect in June 2023 | Kwontified
A0338.desc: President Biden signed the year-end government spending bill on December 29, 2022, the Associated Press reported , making the INFORM Consumers Act law.
A0338.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 30, 2022. 1-minute read.
A0338.body:
President Biden signed the year-end government spending bill on December 29, 2022, the Associated Press reported, making the INFORM Consumers Act law. The Act requires online marketplaces to verify and disclose information about their high-volume third-party sellers. Its requirements take effect 180 days after enactment, which falls in late June 2023.

What happened

Congress added the INFORM Consumers Act to the spending bill, which the House passed on December 23, eBay noted. The Act directs marketplaces to verify the government ID, tax ID, bank account information and contact details of high-volume third-party sellers, defined as sellers with 200 or more separate sales totaling $5,000 or more in a 12-month period, according to its Senate sponsors.

Marketplaces must also ensure those sellers disclose basic identity and contact information to shoppers, and must offer a way for shoppers to report suspicious listings. Individual sellers may keep a personal street address and phone number private if they answer shopper questions by email promptly. The Federal Trade Commission will enforce the law, and violations carry civil penalties.

Why it matters for brands

The law is aimed at stolen, counterfeit and unsafe goods sold by anonymous sellers. For brands that face unauthorized resellers or counterfeits, more verified seller identities should make it easier to find and act against them.

For brands that sell on marketplaces themselves, the law adds paperwork. Nearly every established brand seller meets the high-volume threshold, so marketplaces will ask for documents and certifications, and sellers who are slow to respond could face disruption to their accounts.

What to do now

  1. Gather current government ID, tax ID, bank and contact records for every marketplace seller account you operate.
  2. Make sure the business name and contact details shoppers will see are the ones you want public.
  3. Watch for verification requests from Amazon, Walmart, eBay and others in the first half of 2023, and answer them quickly.

A0358.crumb: Temu runs its first Super Bowl ad, five…
A0358.title: Temu runs its first Super Bowl ad, five months after launching in the U.S.
A0358.alt: A grey plastic crate overflowing with orange poly mailer bags against a sunlit orange wall.
A0358.ttag: Temu runs its first Super Bowl ad, five months after launching in the U.S. | Kwontified
A0358.desc: Temu, the shopping app owned by PDD Holdings, aired a 30-second commercial twice during the Super Bowl on February 12, 2023, in the first and third…
A0358.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 13, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0358.body:
Temu, the shopping app owned by PDD Holdings, aired a 30-second commercial twice during the Super Bowl on February 12, 2023, in the first and third quarters, Adweek reported. The company launched in the U.S. in September 2022, which makes it one of the youngest brands ever to advertise during the game.

What happened

The spot, titled “Shop Like a Billionaire” and created by the agency Saatchi & Saatchi, shows a shopper delighted by low-priced items on the Temu app. Adweek reported that a 30-second slot in the game cost about $7 million, and that Temu planned to run the ad twice more after the game and during the Daytona 500.

The campaign builds on heavy spending to acquire users. Temu has held the top spot on Apple’s U.S. App Store since January 3 and had about 19 million lifetime installs, more than 18 million of them in the U.S., TechCrunch reported in January, citing Sensor Tower. TechCrunch noted that much of that growth appears to come from marketing spend.

Why it matters for brands

Temu is no longer a quiet experiment. A Super Bowl buy is a bid for mass awareness among American shoppers, not just early adopters, and it signals that PDD is willing to spend heavily to make Temu a household name.

For brands, the near-term effect is on attention and price perception rather than on their own channels. Temu does not sell most established brands. It sells low-priced, often unbranded goods shipped from overseas. But every shopper it reaches sees a price for a phone case, a kitchen tool or a piece of jewelry that may anchor what they expect to pay elsewhere.

Paid acquisition at this scale also raises the cost of attention. Temu bids for the same app store, social and video audiences that brands use to reach shoppers.

What to do now

  1. Identify which of your products face direct price comparison with low-priced Temu alternatives, and make the differences in quality, delivery speed and returns clear on your listings.
  2. Watch your own social and app-install advertising costs over the coming weeks for signs of heavier competition for the same audiences.
  3. Track whether your lowest-priced products lose sales while the rest of your range holds steady, which would point to shoppers testing Temu for small purchases.

A0383.title: Amazon sets Accelerate 2023 for September 13-14 in Seattle
A0383.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0383.ttag: Amazon sets Accelerate 2023 for September 13-14 in Seattle | Kwontified
A0383.desc: Amazon has announced that its annual seller conference, Amazon Accelerate, will take place live in Seattle on September 13-14, 2023, with pre-conference…
A0383.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 10, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0383.body:
Amazon has announced that its annual seller conference, Amazon Accelerate, will take place live in Seattle on September 13-14, 2023, with pre-conference activities for in-person attendees starting at noon on September 12, Value Added Resource reported on March 9, quoting Amazon’s announcement.

What happened

Amazon describes Accelerate as its premier annual conference for selling partners and anyone interested in selling in its stores, with sessions on new tools, access to Amazon experts and networking with other sellers. The company said it would release details on registration, keynote speakers, hotels and travel discounts in the coming months.

Amazon had not said whether it would also offer virtual sessions, as it did for the 2022 conference, according to the same report.

Why it matters for brands

Accelerate is where Amazon tends to introduce changes to the tools sellers use every day, from listing and inventory features to advertising and brand programs. Announcements made in September often take effect during the fourth quarter, the busiest selling period of the year.

That timing matters for planning. A brand that learns about a new tool in mid-September has only weeks to decide whether to use it before holiday traffic arrives. Brands that build time for that review into their calendars can act on useful changes quickly, rather than discovering them after the season has started.

Accelerate is also one of the few chances for sellers to speak directly with Amazon teams. For brands with unresolved account, catalog or advertising questions, that access can be worth more than the keynote announcements.

What to do now

Decide early whether your team will attend in person, so travel can be booked once registration opens. If you cannot attend, assign someone to follow the announcements closely in September.

Write down the questions you would most like Amazon to answer, such as gaps in reporting, catalog problems or advertising features you need. Bring them to the conference, or use them as a checklist against what Amazon announces.

Finally, leave room in your fourth-quarter plan for changes. Hold a short review in late September to decide which announcements to adopt before the holiday season and which to test in the new year.

We will cover the most important Accelerate announcements for brands when the conference takes place.

A0414.crumb: Amazon sets Prime Day 2023 for July 11-12
A0414.title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2023 for July 11-12
A0414.alt: Stacked cardboard boxes topped with a striped towel beside potted red geraniums on a stone step by a blue wall.
A0414.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Day 2023 for July 11-12 | Kwontified
A0414.desc: Amazon will hold its 2023 Prime Day sales event on Tuesday, July 11, and Wednesday, July 12, the company announced on June 21, GeekWire reported .
A0414.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 22, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0414.body:
Amazon will hold its 2023 Prime Day sales event on Tuesday, July 11, and Wednesday, July 12, the company announced on June 21, GeekWire reported. The event begins at 3 a.m. Eastern time on July 11 and runs through July 12, Retail TouchPoints reported.

What happened

Amazon confirmed the dates for its 48-hour, members-only sale, which falls one day earlier than the July 12 and 13 dates of 2022. Amazon is also adding invite-only deals for some products, along with savings on some brands’ own websites through its Buy with Prime service, GeekWire reported.

Amazon described the 2022 event as the biggest Prime Day in its history, with more than 300 million items bought worldwide and $1.7 billion saved by Prime members.

Shoppers may be more careful in 2023. Research from RetailMeNot found the average Prime Day shopper planning to spend $250 across Amazon and rival retailers’ sales, down from $388 in 2022, Retail TouchPoints reported.

Why it matters for brands

The announcement leaves less than three weeks before the event. Amazon’s deadline for submitting Prime Day deals passed in April, so for most brands the remaining decisions are about stock, advertising and how to handle the days around the event.

Lower planned spending suggests a selective shopper. Deals on products people already intend to buy are likely to do better than impulse items, and competition for attention on the event days is likely to be intense.

What to do now

Confirm that inventory for deal products is in place, with a buffer for the days before and after the event, when shoppers research and return to buy.

Finalize event advertising budgets now, concentrated on deal products and the searches that lead to them, and set rules for raising budgets on July 11 and 12 if results are strong.

Plan to review results within two weeks, across the full surrounding period rather than the two event days alone.

A0416.crumb: Seller verification law takes effect for…
A0416.title: Seller verification law takes effect for online marketplaces
A0416.alt: Five colorful mailboxes on a lilac wall above a string-tied brown paper parcel on the sidewalk.
A0416.ttag: Seller verification law takes effect for online marketplaces | Kwontified
A0416.desc: The INFORM Consumers Act took effect on June 27, 2023, requiring online marketplaces to collect, verify and in some cases disclose information about…
A0416.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 28, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0416.body:
The INFORM Consumers Act took effect on June 27, 2023, requiring online marketplaces to collect, verify and in some cases disclose information about high-volume third-party sellers, Fenwick reported. On June 20, the Federal Trade Commission sent letters to 50 online marketplaces reminding them of their obligations and urging them to comply by that date, Fenwick noted.

What happened

The law applies to third-party sellers with 200 or more sales of new or unused consumer products and $5,000 or more in gross revenue in any continuous 12-month period during the previous 24 months. Marketplaces must collect and verify those sellers’ bank account, contact and tax identification details, and must suspend sellers who do not provide the information within 10 days of a request, Fenwick explained.

Sellers with $20,000 or more in annual gross revenue on a marketplace face added requirements to disclose identifying information to shoppers. Marketplaces must also give shoppers a way to report suspicious activity on each product listing.

Why it matters for brands

For brands selling as third-party sellers on Amazon, Walmart, Target Plus and other marketplaces, verification is now a legal requirement with a firm deadline attached. A missed request for information can lead to a suspension, with sales and advertising stopping until the account is restored.

Brands selling wholesale to a retailer as a vendor are not the sellers the law targets, but many brands run both models. The seller accounts are the ones at risk.

The law is also aimed at counterfeit and stolen goods, which should make it harder for anonymous resellers to undercut brands on their own product pages.

What to do now

Check that the contact, bank and tax details on every seller account are current, and that marketplace notices go to an inbox more than one person monitors.

Respond to any verification or recertification request immediately, and keep the documents marketplaces may ask for ready to send.

Name an owner for account health on each marketplace, with a weekly review of notices.

A0451.crumb: TikTok Shop launches in the United States
A0451.title: TikTok Shop launches in the United States
A0451.alt: A ring light with a phone clamp stands beside a wooden stool holding amber skincare bottles against a teal wall.
A0451.ttag: TikTok Shop launches in the United States | Kwontified
A0451.desc: TikTok officially launched TikTok Shop in the United States on September 12, after months of testing, TechCrunch reported .
A0451.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 13, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0451.body:
TikTok officially launched TikTok Shop in the United States on September 12, after months of testing, TechCrunch reported. The company said more than 200,000 sellers had already signed up to sell through the service, and more than 100,000 creators had joined its affiliate program.

What happened

TikTok Shop lets people buy products directly inside the TikTok app, from short videos, live streams and a dedicated shopping tab. The launch brings together several features, the Associated Press reported: a Shop tab that TikTok has tested since August, affiliate videos in users’ feeds that let creators earn commissions on products they promote, and a logistics service called Fulfilled by TikTok that stores and ships products for merchants.

Merchants can also connect TikTok Shop to the commerce platforms they already use. Shopify merchants, for example, can manage their TikTok Shop from Shopify through the TikTok for Shopify app, Retail TouchPoints reported.

Why it matters for brands

TikTok Shop combines discovery and purchase in one place. Shoppers who see a product in a video can buy it without leaving the app, and creators earn a commission when they do. That makes creators part of the sales channel, not only the marketing.

For brands, it opens a new marketplace with its own rules, fees and fulfillment options, alongside Amazon, Walmart and the brand’s own site. It also raises practical questions: how to manage inventory across one more channel, how to price consistently, and how to work with creators who may promote a product without the brand’s direct involvement.

The size of the early seller base suggests competition on the platform will build quickly.

What to do now

Decide whether TikTok Shop fits your products and audience. Products that demonstrate well on video and appeal to TikTok’s audience are the most natural fit.

If it does, start small. Open a shop with a limited range, connect it to your existing commerce platform, and test the affiliate program with a few creators before scaling up.

Set rules for pricing and inventory across channels before you launch, so a promotion on TikTok does not undercut your other marketplaces or leave you short of stock elsewhere.

We will publish a fuller look at what TikTok Shop means for brands in the coming days.

A0455.title: Amazon Accelerate 2023: the announcements that matter for brands
A0455.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0455.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2023: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0455.desc: Amazon used its annual seller conference, Accelerate, held in Seattle on September 13 and 14, to launch a generative AI tool that writes product listings…
A0455.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 15, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0455.body:
Amazon used its annual seller conference, Accelerate, held in Seattle on September 13 and 14, to launch a generative AI tool that writes product listings and an end-to-end logistics service called Supply Chain by Amazon. Both change how much of a seller’s operation Amazon can run on its behalf.

What happened

On September 13, Amazon launched a generative AI tool that helps sellers create product listings, SiliconANGLE reported. Sellers provide a few details about a product, and the tool drafts a title, bullet points and a description. Amazon said that many sellers had tested the tool in recent months and that most were using the content it generated directly, ChannelX reported. Amazon also cautioned that sellers should review every AI-generated listing for accuracy.

Amazon also announced Supply Chain by Amazon, an automated set of services to move products from manufacturing locations to customers, using Amazon’s logistics, warehousing, distribution and fulfillment capabilities, EcomCrew reported on September 14. The service is designed to cover a seller’s inventory across sales channels, not only orders placed on Amazon.

Why it matters for brands

The two announcements point in the same direction. Amazon is offering to take over more of the work of selling, from writing the listing to moving stock from the factory.

The listing tool can save time, especially for brands with large catalogs. But a listing written quickly is not the same as a listing written well. AI-generated copy can be generic or inaccurate, and listing quality drives both conversion and how well a product is found, including by the AI shopping tools now being tested.

Supply Chain by Amazon could simplify logistics for brands that juggle several warehouses and carriers. It would also deepen their dependence on Amazon, since the same company would hold their inventory, ship their orders and set the fees for both.

What to do now

Test the listing tool on a few products, and compare the results with your current listings before using it widely. Check every generated listing for accuracy, required claims and the attributes shoppers ask about.

Ask what Supply Chain by Amazon would cost compared with your current logistics, and what it would mean to have more of your inventory in one partner’s hands.

We will look at both announcements in more detail for brands in the coming weeks.

A0456.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0456.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Big Deal Days for October 10 and 11 | Kwontified
A0456.desc: Amazon announced on September 18 that its fall Prime event, now called Prime Big Deal Days, will run for 48 hours starting at 3 a.m.
A0456.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 19, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0456.body:
Amazon announced on September 18 that its fall Prime event, now called Prime Big Deal Days, will run for 48 hours starting at 3 a.m. EDT on October 10 and ending on October 11, Fox reported. The event is open to Prime members.

What happened

The event replaces the Prime Early Access Sale, which Amazon held on October 11 and 12, 2022, EcommerceBytes reported. Deals go live at 3 a.m. Eastern time on the first day, MobileSyrup reported, and Amazon is presenting the sale as an early start to holiday shopping.

The announcement comes about three weeks before the event. Amazon told sellers that the date for sending inventory to its warehouses in time for the event had already passed, but that they could still create coupons, Prime Exclusive Discounts and Sponsored Products campaigns before or during the event, according to Amazon’s seller forum.

Why it matters for brands

The October event is the first major sales moment of the holiday season. In 2022, it drew fewer shoppers and smaller orders than July’s Prime Day, so brands should size their plans accordingly.

With the inventory deadline already behind them, most brands’ options now lie in pricing, coupons and advertising. Click prices typically rise during these events as more brands compete for the same shoppers, so budgets set now will determine how much visibility a brand can buy on October 10 and 11.

Competing retailers usually run their own events around the same dates, which affects pricing decisions for brands that sell across several channels.

What to do now

Confirm your stock position for the products you plan to promote, since inventory already at Amazon is what you can sell during the event.

Set advertising budgets for the days before, during and after the event, and plan bid changes in advance.

Decide on coupons or Prime Exclusive Discounts for products with the margin to support them, and check your pricing across other channels so the October offer does not create conflicts.

We will publish a review of Prime Big Deal Days for brands after the event.

A0460.title: Amazon will show limited ads in Prime Video starting in 2024
A0460.alt: Empty wooden picture frame and a twine-tied cardboard parcel leaning against a sunlit mustard-yellow wall.
A0460.ttag: Amazon will show limited ads in Prime Video starting in 2024 | Kwontified
A0460.desc: Amazon said on September 22 that Prime Video shows and movies will include limited advertisements starting in early 2024, Axios reported .
A0460.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 25, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0460.body:
Amazon said on September 22 that Prime Video shows and movies will include limited advertisements starting in early 2024, Axios reported. Members in the United States will be able to keep their viewing ad-free for an additional $2.99 a month.

What happened

The ads will start in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and Canada in early 2024, followed by France, Italy, Spain, Mexico and Australia later in the year, Fox reported. Live events on Prime Video, such as sports, already carry advertising.

Amazon made the announcement in a blog post and said it would introduce the ads so it could keep investing in content, PYMNTS reported. It said it would not change the price of a Prime membership in 2024, Advanced Television reported, and that it would email members several weeks before the ads begin.

Why it matters for brands

The change creates a large new supply of streaming video advertising inside Amazon. Prime Video reaches the same Prime members who shop on Amazon, so brands will be able to show video ads to shoppers in a premium viewing environment and connect those ads to shopping behavior that Amazon can measure.

That makes streaming TV a more practical option for brands that already advertise on Amazon. Until now, most of Amazon’s video advertising sat in places such as Freevee, Twitch and live sports. Prime Video adds shows and movies watched by a much wider audience.

It also raises questions brands will need to answer as details emerge: how the ads will be bought, what they will cost, how they will be measured against sales on Amazon, and how much of a brand’s budget should move from search advertising toward upper-funnel video.

What to do now

Watch for Amazon’s details on how Prime Video ads will be sold and measured, which are likely to come through Amazon’s advertising tools before the launch in 2024.

Consider whether streaming video fits your brand. Brands with strong creative and a need to reach new customers, rather than only shoppers already searching, are the most natural fit.

If you plan to test it, start building the video creative now, and plan how you will measure its effect on sales.

We will look at what Prime Video ads mean for advertising plans in more detail in the coming weeks.

A0461.title: The FTC and 17 states sue Amazon on antitrust grounds
A0461.alt: An open cardboard box spilling kraft packing paper beside a roll of tape on a sunlit wooden bench.
A0461.ttag: The FTC and 17 states sue Amazon on antitrust grounds | Kwontified
A0461.desc: The Federal Trade Commission and attorneys general from 17 states sued Amazon on September 26 in federal court in Seattle, accusing the company of using…
A0461.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 27, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0461.body:
The Federal Trade Commission and attorneys general from 17 states sued Amazon on September 26 in federal court in Seattle, accusing the company of using monopoly power to inflate prices, degrade quality for shoppers and unlawfully exclude rivals, CNBC reported. The case centers on how Amazon treats the independent sellers who use its marketplace.

What happened

The complaint focuses on two sets of practices, according to the FTC.

The first is what the FTC calls anti-discounting. It alleges that Amazon uses measures that punish sellers and deter other online retailers from offering prices lower than Amazon’s, which keeps prices higher for products across the internet.

The second concerns fulfillment. The FTC alleges that Amazon makes Prime eligibility, which it describes as a virtual necessity for doing business on Amazon, conditional on sellers using Amazon’s own fulfillment service. That, it says, has made it substantially more expensive for sellers to offer products on other platforms. By tying Prime eligibility to Fulfillment by Amazon, the FTC alleges, Amazon restricts sellers’ choice of fulfillment provider, SiliconANGLE reported.

The case is at its start, and a lawsuit of this size can take years to resolve.

Why it matters for brands

Nothing changes for sellers immediately. Amazon’s rules on pricing, Prime eligibility and fulfillment remain in force while the case proceeds.

But the suit targets the practices that shape how most brands sell on Amazon: how they price across channels, and how they get the Prime badge that drives so much of their sales. If the case succeeds, or if Amazon changes its policies to reduce its legal risk, those rules could change. That could affect fulfillment costs, the options for reaching Prime shoppers, and how freely brands can price differently on other sites.

What to do now

Keep operating under Amazon’s current rules. Do not change pricing or fulfillment strategy based on the lawsuit alone.

Review how much of your business depends on Prime eligibility and Fulfillment by Amazon, and what alternatives you would consider if the rules changed.

Watch for any policy changes from Amazon on pricing or fulfillment in the months ahead.

We will look at what the case could change for sellers in more detail.

A0470.crumb: Prime Big Deal Days 2023: an early read…
A0470.title: Prime Big Deal Days 2023: an early read from public sources
A0470.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0470.ttag: Prime Big Deal Days 2023: an early read from public sources | Kwontified
A0470.desc: Amazon says Prime Big Deal Days surpassed its expectations.
A0470.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 13, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0470.body:
Amazon says Prime Big Deal Days surpassed its expectations. Early panel data shows orders slightly larger than the October 2022 event, but smaller than July’s. This is a preliminary read from public sources. It suggests a solid fall sale rather than a second Prime Day, and brands should judge their own results against the October 2022 event, not against July.

What happened

Amazon held Prime Big Deal Days on October 10 and 11. On October 12, Doug Herrington, CEO of Worldwide Amazon Stores, said the event surpassed Amazon’s expectations and was a strong start to the holiday season, CNBC reported. Amazon did not release total sales.

According to Numerator’s panel data, the average order during the event was $53.47, down from July’s Prime Day but up slightly from the October 2022 fall sale, CNBC reported.

Numerator’s early read from the first 30 hours of the event found that 46% of shopping households had already placed two or more orders. A third of Prime Big Deal Days shoppers said they also shopped or planned to shop Walmart’s competing event, and 27% had shopped Target Circle Week, according to Numerator.

Why it matters for brands

The early data points to an event that grew on the October 2022 event but did not match July. That is consistent with the planning assumption that the October event behaves like a smaller Prime Day, not an equal one.

It also shows how crowded the week was. With Walmart and Target running events around the same dates, many shoppers compared offers across retailers. A brand’s results on Amazon may reflect its prices elsewhere as much as its Amazon deals.

These figures are early and come from a consumer panel, not from Amazon’s own sales data. Final numbers, and each brand’s own results, will tell a fuller story.

What to do now

  1. Compare your event results with the October 2022 event and with your forecast ranges, not with July’s Prime Day.
  2. Pull the week before and the week after the event, and check whether sales were added or simply pulled forward.
  3. Review your prices at Walmart and Target during the same week, since shoppers were comparing across all three.

We will publish a fuller assessment once complete data is available.

A0479.title: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2023: the announcements that matter for brands
A0479.alt: A spotlight on a stand aimed at a plain white box on a white plinth against a navy blue wall.
A0479.ttag: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2023: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0479.desc: Amazon Ads used its unBoxed conference in New York, held October 24 to 26, to announce a self-service streaming TV ad product with no minimum spend, an AI…
A0479.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 27, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0479.body:
Amazon Ads used its unBoxed conference in New York, held October 24 to 26, to announce a self-service streaming TV ad product with no minimum spend, an AI tool that generates lifestyle images for ads, a data clean room for publishers, and the extension of Sponsored Products ads to sites beyond Amazon. For most brands, the first two matter most, because they lower the cost of formats that used to need large budgets or a creative agency.

What happened

Amazon introduced Sponsored TV, which lets brands run streaming TV ads with no minimum spend requirement, Modern Retail reported on October 26. It also introduced a generative AI tool in beta that creates lifestyle images, placing a product in a setting rather than on a plain background, and Amazon Publisher Cloud, which lets publishers analyze their own audience signals alongside Amazon Ads insights, according to the same report.

Amazon also said Sponsored Products campaigns will extend to premium apps and websites in the US, including Pinterest, BuzzFeed and Hearst Newspapers, Canopy Management reported on October 26.

Why it matters for brands

Until now, streaming TV ads on Amazon generally required buying through Amazon’s demand-side platform, with budgets that put them out of reach for many brands. Sponsored TV moves streaming video into the self-service console most brands already use. That makes it possible to test video at a small scale, alongside search ads.

The image tool addresses a common gap. Many brands have clean product photos but few lifestyle images, which tend to perform better in display and brand ads. A tool that generates them from existing photos lowers the cost of testing creative.

Extending Sponsored Products beyond Amazon changes where search budgets can appear. Brands should watch how those placements are reported, so off-Amazon results are not mixed in with on-Amazon ones without being noticed.

As with any new ad product, early results will vary, and brands should measure what each adds rather than assume it works.

What to do now

  1. Plan a small Sponsored TV test with its own budget, and measure it against a holdout rather than on immediate return.
  2. Try the image tool on a few products, and review every generated image for accuracy before using it.
  3. Check your Sponsored Products reports for placements outside Amazon as they appear, and track them separately.

We will publish a fuller assessment of what unBoxed changes for advertisers next week.

A0482.title: Amazon sets Black Friday event for November 17 to 27
A0482.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
A0482.ttag: Amazon sets Black Friday event for November 17 to 27 | Kwontified
A0482.desc: Amazon said on November 6 that its Black Friday event will start on Friday, November 17, a week before Black Friday itself, followed by a Cyber Monday…
A0482.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 7, 2023. 1-minute read.
A0482.body:
Amazon said on November 6 that its Black Friday event will start on Friday, November 17, a week before Black Friday itself, followed by a Cyber Monday weekend event from November 25 to 27. The longer window spreads shopper demand across eleven days. Brands should spread their budgets, stock and deal timing to match, rather than concentrating everything on the weekend.

What happened

Amazon announced that its Black Friday selling event will begin on Friday, November 17, HomePage News reported on November 6. Amazon will continue the promotion with a Cyber Monday weekend event starting Saturday, November 25, and running through Monday, November 27, RTTNews reported on November 6.

Black Friday falls on November 24 in 2023, and Cyber Monday on November 27.

Why it matters for brands

An eleven-day event behaves differently from a weekend. Demand that used to arrive over four days will be spread across more than a week, with peaks likely around the start of the event, Black Friday itself and Cyber Monday.

That affects three things. Advertising budgets set for a long weekend may run out early, or spend too heavily in the first days. Inventory planned for a short burst may sell through before the peak days arrive. And deals scheduled for the weekend alone may miss shoppers who buy early.

It also gives brands more room. Shoppers who start early can be reached at lower competition in the first days, before the busiest dates push click prices up.

What to do now

  1. Re-phase Cyber Week advertising budgets across November 17 to 27, with daily caps so spend lasts through Cyber Monday.
  2. Check that inventory for promoted products covers eleven days of demand, not four.
  3. Confirm which of your deals run in which part of the event, and fill gaps in the first week if needed.

We will publish our Cyber Week forecast ranges alongside this news.

A0493.crumb: Cyber Week 2023: an early read from…
A0493.title: Cyber Week 2023: an early read from public sources
A0493.alt: Blue, red and orange paper shopping bags lined up on a weathered wooden bench against a sunlit cream wall.
A0493.ttag: Cyber Week 2023: an early read from public sources | Kwontified
A0493.desc: Cyber Week 2023 set a record for online spending, beating Adobe’s own forecast.
A0493.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 29, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0493.body:
Cyber Week 2023 set a record for online spending, beating Adobe’s own forecast. Cyber Monday reached $12.4 billion and the five days from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday reached $38 billion. This is a preliminary read from public, market-wide data. It suggests shoppers responded to discounts more strongly than expected, and brands should check whether their own results beat their plans by a similar margin before drawing conclusions.

What happened

Consumers spent $12.4 billion online on Cyber Monday, up 9.6% from a year earlier and above Adobe’s initial projection, according to Adobe on November 28. Cyber Week as a whole brought in $38 billion, up 7.8%, with Black Friday at $9.8 billion, up 7.5%, and Thanksgiving at $5.6 billion, up 5.5%.

Adobe had forecast $37.2 billion for Cyber Week and $12 billion for Cyber Monday in October. Paid search remained the biggest marketing driver of retailers’ online sales across Cyber Week, at 27%, Adobe said.

Shoppers leaned on flexible payment. Buy now, pay later accounted for $940 million in Cyber Monday spending, up 42.5%, The Boston Globe reported on November 28.

Why it matters for brands

The market grew faster than forecast. Cyber Week came in about 2% above Adobe’s October projection, and Cyber Monday about 3% above it. That gives brands a benchmark for reading their own results: a brand that merely matched its plan may have lost share in a week when the market beat expectations.

The prominence of paid search matters too. With search driving more than a quarter of online sales, the click premium and budget pacing during the event shaped which brands captured the extra demand.

These figures are market-wide and preliminary. They do not show any single retailer’s results, and each brand’s outcome depended on its category, deals and stock.

What to do now

  1. Compare your Cyber Week results with your plan, and with the market’s roughly 2% beat over forecast.
  2. Measure the weeks before and after the event, to see whether sales were added or pulled forward.
  3. Review search spend and click prices by day, to see where budget ran short or went unspent.

We will grade our own Cyber Week forecast against the full data next week.

A0498.title: Amazon details 2024 fee changes, including a low-inventory-level fee
A0498.alt: A brass hanging balance scale tips with a stack of coins on one pan and a twine-tied parcel on the other.
A0498.ttag: Amazon details 2024 fee changes, including a low-inventory-level fee | Kwontified
A0498.desc: Amazon said on December 5 that it will restructure its US fulfillment fees in 2024, lowering outbound fees while adding new fees tied to how sellers send…
A0498.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 6, 2023. 2-minute read.
A0498.body:
Amazon said on December 5 that it will restructure its US fulfillment fees in 2024, lowering outbound fees while adding new fees tied to how sellers send and stock inventory. The most important for many brands is a new low-inventory-level fee for standard-size products that carry too little stock relative to sales. Running lean on Amazon inventory will now cost money directly, so brands should review their cover before the fee takes effect in April.

What happened

Amazon outlined its 2024 changes to US referral and fulfillment fees, separating inbound and outbound services, Value Added Resource reported on December 5. Amazon said it would lower outbound fees while creating new inbound fees that sellers can reduce or avoid depending on how they send in products.

Three changes stand out. An inbound placement service fee will take effect on March 1, 2024, charged 45 days after products are received. New fulfillment fee rates for standard-size products will apply from April 15. And a new low-inventory-level fee will apply from April 1 to standard-size products that carry consistently low inventory relative to sales. Sellers can avoid it by keeping more than about four weeks of inventory relative to sales, according to the same report.

Why it matters for brands

The low-inventory-level fee changes the economics of running lean. Many brands keep Amazon stock tight to limit storage fees and the cash tied up in inventory. From April, carrying too little will also carry a cost.

That puts brands between two fees. Too much stock brings storage and aged-inventory charges. Too little brings the new fee. The right level now sits in a narrower band, and it depends on accurate sales forecasts.

The inbound placement fee also matters. How a brand ships to Amazon, to one location or several, will affect what it pays. Brands should review their shipping plans before March.

What to do now

  1. Calculate weeks of cover for each standard-size product, and flag those running below four weeks.
  2. Review forecasts and reorder timing for those products before April 1.
  3. Compare inbound shipping options and their placement fees before March 1.

We will publish an analysis of the arithmetic behind the low-inventory-level fee next week.
