A0521.crumb: Prime Video ads go live in the US
A0521.title: Prime Video ads go live in the US
A0521.alt: Empty wooden picture frame and a twine-tied cardboard parcel leaning against a sunlit mustard-yellow wall.
A0521.ttag: Prime Video ads go live in the US | Kwontified
A0521.desc: Amazon’s change to show limited ads in Prime Video movies and TV shows took effect on January 29, as it had told members in December, with an ad-free…
A0521.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jan 30, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0521.body:
Amazon’s change to show limited ads in Prime Video movies and TV shows took effect on January 29, as it had told members in December, with an ad-free option for an extra $2.99 a month. That moves a large streaming audience into Amazon’s advertising inventory by default. Brands planning streaming video in 2024 should treat Prime Video as a new placement to test against their own sales, rather than as reach to buy on faith.

What happened

In late December, Amazon emailed US Prime members to say that, starting January 29, Prime Video movies and TV shows would include limited advertisements, with no change to the price of Prime and a new ad-free option for an additional $2.99 a month, MacRumors reported on December 27.

Ads were to begin in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and Canada, with France, Italy, Spain, Mexico and Australia to follow later in 2024, RetailWire reported. Amazon had first announced the plan in September.

Why it matters for brands

The change is structural. Because ads are the default and the ad-free option costs extra, most Prime members who keep their current plan will see ads. That gives Amazon a large streaming audience to sell to advertisers, connected to its shopping data.

For brands, the opportunity is reach on a big screen to an audience Amazon can link to purchase behavior. The risk is buying that reach because it is new and large, without checking what it adds. Streaming video affects sales slowly and often outside the ad’s own reporting, so attributed results will understate some effects and overstate others.

Pricing is also likely to move. A new placement with a large audience may attract strong early demand from advertisers, and the price of reaching viewers will reflect that.

What to do now

  1. Treat Prime Video as a test, with a holdout or a matched comparison, before shifting budget into it.
  2. Judge results on branded searches and total sales across channels, not only on attributed sales.
  3. Start with products whose demand responds to awareness, such as new launches, rather than everyday staples.

We will report on early Prime Video results as brands’ first tests come in.

A0523.title: Amazon introduces Rufus, a generative AI shopping assistant, in beta
A0523.alt: A gray fabric smart speaker beside a bowl of lemons and a notepad on a sunlit wooden table against a sage wall.
A0523.ttag: Amazon introduces Rufus, a generative AI shopping assistant, in beta | Kwontified
A0523.desc: Amazon introduced Rufus on February 1, a generative AI shopping assistant that answers shoppers’ questions using its product catalog, customer reviews and…
A0523.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 2, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0523.body:
Amazon introduced Rufus on February 1, a generative AI shopping assistant that answers shoppers’ questions using its product catalog, customer reviews and community questions and answers. That makes the content on a product page something an AI reads and summarizes for shoppers, not only something shoppers read themselves. Brands should review their listings, reviews and answered questions as inputs to Rufus, and check how it describes their products as it rolls out.

What happened

Amazon launched Rufus in beta to a small subset of customers in its mobile app, saying it would roll out to more US customers in the coming weeks, according to Amazon on February 1. Rufus answers questions about shopping needs and products, makes comparisons and recommendations, and helps shoppers find items. Amazon cautioned that the technology would not always get answers exactly right.

The assistant was trained on Amazon’s product catalog, shopper reviews and content from its customer questions and answers section, SiliconANGLE reported on February 1. Shoppers can ask about a specific product while viewing its page, and Rufus answers from the listing details, reviews and answers.

Rufus follows Amazon’s AI-generated review summaries, introduced in 2023.

Why it matters for brands

The change is in who reads the listing first. When a shopper asks Rufus whether a jacket is machine washable or a drill is easy to hold, Rufus looks for the answer in the listing, the reviews and the answered questions. If the information is missing or unclear, the answer may be vague, wrong, or drawn from a reviewer’s complaint.

That raises the value of complete, specific product information. Facts that a shopper might ask about, such as materials, sizes, compatibility and care, should be stated plainly. Answered questions become more useful, since Rufus can draw on them. And recurring complaints in reviews are more likely to be repeated to shoppers who ask.

The rollout is gradual, so most shoppers will not see Rufus immediately. But brands have time now to prepare before it reaches more of their customers.

What to do now

  1. Review key listings for the facts shoppers ask about, and state them plainly in the title, bullets and description.
  2. Check the customer questions on key products, and make sure common ones have clear, accurate answers.
  3. Read recent reviews for recurring complaints, and fix the product or listing issues behind them.

We will publish an analysis next week of what Rufus reads on a listing and how brands should respond.

A0531.title: Walmart agrees to acquire Vizio
A0531.alt: A blue shopping basket of bread, apples, milk, and a bottle on a yellow stool against a bright blue wall.
A0531.ttag: Walmart agrees to acquire Vizio | Kwontified
A0531.desc: Walmart agreed on February 20 to acquire TV maker Vizio for about $2.3 billion, to grow its advertising business, Walmart Connect, through Vizio’s…
A0531.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 21, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0531.body:
Walmart agreed on February 20 to acquire TV maker Vizio for about $2.3 billion, to grow its advertising business, Walmart Connect, through Vizio’s SmartCast television operating system. The deal would give Walmart a way to place ads on home TV screens and link them to what shoppers buy at Walmart. Brands advertising with Walmart should expect TV placements tied to Walmart’s shopper data, and should plan to test them the way they would test any new channel.

What happened

Walmart and Vizio announced an agreement for Walmart to acquire Vizio for $11.50 per share in cash, a fully diluted equity value of about $2.3 billion, according to Walmart on February 20.

Walmart said Vizio’s platform has more than 500 direct advertiser relationships, and that Vizio’s Platform+ business, which consists largely of advertising, accounts for a majority of Vizio’s gross profit. Walmart also said Walmart Connect grew 30% in its fiscal year 2024. The deal is subject to regulatory clearance and other closing conditions.

Why it matters for brands

The deal is about advertising, not televisions. Walmart already knows what millions of shoppers buy in its stores and online. Vizio’s operating system gives it a screen in many of those shoppers’ homes. Together, they would let Walmart show ads on TV and then measure whether the people who saw them bought the product at Walmart.

That follows a path Amazon has taken with Prime Video and its streaming devices. Retailers with large shopper data sets are adding their own video screens, so they can sell advertising across the full journey, from the living room to the checkout.

For brands, this means more connected TV options sold by retailers, with measurement tied to sales. It also means more places to spend, and more reporting that credits the retailer’s own media. Brands will need to judge these placements on whether they add sales, not only on what the retailer’s reports attribute to them.

What to do now

  1. Expect Walmart Connect to add TV placements over time, and plan budget for a test once they are available.
  2. Ask how Walmart will measure TV results against sales, and insist on comparisons with a control group.
  3. Keep Walmart and Amazon video plans separate, since each retailer will measure against its own sales.

We will cover what the Vizio deal means for Walmart Connect advertisers as details emerge.

A0536.crumb: Amazon announces its first Big Spring…
A0536.title: Amazon announces its first Big Spring Sale, March 20 to 25
A0536.alt: A taped cardboard box on a metal garden table beside a watering can and a tray of seedlings by a mint-green wall.
A0536.ttag: Amazon announces its first Big Spring Sale, March 20 to 25 | Kwontified
A0536.desc: Amazon announced on March 14 its first Big Spring Sale, a six-day event from March 20 to March 25 that is open to all shoppers, not only Prime members.
A0536.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 15, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0536.body:
Amazon announced on March 14 its first Big Spring Sale, a six-day event from March 20 to March 25 that is open to all shoppers, not only Prime members. That gives Amazon a third major sale in the year, in a season that had none, and a longer one than Prime Day. Brands in seasonal categories should confirm their deals and stock now, and plan advertising for a week of higher click prices and broader traffic.

What happened

The sale will begin at midnight Pacific time on March 20 and run through March 25, Fortune reported on March 14. It will feature deals on seasonal items from fashion to lawn and garden goods.

Amazon said shoppers could expect up to 50% off select beauty products and select sports and outdoor equipment, and up to 40% off select home products and spring apparel, HomePage News reported the same day.

Unlike Prime Day, the sale is not limited to Prime members, so anyone can take advantage of the deals, NBC News reported.

Why it matters for brands

The event adds a planned peak to a quiet part of the year. Open access matters most. Because shoppers do not need Prime to take part, the sale can reach people who never shop Prime Day, which may widen its traffic but also its competition.

The length matters too. Six days is three times as long as Prime Day’s two. A longer event spreads demand out, which can ease stock pressure but stretches advertising budgets across more days of elevated click prices.

Categories matter most of all. Brands in beauty, outdoor, home and spring fashion are where Amazon is focusing, and where traffic and competition are likely to be highest. Brands outside those categories may see higher costs without the same lift.

What to do now

  1. Confirm deals and stock for products in the featured categories, and protect top sellers from stockouts.
  2. Set a spending cap for the six days, tied to advertising cost of sales, and raise bids gradually into the event.
  3. Measure the full period, including the week before and after, against a normal week to see what the event added.

We published a forecasting method for the sale on March 12, and will report on results after the event.

A0551.alt: Metal and wood shelving of amber, green, white and black bottles with blank labels and kraft boxes against a blue wall
A0551.ttag: Walmart Connect sets 2024 plans: auction display, self-serve access, new advertisers | Kwontified
A0551.desc: Walmart said on April 1 that it is making onsite display advertising primarily programmatic and auction-based, opening it to brands of all sizes in April…
A0551.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 2, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0551.body:
Walmart said on April 1 that it is making onsite display advertising primarily programmatic and auction-based, opening it to brands of all sizes in April 2024, and supporting advertisers that do not sell through Walmart. That brings more advertisers into the same placements and lets prices move with demand. Brands advertising on Walmart should expect more competition for display, and should set bids and budgets on what each placement returns rather than on fixed rates.

What happened

Walmart described its 2024 plans for Walmart Connect, its advertising business, in a post on April 1, according to Walmart.

Walmart said its onsite display advertising is becoming primarily programmatic and auction-based, with greater access and control, and that it will be available to brands of all sizes starting in April. It also said it would support non-endemic brands, meaning advertisers that do not sell products through Walmart.

Walmart said marketplace sellers are now its fastest-growing advertisers, with their Sponsored Search spending growing 63% in 2023 and doubling on its self-serve platform. It also described more self-serve tools, including expanded Brand Shop capabilities with video and new templates.

Why it matters for brands

The shift to auctions changes how display is priced. Under fixed rates, a brand paid a set price for a placement. Under an auction, the price depends on how many advertisers want the same shoppers at the same time. That can lower costs when demand is light and raise them sharply in busy periods.

Opening display to brands of all sizes, and to advertisers that do not sell at Walmart, adds more bidders. Smaller brands and marketplace sellers gain access to placements that were harder to reach. Larger brands that relied on display may find more competition for the same inventory.

The growth in marketplace seller advertising points the same way. As more sellers advertise, competition rises across Walmart’s ad products, not only display.

What to do now

  1. Test Walmart’s auction-based display with a defined budget and a clear goal before scaling it.
  2. Set bids by what each placement returns, and watch costs closely during busy periods.
  3. Review Walmart search and display budgets together, since more advertisers will compete across both.

We will publish an analysis next week of when display makes sense on Walmart.

A0562.crumb: US law requires TikTok’s divestiture or a…
A0562.title: US law requires TikTok’s divestiture or a ban
A0562.alt: A ring light with a phone clamp stands beside a wooden stool holding amber skincare bottles against a teal wall.
A0562.ttag: US law requires TikTok’s divestiture or a ban | Kwontified
A0562.desc: President Biden signed a law on April 24 that requires ByteDance to sell TikTok’s US business or see the app banned in the United States, starting a…
A0562.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 25, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0562.body:
President Biden signed a law on April 24 that requires ByteDance to sell TikTok’s US business or see the app banned in the United States, starting a 270-day clock that can be extended by 90 days. TikTok has said it will challenge the law in court, so nothing changes for shoppers yet. Brands selling through TikTok Shop or relying on TikTok for discovery should keep operating, but build a contingency plan that moves audiences and content to channels they control.

What happened

President Biden signed legislation on April 24 requiring ByteDance, TikTok’s China-based parent company, to sell the app or face a US ban, SiliconANGLE reported the same day. The law allows the deadline to be extended by 90 days if there is evidence of significant progress toward a sale, and TikTok said it would challenge the law in court, the report said.

The House passed the measure 360 to 58 on April 20 and the Senate passed it 79 to 18, and the signing starts a 270-day countdown to a sale or a prohibition, according to Techmeme’s summary of coverage on April 24.

Why it matters for brands

The law creates a long period of uncertainty rather than an immediate change. The app and TikTok Shop continue to operate while the deadline runs and any court challenge proceeds. Shoppers can still discover and buy products there.

But the risk is now on a timetable. A brand that depends on TikTok for discovery or sales faces a real possibility of losing that channel. The deadline falls in early 2025, and an extension could push it further, so the outcome may not be known until well after the 2024 holiday season.

Brands with the most at stake are those whose growth came mainly through TikTok: products that went viral there, creators who drive their sales, and TikTok Shop listings that account for a large share of revenue.

What to do now

  1. Keep running TikTok and TikTok Shop, but measure how much of your sales and new customers depend on them.
  2. Repurpose TikTok content to Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, and invite TikTok followers to email lists and other owned channels.
  3. Make sure products that gained demand on TikTok are well listed and stocked on Amazon, Walmart and your own site, where shoppers may search for them.

We will publish a fuller planning guide for TikTok Shop sellers in the coming days.

A0588.title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2024 for July 16 and 17
A0588.alt: Stacked cardboard boxes topped with a striped towel beside potted red geraniums on a stone step by a blue wall.
A0588.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Day 2024 for July 16 and 17 | Kwontified
A0588.desc: Amazon said on June 25 that its tenth Prime Day will run for 48 hours on July 16 and 17, a few days later in July than the 2023 event.
A0588.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 26, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0588.body:
Amazon said on June 25 that its tenth Prime Day will run for 48 hours on July 16 and 17, a few days later in July than the 2023 event. The date confirms the window brands have been planning toward and leaves three weeks to finish preparations. Brands should lock their event budgets and bids now, check that stock reached Amazon by the June 20 cutoff, and plan for early deals in the days before the event.

What happened

Amazon announced on Tuesday, June 25, that it would hold its annual Prime Day event, the tenth in its history, on July 16 and 17, MarketScreener reported. The event begins at 12:01 a.m. Pacific time on July 16, VCPost reported the same day.

The 48-hour sale is open to Prime members and will run in more than 20 countries, NBC News reported. Prime Day 2023 was held on July 11 and 12, and the 2022 event on July 12 and 13, the report noted.

Why it matters for brands

The announcement mostly confirms what planners expected. Amazon’s deal deadlines passed in April and May, and its inventory cutoff for sellers was June 20, so most of a brand’s deals and stock for the event are already set.

What the dates add is a firm timetable for the decisions still open. Advertising budgets, bids, coupons and the timing of early promotions can now be planned to the day. The event also falls a few days later than in 2023, which matters for brands comparing results with the July 2023 event and for those whose replenishment cycles or stock arrivals were planned around mid-July.

The three weeks before the event will bring early deals, which can pull some demand forward. Brands should expect a smaller lift in those weeks than during the event itself.

What to do now

  1. Set event budgets and raise bids on your best-converting searches ahead of July 16, expecting higher click prices during the 48 hours.
  2. Confirm that event stock arrived at Amazon by the June 20 cutoff, and trim budgets on products where stock is short.
  3. Compare results with the July 11 to 12, 2023 event by day of the event, not by calendar date.

Our Prime Day 2024 forecast, published June 25, sets out ranges for sales, click prices and deal share that brands can plan against.

A0600.title: Early read: Prime Day 2024 drew $14.2 billion online, preliminary data shows
A0600.alt: Red hand cart stacked with taped cardboard shipping boxes against a weathered blue wall.
A0600.ttag: Early read: Prime Day 2024 drew $14.2 billion online, preliminary data shows | Kwontified
A0600.desc: US shoppers spent $14.2 billion online across all retailers during Prime Day 2024, up 11% from 2023, according to Adobe Analytics, and Amazon said it was…
A0600.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 19, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0600.body:
US shoppers spent $14.2 billion online across all retailers during Prime Day 2024, up 11% from 2023, according to Adobe Analytics, and Amazon said it was its biggest Prime Day ever. These are early, market-wide figures, not brand results, and the full picture will take weeks. Brands should compare their own event results with the weeks before and after, not with headline growth.

What happened

US online spending across retailers reached $14.2 billion over July 16 and 17, up 11% from a year earlier, with $7.2 billion on the first day and $7 billion on the second, Adobe reported on July 18. Back-to-school spending helped drive the total, and online prices were down 4.2% from a year earlier in June, Adobe said.

Amazon said Prime Day 2024 set records for sales and items sold, and that millions of customers joined Prime in the three weeks before the event, though it did not disclose sales figures, the Associated Press reported on July 18.

Not every measure rose. The average household spent about $152 on Amazon during the event, down slightly from 2023, according to Numerator data cited by Transport Topics.

Why it matters for brands

These figures are preliminary and market-wide. Adobe’s number covers online spending across all US retailers, not Amazon alone, and it is not adjusted for inflation, though Adobe said online prices were falling.

The headline growth came in slightly above the range we published on June 25, which put the reach case at about $14 billion, or 10% growth. We will grade that forecast in full once more data is available.

For individual brands, the headline says little. A brand’s result depends on its category, its deals and how much of its event volume was pulled forward from the weeks after. Lower spending per household alongside record items sold suggests many shoppers bought cheaper items or deeper deals.

What to do now

  1. Compare event sales and margin with a normal baseline, not with the market’s 11% growth.
  2. Track sales for the next three to four weeks to see how much demand the event pulled forward.
  3. Review click prices and conversion by day, to see whether the reserve rules in your plan held up.

Our full Prime Day 2024 review, grading the forecast against results, will follow by the end of July.

A0602.title: Google drops its plan to remove third-party cookies from Chrome
A0602.alt: Five colorful mailboxes on a lilac wall above a string-tied brown paper parcel on the sidewalk.
A0602.ttag: Google drops its plan to remove third-party cookies from Chrome | Kwontified
A0602.desc: Google said on July 22 that it will no longer phase out third-party cookies in its Chrome browser, and will instead offer users a choice about tracking.
A0602.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 23, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0602.body:
Google said on July 22 that it will no longer phase out third-party cookies in its Chrome browser, and will instead offer users a choice about tracking. The change ends a plan delayed several times since 2020, but details of the new choice remain unclear. Brands should keep investing in first-party data and retail media audiences rather than assuming the old cookie-based targeting will return to full strength.

What happened

Google scrapped its plan to end Chrome’s support for third-party cookies, and said it would instead introduce a new experience in Chrome that lets people make an informed choice about tracking across their web browsing, SiliconANGLE reported on July 22. Some Privacy Sandbox technologies will still become available, the report said.

The reversal ends a long saga of preparation, delays and criticism from the industry and regulators, and details on how the user choice will work were sparse, The Current reported the same day. Google had delayed the phaseout for a third time in April after criticism from UK regulators, eMarketer noted.

Why it matters for brands

The decision reduces pressure on advertisers in the short term. Cookie-based targeting and measurement on the open web will keep working in Chrome for users who allow it, rather than disappearing on a fixed date.

But it does not restore the old world. Other browsers already limit third-party cookies, and if Chrome users are offered a clear choice, many may decline tracking. Signal loss is likely to continue, just more gradually.

For brands selling on marketplaces, the main implication is about data. Retail media networks run on retailers’ own first-party data, which never depended on third-party cookies. That advantage remains, and the decision gives no reason to pull back from retail media audiences or from building a brand’s own customer data.

What to do now

  1. Keep building first-party data, such as email lists and customer accounts, regardless of Chrome’s cookie policy.
  2. Continue testing retail media audiences and measurement that do not rely on third-party cookies.
  3. Watch for details of Chrome’s user choice, since the share of users who opt out will decide how much tracking really changes.

We will publish a longer view on what the decision means for retail media in the coming days.

A0627.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0627.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Big Deal Days 2024 for October 8 and 9 | Kwontified
A0627.desc: Amazon said on September 17 that its Prime Big Deal Days event will run on October 8 and 9, its third October event for Prime members.
A0627.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 18, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0627.body:
Amazon said on September 17 that its Prime Big Deal Days event will run on October 8 and 9, its third October event for Prime members. Target has already scheduled a rival event for the same week. Brands that submitted deals and shipped inventory weeks ago are now set; the remaining decisions are advertising budgets, coupons and how to handle the weeks around the event.

What happened

Amazon will hold its third annual Prime Big Deal Days on October 8 and 9, offering early holiday deals to Prime members, EcommerceBytes reported on September 17. Sellers using Fulfillment by Amazon had until September 13 to get inventory to fulfillment centers in order to take part, the report said. The event will run in Turkey for the first time.

The 48-hour event will take place in 19 countries, with new deals appearing as often as every five minutes during select periods, RetailWire reported the same day.

Amazon also promoted the event as a time to stock up on everyday needs such as batteries, home storage and pet care. Target had already announced its own member event, Target Circle Week, for October 6 to 12, Home Page News reported.

Why it matters for brands

The dates confirm what the deadlines implied. With deal submissions closed in August and the inventory cutoff past, most of the event’s structure is already fixed for each brand. What remains open is how much to spend on advertising and how to manage stock and pricing before and after.

Two features of the 2024 event deserve attention. Amazon’s emphasis on everyday essentials means stock-up buying is likely again, which pulls sales forward from the following weeks for staples. And Target’s overlapping Circle Week means shoppers will compare prices across retailers during the same days.

The event also lands before a shorter holiday season. Thanksgiving falls on November 28 in 2024, so October is an early opportunity to reach gift shoppers.

What to do now

  1. Set advertising budgets for October 8 and 9, keeping a reserve for the hours that run hottest.
  2. Check that prices and deals are consistent across Amazon and Target for the overlapping days.
  3. Plan to measure the event over several weeks, especially for everyday staples where stocking up borrows from later sales.

We will review the results after the event and what they suggest for Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

A0631.title: Amazon Accelerate 2024: the announcements that matter for brands
A0631.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0631.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2024: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0631.desc: Amazon used its Accelerate conference in Seattle on September 19 to put generative AI at the center of selling.
A0631.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 20, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0631.body:
Amazon used its Accelerate conference in Seattle on September 19 to put generative AI at the center of selling. It launched a test version of an AI assistant for sellers, a tool that turns product images into video ads and bulk AI writing for product listings. For brands, the tools lower the cost of content and analysis but make accuracy and review more important.

What happened

Amazon announced a beta of Project Amelia, an AI-powered selling assistant inside Seller Central that answers questions and offers guidance using knowledge of Amazon and of the seller’s own business, GeekWire reported on September 19. In a demonstration, Amelia gave personalized advice, such as how a brand should prepare for the holiday peak, Modern Retail reported the same day.

Amazon also introduced Video Generator, a tool that turns a still product image into a video advertisement, Modern Retail reported. And Amazon said sellers will be able to use AI to write product listings in bulk based on their entire catalog, CNBC reported.

Why it matters for brands

Video has been expensive, so many smaller brands skipped it. A tool that creates video from existing images lowers that barrier and is likely to put more video ads into search results. Brands already using video will face more competition for attention.

AI listings raise the stakes on accuracy. Writing listings in bulk saves time, but errors spread just as quickly. As we wrote in July, review is what makes AI content pay: a human check on claims, sizes and compatibility protects against returns and lost trust.

Project Amelia could shorten the time it takes to diagnose problems and plan events. But it is a beta, and its advice reflects Amazon’s view of the seller’s business. Brands should treat it as one input alongside their own data.

The announcements fit a pattern: AI for shoppers through Rufus, and now for sellers. Brands with accurate, complete listings will be better placed as more buying and selling runs through AI.

What to do now

  1. Test Video Generator on a few products with strong images, and compare the results with existing ads before rolling out widely.
  2. Set a review process for any AI-written listings, checking claims, sizes and compatibility before publishing.
  3. Use Project Amelia, where available, to speed up routine questions, but confirm important decisions against your own data.

We will cover what these tools change for sellers next week.

A0641.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.

A0641.desc: Amazon said on October 10 that Prime Big Deal Days was its biggest October shopping event ever.
A0641.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 11, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0641.body:
Amazon said on October 10 that Prime Big Deal Days was its biggest October shopping event ever. It gave no sales total, and early third-party data covers only parts of the market. Treat this read as preliminary: the useful test for brands is their own sales over the coming weeks, not Amazon’s headline.

What happened

Amazon said the October 8 and 9 event was its largest October shopping event, with more Prime members shopping than in 2023, and that independent sellers had record sales compared with the 2023 event, RTTNews reported on October 10. A record number of customers signed up for Prime in the three weeks before the event, Amazon said.

Early data from sellers was strong but partial. Clients of the agency Momentum Commerce grew sales 41% from a year earlier on the first day, and Salesforce data showed online orders up 23% in food and beverage and 21% in health and beauty, Digital Commerce 360 reported on October 9.

Why it matters for brands

A record without a number is hard to judge. Amazon did not say how much shoppers spent, and agency figures reflect their own clients, not the whole market. Brands should not assume their results match the headline.

The categories that grew fastest early, food and beverage and health and beauty, are full of products shoppers stock up on. Strong event sales in those categories often mean softer sales in the weeks after, which is why the event should be judged over a longer period.

Our forecast for the event expected a sales lift of about 1.5 to 2.5 times normal on promoted products. Brands can compare their own results with that range now, and should compare again in four to six weeks.

What to do now

  1. Compare event-day sales and click prices on promoted products with a normal week, against the forecast ranges.
  2. Track sales for staples over the next four to six weeks to measure any dip from stocking up.
  3. Carry lessons on deal depth and budget into Black Friday and Cyber Monday plans now.

We will publish a full grading of the event against our forecast once the weeks after it are in.

A0645.title: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2024: the announcements that matter for brands
A0645.alt: A spotlight on a stand aimed at a plain white box on a white plinth against a navy blue wall.
A0645.ttag: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2024: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0645.desc: Amazon Ads used unBoxed in Austin on October 15 to push AI creative tools, a rebuilt Amazon DSP and new measurement.
A0645.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 17, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0645.body:
Amazon Ads used unBoxed in Austin on October 15 to push AI creative tools, a rebuilt Amazon DSP and new measurement. For brands, the creative tools lower production costs now, while the measurement changes, including multi-touch attribution, matter most for how budgets are judged in 2025.

What happened

Amazon Ads introduced AI creative studio and Audio generator, self-service tools that bring its AI image and video generation into one place and add audio, according to an Amazon announcement on October 15. Brands that used its image generator between October 2023 and June 2024 saw almost 5% more sales per advertiser on average, Amazon said, Reuters reported.

Amazon also announced new measurement and launch services. It will begin testing multi-touch attribution later in 2024, with full rollout planned for 2025, and introduced a managed full-funnel service for new product launches, PPC Land and Swipe Insight reported. Separately, it unveiled a rebuilt Amazon DSP experience for buying ads across Amazon’s sites and partners.

Why it matters for brands

Creative is getting cheaper. Tools that turn a product image into display, video and audio ads lower the cost of testing new creative. Brands should expect more creative in auctions, and more pressure to refresh their own.

Measurement may change what looks profitable. Multi-touch attribution credits ads that appear earlier in the path to purchase, not just the last one. When it arrives, upper-funnel campaigns such as streaming and display may look stronger than they do under last-click reporting. Brands should compare the new numbers with their own tests rather than accepting either view alone.

The direction is clear. Amazon wants advertisers spending across the whole funnel, measured by Amazon. That makes independent testing more valuable, not less.

What to do now

  1. Test AI creative studio on a few products and compare results with existing creative.
  2. Plan how you will compare multi-touch results with your own holdout tests in 2025.
  3. Review whether upper-funnel campaigns deserve a test budget in the first quarter.

We will cover what the measurement changes mean for 2025 budgets in a coming post.

A0655.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
A0655.ttag: Amazon sets Black Friday Week for November 21 to December 2 | Kwontified
A0655.desc: Amazon will run its Black Friday Week from November 21 to 29 and its Cyber Monday event from November 29 to December 2, a 12-day stretch.
A0655.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 14, 2024. 1-minute read.
A0655.body:
Amazon will run its Black Friday Week from November 21 to 29 and its Cyber Monday event from November 29 to December 2, a 12-day stretch. With Thanksgiving on November 28, the shortest gap to Christmas in years leaves brands less time after the event to recover, so stock and budgets should be set for the whole period now.

What happened

Amazon announced its Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday deal events, starting November 21 at 12:01 a.m. Pacific time and running through December 2, according to the company’s release on Business Wire. New in 2024, Amazon said it would launch themed daily deal drops, and promoted its Rufus shopping assistant and AI shopping guides for gift shoppers.

Amazon also said more than 60% of sales in its store come from independent sellers, according to the same release. In 2023, Amazon’s Black Friday event ran 11 days, from November 17 to 27, Home Page News reported at the time.

Why it matters for brands

The event is longer, but the season is shorter. There are 27 days from Thanksgiving to Christmas in 2024, five fewer than in 2023. Brands have less time after Cyber Monday to sell through remaining holiday stock or recover from a slow event.

Daily deal drops spread traffic across the event. Shoppers are encouraged to return each day, so visibility on any single day matters less than staying present for all 12.

AI shopping tools change how gift shoppers find products. Listings with clear answers to common gift questions are more likely to be surfaced by Rufus and the shopping guides.

What to do now

  1. Plan budgets and stock for all 12 days, with reserves for the final Cyber Monday weekend.
  2. Make sure listings answer gift questions clearly, for AI tools and shoppers alike.
  3. Plan for the short gap to Christmas: set post-event promotions and delivery cutoffs now.

We will publish our forecast ranges for the event shortly.

A0657.title: Amazon launches Haul, a low-price storefront to take on Temu
A0657.alt: Gray plastic crate overflowing with orange poly mailer bags against a sunlit orange wall.
A0657.ttag: Amazon launches Haul, a low-price storefront to take on Temu | Kwontified
A0657.desc: Amazon has launched Haul, a storefront of products priced at $20 or less with delivery in one to two weeks, aimed at shoppers drawn to Temu and Shein.
A0657.kicker: News. Creative and conversion. Multiple channels
A0657.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 14, 2024. 1-minute read.
A0657.body:
Amazon has launched Haul, a storefront of products priced at $20 or less with delivery in one to two weeks, aimed at shoppers drawn to Temu and Shein. For brands, Haul adds low-price competition inside Amazon itself, so products sold mainly on price face new pressure while brands that compete on quality and speed should make those advantages visible.

What happened

Amazon launched Haul in a beta version for shoppers using its smartphone app or mobile browsers, Bloomberg reported on November 13. Items are priced at $20 or less, focused on clothing, home goods, jewelry and electronics.

Purchases are delivered in one to two weeks, and Amazon charges a $3.99 shipping fee that is waived on orders over $25, according to the same report. Amazon had first described plans for a discount storefront of unbranded items shipped from China in June.

Why it matters for brands

Low-price competition now sits inside Amazon. Shoppers who might have left for Temu can stay in Amazon’s app, which keeps their spending within reach of Amazon’s search and advertising. But it also puts ultra-low-price alternatives a few taps away from branded products.

The trade-off is speed. Haul’s one-to-two-week delivery contrasts with Prime’s fast delivery. Brands that compete on quality, reliability and quick delivery have a clear difference to show.

Price-led products face the most pressure. Simple, low-cost items such as phone cases, socks and basic home goods are exactly what Haul targets. Brands selling similar products on price alone should expect more competition.

What to do now

  1. Identify products that compete mainly on price, and check whether Haul alternatives appear for their key searches.
  2. Make quality, reviews and fast delivery prominent in listings for those products.
  3. Avoid matching ultra-low prices on products where the brand’s advantages justify a higher price.

We covered Amazon’s push for low prices and its costs for brands in an October post, and will track how Haul develops.

A0666.title: Early read: Cyber Week 2024 online sales rose 8%, led by Black Friday
A0666.alt: Blue, red and orange paper shopping bags lined up on a weathered wooden bench against a sunlit cream wall.
A0666.ttag: Early read: Cyber Week 2024 online sales rose 8%, led by Black Friday | Kwontified
A0666.desc: US online spending over Cyber Week 2024 rose 8.2% to $41.1 billion, according to Adobe, with growth strongest on Thanksgiving and Black Friday rather than…
A0666.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 4, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0666.body:
US online spending over Cyber Week 2024 rose 8.2% to $41.1 billion, according to Adobe, with growth strongest on Thanksgiving and Black Friday rather than Cyber Monday. These are preliminary figures from public sources. For brands, the early read suggests shoppers bought sooner when deals were good, so the days before Cyber Monday mattered more than in past years.

What happened

Shoppers spent $41.1 billion online in the United States across Cyber Week, the five days from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, up 8.2% from 2023, Adobe reported on December 3. That was above Adobe’s September forecast of $40.6 billion.

Cyber Monday remained the biggest day, at $13.3 billion, up 7.3%. Black Friday brought in $10.8 billion, up 10.2%, and Thanksgiving $6.1 billion, up 8.8%. Adobe’s lead analyst said growth was stronger on Thanksgiving and Black Friday than on Cyber Monday, as early discounts persuaded many shoppers to buy sooner.

Another data provider saw slower growth. Salesforce put US Cyber Week spending at $76 billion, up 7%, and US Cyber Monday spending at $12.8 billion, up 2%, TechCrunch reported on December 3. The two firms measure differently, so their totals are not directly comparable.

Why it matters for brands

Shoppers moved earlier. Stronger growth on Thanksgiving and Black Friday means the days before Cyber Monday carried more of the event. Brands that held budget or stock for Monday may have missed demand that came sooner.

The total landed within the range we set in our November 15 forecast. A full comparison of results against that forecast, including click prices and the share of sales sold on deals, will follow once brands’ own data is in.

Public totals are not a brand’s result. Category, stock and advertising decisions all shape individual outcomes, so brands should compare their own numbers with 2023 before drawing conclusions.

What to do now

  1. Compare your Thanksgiving-to-Cyber-Monday sales by day with 2023 to see whether your demand also moved earlier.
  2. Separate sales made at deal prices from full-price sales, and check click prices against your plan.
  3. Plan the rest of December using the strongest products from Cyber Week, while stock remains.

We will publish a full read of Cyber Week once brands’ results are in.

A0667.title: Walmart completes its Vizio acquisition to grow TV advertising
A0667.alt: Metal and wood shelving of amber, green, white and black bottles with blank labels and kraft boxes against a blue wall
A0667.ttag: Walmart completes its Vizio acquisition to grow TV advertising | Kwontified
A0667.desc: Walmart has completed its roughly $2.3 billion acquisition of TV maker Vizio, adding Vizio’s TV operating system and advertising business to Walmart…
A0667.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 4, 2024. 2-minute read.
A0667.body:
Walmart has completed its roughly $2.3 billion acquisition of TV maker Vizio, adding Vizio’s TV operating system and advertising business to Walmart Connect, its advertising arm. For brands, it means Walmart can offer ads on Vizio TVs linked to its own shopper data. Brands advertising with Walmart should expect TV options to appear in Walmart Connect plans and should ask how those ads will be measured against sales.

What happened

Walmart announced on December 3 that it had completed its acquisition of Vizio, according to its press release. Walmart agreed on February 20, 2024 to buy Vizio for $11.50 per share in cash, equal to about $2.3 billion.

Walmart said the deal will bring new ways for advertisers to reach customers through Walmart Connect. Vizio’s advertising business accounts for all of Vizio’s gross profit, and Walmart Connect grew 26% in the third quarter, according to the release. The two companies will operate separately for the foreseeable future.

Why it matters for brands

Walmart now owns a place on the television screen. Ads on Vizio TVs reach households while they watch, and Walmart can connect that audience to its own records of what shoppers buy. That combination could let brands see whether a TV ad led to purchases at Walmart.

It extends Walmart Connect beyond Walmart’s own sites and stores. Brands that advertise with Walmart Connect today should expect TV placements to become part of the options offered to them.

The details will take time. With the two companies operating separately for now, the products and measurement that combine Vizio’s audience with Walmart’s data have not yet been described.

What to do now

  1. If you advertise with Walmart Connect, ask your contact when Vizio TV placements will be available and how they will be measured.
  2. Before buying TV ads through Walmart, agree how sales will be measured, ideally against a group that did not see the ads.
  3. Watch for TV advertising to compete with your existing Walmart budget, and set a separate test budget rather than moving spend from proven campaigns.

We will cover how the combined offer develops as Walmart shares more detail.

A0688.title: TikTok briefly goes dark in the US at the ban deadline
A0688.alt: A ring light with a phone clamp stands beside a wooden stool holding amber skincare bottles against a teal wall.
A0688.ttag: TikTok briefly goes dark in the US at the ban deadline | Kwontified
A0688.desc: TikTok shut down for US users late on Saturday, January 18, ahead of the federal sale-or-ban deadline, then restored service on Sunday after…
A0688.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jan 21, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0688.body:
TikTok shut down for US users late on Saturday, January 18, ahead of the federal sale-or-ban deadline, then restored service on Sunday after President-elect Trump promised to delay enforcement. On January 20, President Trump signed an executive order pausing enforcement for 75 days. For brands, the outage showed how quickly a channel can disappear, so they should use the pause to make their TikTok investment portable.

What happened

TikTok went dark on Saturday night, with users who opened the app seeing a message that it was not available because of the law, and restored service on Sunday after Trump said he would issue an executive order to pause the ban, the Boston Globe reported on January 19.

The app was not immediately restored to the Apple and Google app stores, which appeared to be waiting for the executive order, SiliconANGLE reported on January 19.

On January 20, President Trump signed an executive order instructing the attorney general not to take any action to enforce the law for 75 days, TechCrunch reported that day. The order also said companies that work with TikTok during the pause will not be held liable, NPR reported. A 75-day pause from January 20 runs to April 5.

Why it matters for brands

The outage was short, but it was real. For about a day, brands selling through TikTok Shop and creators promoting their products lost the channel entirely. A longer outage would cut off sales, content and customer relationships built on the app.

The pause is temporary. The law remains in place, and the executive order delays enforcement rather than removing the requirement for a sale. Brands should treat the next 75 days as time to prepare, not as a resolution.

What to do now

  1. Secure rights to reuse your best TikTok creator videos on Instagram, YouTube and marketplace listings.
  2. Invite TikTok Shop buyers to follow you on other channels or sign up for email, so you can reach them if the app goes dark again.
  3. Keep TikTok Shop stock and spending at levels you could absorb losing, and review the plan before April 5.

We will follow the 75-day pause and what it means for brands selling on TikTok.

A0705.title: Amazon announces Alexa+, an assistant that shops and books
A0705.alt: A gray fabric smart speaker beside a bowl of lemons and a notepad on a sunlit wooden table against a sage wall.
A0705.ttag: Amazon announces Alexa+, an assistant that shops and books | Kwontified
A0705.desc: Amazon announced Alexa+ on February 26, a generative AI version of its assistant that can order groceries, book services and complete tasks across other…
A0705.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 27, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0705.body:
Amazon announced Alexa+ on February 26, a generative AI version of its assistant that can order groceries, book services and complete tasks across other companies’ apps. It will be free for Prime members and roll out from March. For brands, it is an early sign that more shopping will start with a spoken request to an assistant rather than a search, so product information needs to be ready for assistants to read.

What happened

Amazon executives demonstrated Alexa+ ordering groceries from Amazon Fresh and carrying out tasks in other services, including booking Uber trips, finding concert tickets through Ticketmaster and making dinner reservations, SiliconANGLE reported on February 26, 2025. The service costs $19.99 a month, with the fee waived for Prime members, and will roll out first in the United States.

Early access begins in March, with wider availability in the following months, and the service will work on almost every Alexa device Amazon has shipped, Engadget reported during the event. Alexa+ can take multi-step actions and draws on models available through Amazon Bedrock, eWeek reported the same day.

Why it matters for brands

Alexa+ moves Amazon’s assistant from answering questions to acting on them. When a shopper asks an assistant to reorder a household staple or find a gift, the assistant chooses what to buy. The brand’s product page is no longer the first thing the shopper sees; it is the information the assistant reads.

The rollout is gradual, and many shoppers will keep searching the usual way for some time. But making Alexa+ free for Prime members gives it a large potential audience from the start.

What to do now

  1. Review product titles, descriptions and attributes so an assistant can tell exactly what each product is and who it suits.
  2. Make sure your most reordered products are in stock and eligible for Prime, since an assistant acting for a Prime member is likely to favor them.
  3. Track sales from repeat purchases and voice orders as Alexa+ rolls out, to see whether assistant-driven buying is reaching your category.

We will follow how Alexa+ changes shopping on Amazon as it reaches more customers.

A0708.title: Amazon sets its Big Spring Sale 2025 for March 25 to 31
A0708.alt: A taped cardboard box on a metal garden table beside a watering can and a tray of seedlings by a mint-green wall.
A0708.ttag: Amazon sets its Big Spring Sale 2025 for March 25 to 31 | Kwontified
A0708.desc: Amazon announced on March 18 that its Big Spring Sale will run for seven days, from March 25 to March 31, open to all shoppers with extra deals for Prime…
A0708.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 19, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0708.body:
Amazon announced on March 18 that its Big Spring Sale will run for seven days, from March 25 to March 31, open to all shoppers with extra deals for Prime members. For brands, the confirmed dates leave one week to finish deal, stock and advertising plans, and our forecast still points to a modest lift that does not justify Prime Day budgets.

What happened

The sale will begin on Tuesday, March 25 and run through Monday, March 31, and anyone can shop it, not only Prime members, 9to5toys reported on March 18, 2025.

Shoppers will find deals across more than 35 categories, and for the first time Amazon is also running a Big Spring Haul event with 50% off purchases on Haul, its storefront for items priced at $20 or less, RetailWire reported on March 18.

Why it matters for brands

The event is longer than a Prime event and open to everyone, which spreads shoppers across a full week. In 2024, the first Big Spring Sale lifted sales by about 3% against recent weeks, far below Amazon’s Prime events, and our March 4 forecast put the 2025 lift at 2% to 7%.

The Haul promotion adds pressure at the low end of the market. Brands selling low-priced items in categories where Haul is strong may see more price competition during the week.

What to do now

  1. Confirm deal submissions and stock for the products you plan to promote, and size inventory for a modest lift rather than a Prime Day surge.
  2. Set advertising budgets and bid ceilings for March 25 to 31, pacing spend across the week instead of front-loading it.
  3. Track new-to-brand customers and results against the trailing four weeks, so you can judge what the week added.

We will report on what the Big Spring Sale delivers once results are in.

A0723.crumb: US announces broad new tariffs on imports…
A0723.title: US announces broad new tariffs on imports from nearly every country
A0723.alt: A shrink-wrapped pallet of cardboard boxes beside a yellow pallet jack against a gray wall.
A0723.ttag: US announces broad new tariffs on imports from nearly every country | Kwontified
A0723.desc: President Trump announced on April 2 a 10% tariff on imports from almost all countries starting April 5, with higher rates for about 60 countries starting…
A0723.byline: By Kwontified. Published Apr 3, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0723.body:
President Trump announced on April 2 a 10% tariff on imports from almost all countries starting April 5, with higher rates for about 60 countries starting April 9, including 34% for China, 20% for the European Union and 46% for Vietnam. For brands that import products or materials, landed costs will rise within days, so pricing, stock and sourcing plans need review now.

What happened

The administration announced a baseline 10% tariff on imports from all countries, effective 12:01 a.m. on April 5, 2025, and higher rates for roughly 60 countries effective April 9, Thompson Coburn reported in a trade alert on April 2. Rates named include 34% for China, 20% for the European Union and 46% for Vietnam.

The new tariffs come on top of existing duties unless the order says otherwise, according to the same alert. Goods from China already faced a 20% tariff from March 4, so by our count the combined new tariff on many Chinese goods reaches 54%. The order also says duty-free treatment for low-value parcels will be removed once processes are in place.

Why it matters for brands

The tariffs reach far beyond China. Brands that moved production to Vietnam, other parts of Southeast Asia or elsewhere to reduce tariff exposure now face high rates there too. Few sourcing countries escape the 10% baseline.

Costs will reach different channels in different ways. Brands selling to retailers at fixed cost prices, such as Amazon vendors, absorb increases until they renegotiate. Brands selling directly set their own prices but must decide how much to pass on.

Goods already loaded and in transit before each effective date are not subject to the new tariffs, according to the same alert, which gives brands with stock on the water a short window.

What to do now

  1. Calculate the new landed cost of every imported product by country of origin, using the April 5 and April 9 rates.
  2. Review prices product by product, deciding where to absorb, share or pass on the increase, and plan vendor cost conversations where you sell wholesale.
  3. Check stock levels and inbound shipments, since goods already in transit avoid the new rates and stock bought before the change will protect margin for a time.

We will follow how the tariffs affect marketplace prices and competition in the weeks ahead.

A0736.title: Duty-free treatment ends for low-value goods from China and Hong Kong
A0736.alt: Five colorful mailboxes on a lilac wall above a string-tied brown paper parcel on the sidewalk.
A0736.ttag: Duty-free treatment ends for low-value goods from China and Hong Kong | Kwontified
A0736.desc: From 12:01 a.m. on May 2, goods valued at $800 or less from China and Hong Kong no longer enter the United States duty-free.
A0736.byline: By Kwontified. Published May 2, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0736.body:
From 12:01 a.m. on May 2, goods valued at $800 or less from China and Hong Kong no longer enter the United States duty-free. Parcels sent by mail face a duty of 120% of their value or $100 per item, rising to $200 on June 1. For brands, that removes much of the cost advantage of the cheapest direct-from-China sellers on marketplaces, changing price competition in many categories.

What happened

Beginning at 12:01 a.m. Eastern time on May 2, 2025, goods from China or Hong Kong valued at $800 or less that would otherwise have qualified for duty-free entry are no longer eligible, Barnes Richardson reported on April 24, describing the customs notice implementing the April 2 executive order.

Imports through the international postal network that would have qualified now face either a duty of 120% of the value of the package or a flat $100 per package, which rises to $200 at 12:01 a.m. on June 1, according to the same report.

The duty-free route had been paused once before. The end of duty-free treatment for small parcels from China was first set for early February and then paused to give agencies time to prepare, the AP reported on February 8.

Why it matters for brands

The change hits sellers who ship low-cost goods directly from China to US shoppers, who relied on duty-free entry for very low prices. Paying duties raises their costs sharply.

That changes the competition brands face. In categories crowded with cheap direct-from-China listings, those rivals must either raise prices, slow down or move to stock held in US warehouses, where goods have already been imported and duties paid.

Marketplaces built on direct shipping from China feel it most. About 20% of Temu’s US sales already shipped from local sellers, according to estimates cited by Reuters on February 9, and the new rules push further that way.

What to do now

  1. Watch competitor prices in your categories over the next few weeks, especially on Temu, Amazon Haul and listings that ship from China.
  2. Hold your own prices where cheap rivals become more expensive, rather than discounting into a market that is moving up.
  3. If your own goods ship directly from China to customers, calculate the new duty on each order and decide whether to move stock to US warehouses.

We will follow how marketplaces respond.

A0755.title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2025 for July 8 to 11, its first four-day event
A0755.alt: Stacked cardboard boxes topped with a striped towel beside potted red geraniums on a stone step by a blue wall.
A0755.ttag: Amazon sets Prime Day 2025 for July 8 to 11, its first four-day event | Kwontified
A0755.desc: Amazon has set Prime Day 2025 for July 8 to 11, the first time the event will run four days instead of two.
A0755.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 18, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0755.body:
Amazon has set Prime Day 2025 for July 8 to 11, the first time the event will run four days instead of two. For brands, the confirmed dates fix the deadlines for stock, advertising budgets and deal pacing over a longer event.

What happened

Amazon announced on June 17 that its annual Prime Day sales event will run from July 8 through July 11, expanding to four days from two, Reuters reported that day. An Amazon vice president told Reuters the company was extending the event because members said they needed more time to shop the deals.

The event starts at 12:01 a.m. Pacific time on July 8, and Amazon is introducing “Today’s Big Deals,” themed daily deal drops exclusive to Prime members, RTTNews reported on June 17. Early access to deals from small businesses runs from June 23 through July 6, and independent sellers represent more than 60% of sales in Amazon’s store, according to the same report.

The 2024 event set the benchmark. Shoppers spent $14.2 billion online during the two-day Prime Day in July 2024, up 11%, according to Adobe Analytics figures cited by Chain Store Age.

Why it matters for brands

The dates are now fixed, so the planning window is short. Brands have about three weeks to confirm stock, finalize deals and set advertising budgets.

Four days changes pacing. Stock must last twice as long as in a two-day event, and advertising budgets must be spread across the event rather than spent in a rush.

Themed daily drops can create sharp one-day spikes for featured brands.

The early small-business window starts before the main event. Independent sellers whose deals appear from June 23 face a longer promotional period, and the cost that comes with it.

What to do now

  1. Confirm that stock for your Prime Day products will reach Amazon in time and can cover four days of demand.
  2. Set advertising budgets for each day of the event, with room to shift spending toward the days and products that perform best.
  3. If you are an independent seller, decide whether to take part in the early small-business deals window from June 23, and check the margin cost of a longer deal period.

We will follow how the four-day event performs.

A0768.title: Prime Day 2025 early read: $24.1 billion online, preliminary
A0768.alt: Red hand cart stacked with taped cardboard shipping boxes against a weathered blue wall.
A0768.ttag: Prime Day 2025 early read: $24.1 billion online, preliminary | Kwontified
A0768.desc: US shoppers spent an estimated $24.1 billion online during the four days of Prime Day 2025, up 30.3% from 2024, according to early Adobe figures.
A0768.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jul 14, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0768.body:
US shoppers spent an estimated $24.1 billion online during the four days of Prime Day 2025, up 30.3% from 2024, according to early Adobe figures. Amazon called it its biggest Prime Day ever. These are preliminary public figures, but they show that four days lifted spending well above 2024.

What happened

Online spending across US retailers reached $24.1 billion from July 8 to 11, above Adobe’s own forecast, Reuters reported on July 12. The total was up 30.3% from 2024, according to Adobe data released on Saturday morning, Barron’s reported on July 12. Amazon said the event was its biggest Prime Day ever, but did not disclose a sales figure.

The length matters. The 2024 event ran two days and drew $14.2 billion in US online spending, according to Adobe figures cited by Chain Store Age on June 17. Spread over four days, the 2025 total works out to about $6.0 billion a day, against about $7.1 billion a day in 2024. The total was a record, but spending per day was lower.

Why it matters for brands

The longer event worked for total spending. Four days produced far more than two, though not double the 2024 base.

Lower spending per day suggests shoppers spread purchases across the longer window rather than buying more each day. Brands should check how their own sales spread across the four days.

The figures cover spending across retailers, not Amazon alone, and are preliminary. Brand results will vary widely by category and deal depth.

What to do now

  1. Pull your own four-day results by day and by product, and compare them with your plan and with 2024.
  2. Separate deal sales from full-price sales, and check how much demand came in the days just before and after the event.
  3. Review stock left after the event, and plan how to clear or reallocate it before the next events.

We will publish a fuller assessment once more data is available.

A0789.alt: A brass hanging balance scale tips with a stack of coins on one pan and a twine-tied parcel on the other.
A0789.ttag: De minimis duty-free treatment ends for all countries on August 29 | Kwontified
A0789.desc: Duty-free entry for low-value parcels from every country ends at 12:01 a.m. Eastern on August 29, under an executive order signed July 30.
A0789.byline: By Kwontified. Published Aug 29, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0789.body:
Duty-free entry for low-value parcels from every country ends at 12:01 a.m. Eastern on August 29, under an executive order signed July 30. Shipments valued at $800 or less now owe all applicable duties, with a temporary per-item option for postal parcels. Brands and sellers that rely on direct-to-consumer cross-border shipping face new costs and paperwork from today.

What happened

The order suspends duty-free de minimis treatment for all countries, effective 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on August 29, 2025, Thompson Coburn reported on July 31. A per-item duty option for postal shipments is available from August 29, 2025 to February 28, 2026, after which ad valorem duties apply to all such shipments, according to the same alert.

The postal rates are set by country. Postal packages may pay $80, $160 or $200 per item depending on the country’s tariff rate, or the ad valorem rate, while other shipments valued at $800 or less are subject to all applicable duties, Thompson Hine reported in July 2025.

The volume affected is large. De minimis shipments rose from 134 million in 2015 to more than 1.36 billion in 2024, according to the White House fact sheet cited by Torres Trade Law on August 5.

Why it matters for brands

China and Hong Kong lost duty-free treatment in May. The change now reaches every country, including Canada, Europe and the rest of Asia.

Sellers shipping low-value orders directly to US shoppers lose a cost advantage over sellers who import in bulk and ship from US stock. Brands competing with those sellers may see the price gap narrow.

Shoppers buying from overseas sites may face higher prices, delays or duty charges at delivery.

What to do now

  1. Check every cross-border flow, including samples, replacement parts and direct-to-consumer orders, for de minimis use.
  2. Update landed costs and prices for affected products, and decide whether to move to bulk import and US fulfillment.
  3. Confirm with carriers and brokers how postal and courier shipments will be entered and charged from August 29.

We will report on how sellers adjust in the coming weeks.

A0797.title: Prime Big Deal Days 2025 set for October 7 to 8
A0797.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0797.ttag: Prime Big Deal Days 2025 set for October 7 to 8 | Kwontified
A0797.desc: Amazon announced on September 16 that Prime Big Deal Days will run October 7 to 8, in the US and 17 other countries, including Ireland, Colombia and…
A0797.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 17, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0797.body:
Amazon announced on September 16 that Prime Big Deal Days will run October 7 to 8, in the US and 17 other countries, including Ireland, Colombia and Mexico for the first time. The dates arrived after the September 12 deal submission deadline, so brands’ deal choices are already locked. What remains open is stock, advertising and pricing for the two days.

What happened

Amazon set Prime Big Deal Days for October 7 to 8 and said the event will also run in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Poland, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom and, for the first time, Ireland, Colombia and Mexico, Homepage News reported on September 16, 2025.

The event begins at 12:01 a.m. Pacific Time on October 7, 9to5Toys reported the same day.

Submissions for Best Deals and Lightning Deals had already closed on September 12, EcommerceBytes reported on August 20.

Why it matters for brands

The deadline came before the dates. Brands committed their deals without knowing exactly when the event would run, and those commitments now set the depth and range of their discounts.

The event is three weeks away. That leaves time to adjust advertising budgets, check that stock is in place and set prices for products without deals.

Three new countries widen the event. Brands selling in Mexico, Colombia or Ireland face their first Prime Big Deal Days there and should plan stock and advertising for each.

What to do now

  1. Confirm which deals were accepted and check stock is in place for those products.
  2. Set advertising budgets for October 6 to 9, with extra room on the two event days for deal products.
  3. For brands in Mexico, Colombia or Ireland, plan stock and advertising for each market’s first event.

We will cover what the event shows about deal performance and advertising costs after October 8.

A0801.title: Amazon Accelerate 2025: the announcements that matter for brands
A0801.alt: Empty wooden folding chairs facing a lectern against a coral wall, with a blank lanyard badge hung on one chair.
A0801.ttag: Amazon Accelerate 2025: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0801.desc: Amazon used its Accelerate seller conference in Seattle to give its Seller Assistant agentic AI, end commingling of inventory within FBA and connect its…
A0801.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 19, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0801.body:
Amazon used its Accelerate seller conference in Seattle to give its Seller Assistant agentic AI, end commingling of inventory within FBA and connect its fulfillment network to Walmart, Shopify and SHEIN orders. For brands, the most immediate changes are control over their own inventory, AI tools that can act on their behalf and new ways to fulfill orders from other channels.

What happened

Seller Assistant now has agentic capabilities: it can set goals, develop strategies and, with permission, take action on behalf of sellers, Amazon said in a post on its Selling Partners site on September 18, 2025. The enhanced Seller Assistant is available to all US sellers at no additional cost, and Amazon also introduced AI tools for building ads in Creative Studio, PPC Land reported on September 17.

Amazon will end commingling within FBA. Brand owners will no longer need to apply an FBA sticker to products with a manufacturer barcode, a change Amazon expects to save sellers about $600 million a year, according to its post.

Amazon announced partnerships with Walmart, Shopify and SHEIN through Multi-Channel Fulfillment, which lets businesses use Amazon’s network to deliver orders from other sales channels. Sellers using it reported a sales increase of nearly 19% on average after adding it to off-Amazon channels, Amazon said.

Amazon also introduced Custom Analytics, which combines more than 100 metrics in one free tool, Profit Analytics and shoppable A+ Content, according to the same post.

Why it matters for brands

The end of commingling is the clearest win for brand owners. Products from different sellers will no longer be pooled under one listing in fulfillment centers, which reduces the risk of counterfeit or damaged units reaching a brand’s customers under its name.

Agentic tools change how accounts are run. An assistant that can act with permission needs clear rules on what it may change, especially for pricing, ads and listings.

Fulfillment for Walmart and Shopify orders through Amazon could simplify inventory for brands selling on several channels, but it also deepens reliance on one network.

What to do now

  1. Review FBA inventory labeling and plan the move to manufacturer barcodes as Amazon ends commingling.
  2. Set permissions for Seller Assistant before letting it act, starting with low-risk tasks.
  3. Assess whether Multi-Channel Fulfillment for Walmart or Shopify orders would cut costs or add risk.

We will publish a fuller analysis of what Accelerate changes for sellers next week.

A0805.crumb: OpenAI adds Instant Checkout to ChatGPT…
A0805.title: OpenAI adds Instant Checkout to ChatGPT and opens its commerce protocol
A0805.alt: A white six-wheeled delivery robot with its lid open carries a cardboard parcel on a sidewalk by a lilac wall.
A0805.ttag: OpenAI adds Instant Checkout to ChatGPT and opens its commerce protocol | Kwontified
A0805.desc: OpenAI launched Instant Checkout on September 29, letting US ChatGPT users buy items from Etsy sellers without leaving a conversation, with Shopify…
A0805.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 30, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0805.body:
OpenAI launched Instant Checkout on September 29, letting US ChatGPT users buy items from Etsy sellers without leaving a conversation, with Shopify merchants to follow. It also open-sourced the Agentic Commerce Protocol behind it, built with Stripe, so other merchants can connect. For brands, ChatGPT is becoming a place where products are not only recommended but bought.

What happened

OpenAI launched Instant Checkout for US users with Free, Plus and Pro accounts, initially for single-item orders from Etsy merchants, with plans to add multi-item purchases and stores built on Shopify, SiliconANGLE reported on September 29, 2025. OpenAI said more than 700 million people use ChatGPT every week, according to the same report.

The feature runs on the Agentic Commerce Protocol, which OpenAI open-sourced and developed with Stripe. Merchants using Stripe can add support with one line of code, and orders placed in ChatGPT are sent to the retailer, which processes the transaction through its own systems, according to the same report.

Etsy shares rose 16% and Shopify closed up more than 6% on the news, according to the same report. Wider international availability is planned for later, iPhone in Canada reported the same day.

Why it matters for brands

ChatGPT moves from recommending products to selling them. Shoppers who ask for a recommendation can now buy in the same conversation, which shortens the path from question to purchase.

The merchant keeps the transaction. Because orders pass to the retailer’s own systems, brands selling on their own sites or through Shopify can take orders from ChatGPT without a marketplace in between.

The protocol is open. Other AI tools could adopt the same standard, which would make product data and checkout readiness matter across many assistants, not only ChatGPT.

What to do now

  1. Check that product data, prices and availability on your own site are complete and accurate, since assistants read them.
  2. For Shopify or Stripe merchants, review how and when Instant Checkout will be available, and test it on a few products.
  3. Track traffic and orders from ChatGPT separately, to measure what this new channel delivers.

We will look at what an AI agent needs from a brand’s catalog in a post next week.

A0811.crumb: Prime Big Deal Days 2025 early read…
A0811.title: Prime Big Deal Days 2025 early read: smaller baskets, preliminary
A0811.alt: Taped cardboard boxes and two small pumpkins on a weathered bench beside a sunlit ochre wall and fallen leaves.
A0811.ttag: Prime Big Deal Days 2025 early read: smaller baskets, preliminary | Kwontified
A0811.desc: Early data from Prime Big Deal Days 2025 points to smaller orders focused on everyday essentials.
A0811.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 10, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0811.body:
Early data from Prime Big Deal Days 2025 points to smaller orders focused on everyday essentials. The average order was $45.42, and nearly half of shoppers said tariffs affected what they bought. These figures are preliminary and come from a shopper panel, not Amazon’s own sales data.

What happened

The average spend per order during Prime Big Deal Days was $45.42, with 44% of orders at $20 or less and 90% under $100, Numerator reported on October 9, 2025. More than half of shopping households placed two or more orders, and average household spend was about $104.69, according to the same release.

Shoppers cited costs. Nearly half, 48%, said tariffs affected their purchase decisions, and 61% said they also shopped Prime Day in July, according to Numerator’s survey of 5,120 verified buyers, fielded October 7 and 8.

Before the event, Adobe forecast that US online shoppers would spend $9 billion across retailers over the two days, up 6.2%, with discounts peaking at 17% off listed prices, Retail TouchPoints reported on October 6.

Why it matters for brands

Baskets were small and practical. Low-priced essentials dominated, which suggests shoppers used the event to stock up rather than to buy big-ticket gifts.

Cost concerns shaped behavior. With nearly half citing tariffs, value messaging and visible discounts mattered more than usual.

Many shoppers are repeat event buyers. Most also shopped in July, which means brands compete for the same deal-focused shoppers across events.

What to do now

  1. Compare your average order size and unit mix against these early figures, and note which products drove volume.
  2. Review deal performance on low-priced essentials versus higher-priced items before setting Black Friday deals.
  3. Treat these numbers as preliminary and update your read when fuller results are published.

We will compare the event against our forecast ranges when fuller results are available.
