A0813.title: Walmart partners with OpenAI to sell through ChatGPT Instant Checkout
A0813.alt: A blue shopping basket of bread, apples, milk, and a bottle on a yellow stool against a bright blue wall.
A0813.ttag: Walmart partners with OpenAI to sell through ChatGPT Instant Checkout | Kwontified
A0813.desc: Walmart announced on October 14 that it will let customers and Sam’s Club members buy its products inside ChatGPT, using OpenAI’s Instant Checkout.
A0813.byline: By Kwontified. Published Oct 15, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0813.body:
Walmart announced on October 14 that it will let customers and Sam’s Club members buy its products inside ChatGPT, using OpenAI’s Instant Checkout. The feature is due this fall and will include items from Walmart’s third-party sellers. For brands, the largest US retailer is now inside the leading AI assistant, which raises the stakes for product data on Walmart’s marketplace.

What happened

Walmart will join Shopify, Etsy and Salesforce in linking its catalog to ChatGPT’s Instant Checkout, with the integration taking effect later this fall for both Walmart and Sam’s Club, Retail TouchPoints reported on October 14, 2025.

A Walmart spokesperson said the feature will offer a wide range of Walmart items as well as clothing, entertainment and food from third-party sellers, with Sam’s Club items following soon after, CNN reported the same day.

Walmart said customers will be able to plan meals, restock household items and find new products through ChatGPT, describing the experience as a way to “simply chat and buy,” Digital Commerce 360 reported on October 14.

Why it matters for brands

Walmart’s marketplace sellers are included. Products from third-party sellers will be available through ChatGPT, so brands selling on Walmart may reach shoppers in the assistant without separate integration.

Replenishment fits the format. Restocking household items and planning meals are repeat purchases, which favors brands with strong positions in everyday categories.

Product data carries more weight. An assistant choosing among Walmart products relies on titles, attributes, prices and stock, so gaps in Walmart listings could keep products out of recommendations.

What to do now

  1. Review your Walmart listings for complete attributes, accurate prices and current stock before the feature launches.
  2. Identify which of your products are frequent repeat purchases, and make sure they are in stock and well described.
  3. Plan to track any change in Walmart orders once the ChatGPT integration goes live.

We will look at why Walmart wants to be inside ChatGPT in a post later this week.

A0823.crumb: Amazon sues Perplexity to stop its Comet…
A0823.title: Amazon sues Perplexity to stop its Comet agent shopping on Amazon
A0823.alt: A white six-wheeled delivery robot with its lid open carries a cardboard parcel on a sidewalk by a lilac wall.
A0823.ttag: Amazon sues Perplexity to stop its Comet agent shopping on Amazon | Kwontified
A0823.desc: Amazon sued Perplexity on November 4 to stop the startup’s Comet browser agent from buying products on Amazon for its users.
A0823.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 5, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0823.body:
Amazon sued Perplexity on November 4 to stop the startup’s Comet browser agent from buying products on Amazon for its users. Amazon accuses Perplexity of computer fraud because Comet does not disclose when it is shopping on a real person’s behalf. For brands, the case is an early legal test of whether outside AI agents can shop on retailers’ sites without permission.

What happened

Amazon filed a lawsuit in San Francisco federal court demanding that Perplexity stop allowing Comet to make purchases on Amazon for users, Bloomberg reported on November 4, 2025.

Amazon accuses Perplexity of committing computer fraud by failing to disclose when Comet is shopping on a real person’s behalf, in violation of Amazon’s terms of service, according to the complaint, as reported by Bloomberg.

The case follows earlier steps by Amazon to keep outside AI agents away. Amazon had already added crawlers from Anthropic’s Claude, Perplexity and Google’s Project Mariner agents, and later six more AI-related crawlers, to the list its robots.txt file asks to stay away, Modern Retail reported on August 21. Those instructions are advisory, not enforceable, according to the same report.

Why it matters for brands

The lawsuit moves the dispute from technical signals to the courts. Robots.txt asks agents to stay away; a court order could require it. The outcome will shape how freely outside agents can act on Amazon.

Brands may lose a route to shoppers using agents. If outside agents cannot shop on Amazon, shoppers who rely on them will buy where agents are welcome, such as retailers that have partnered with AI assistants.

Amazon’s own tools gain ground. Shoppers who want AI help on Amazon will use Amazon’s assistants, which sit alongside Amazon’s advertising.

What to do now

  1. Track how much of your traffic and sales come from AI assistants on each channel.
  2. Make sure listings on retailers that welcome agents are complete and current, since that is where agent shoppers may go.
  3. Follow the case, since a ruling will set expectations for agent access across retail.

We will look at what the dispute means for who gets to shop on the shopper’s behalf in a post this week.

A0827.title: Amazon sets Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday for November 20 to December 1
A0827.alt: A stack of twine-tied kraft parcels beside a small potted fir tree against a green wall.
A0827.ttag: Amazon sets Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday for November 20 to December 1 | Kwontified
A0827.desc: Amazon announced on November 10 that its Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday deal events will run from November 20 through December 1, a 12-day window.
A0827.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 11, 2025. 1-minute read.
A0827.body:
Amazon announced on November 10 that its Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday deal events will run from November 20 through December 1, a 12-day window. For brands, the dates fix the period for final budgets, bids and stock, with deals already submitted by the October 28 deadline.

What happened

Amazon said its Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday deal events will run from November 20 through December 1, in a release on Business Wire on November 10, 2025.

Amazon said the events would offer deep discounts across more than 35 categories, RTTNews reported the same day. The 2024 event ran from November 21 to December 2, JOE reported on November 10.

Why it matters for brands

The window is long. Twelve days spread shoppers and advertisers over more time, as the four-day Prime Day did in July, so pacing matters more than a single-day push.

Peaks will still cluster. Black Friday on November 28 and Cyber Monday on December 1 sit inside the window, so budgets should be weighted toward those days rather than spread evenly.

Most decisions are already made. Deals were due by October 28, so the remaining levers are bids, budgets, listings and stock.

What to do now

  1. Set daily budgets across November 20 to December 1, weighted toward Black Friday and Cyber Monday, with a reserve for strong performers.
  2. Confirm stock on deal products against the 12-day window, and shift spend away from items running low.
  3. Refresh listings and check that accepted deals are live and correctly priced when the event begins.

We will publish our Cyber Week forecast ranges for sales lift, cost per click and deal share this week.

A0831.title: Amazon unBoxed 2025: the announcements that matter for brands
A0831.alt: A spotlight on a stand aimed at a plain white box on a white plinth against a navy blue wall.
A0831.ttag: Amazon unBoxed 2025: the announcements that matter for brands | Kwontified
A0831.desc: At unBoxed 2025 in Nashville on November 11 and 12, Amazon Ads merged its Sponsored Ads console and Amazon DSP into a single Campaign Manager, introduced…
A0831.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 13, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0831.body:
At unBoxed 2025 in Nashville on November 11 and 12, Amazon Ads merged its Sponsored Ads console and Amazon DSP into a single Campaign Manager, introduced AI agents for building campaigns and creative, and opened a unified reporting experience in beta. For brands, upper-funnel and search advertising are moving onto one platform, with AI handling more of the setup.

What happened

Amazon is collapsing Amazon DSP and Sponsored Ads into a unified Campaign Manager, alongside an AI-powered Ads Agent and a Creative Agent, The Drum reported on November 11, 2025. Kelly MacLean, who leads Amazon’s ad technology, said the tools would operate as a “crystal box, not a black box,” according to the same report.

Amazon Ads also announced a unified reporting experience in open beta, letting advertisers filter and combine data across ad products, accounts and countries, PPC Land reported on November 12. Daily data is available for 15 months and monthly data for up to six years, and managed-service DSP accounts will gain access in the first quarter of 2026, according to the same report.

Why it matters for brands

Search and upper-funnel advertising now sit together. Brands that ran Sponsored Ads and DSP separately can plan, buy and report them in one place, which makes full-funnel budgets easier to manage and compare.

AI takes on more setup. Agents that build campaigns and creative can save time, but brands still need to review what they produce and keep control of targeting and budgets.

Reporting gets longer memory. Fifteen months of daily data makes year-over-year event comparisons easier, including the Cyber Week window now starting.

What to do now

  1. Review how your Sponsored Ads and DSP budgets are planned, and decide whether to manage them together in Campaign Manager.
  2. Test Ads Agent and Creative Agent on a small set of campaigns, and review every output before it goes live.
  3. Use the unified reports to compare this Cyber Week with 2024 on a daily basis.

We will look at what unBoxed 2025 changes for advertisers in a post next week.

A0829.title: Amazon Ads opens a closed beta of an MCP server for AI agents
A0829.alt: A gray fabric smart speaker beside a bowl of lemons and a notepad on a sunlit wooden table against a sage wall.
A0829.ttag: Amazon Ads opens a closed beta of an MCP server for AI agents | Kwontified
A0829.desc: Amazon Ads announced on November 13 a closed beta of a server that lets AI agents work with its advertising platform through the Model Context Protocol,…
A0829.byline: By Kwontified. Published Nov 14, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0829.body:
Amazon Ads announced on November 13 a closed beta of a server that lets AI agents work with its advertising platform through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard. Agents such as Claude, ChatGPT and Amazon Q can query campaigns, pull reports and change settings in plain language. For brands, it is an early sign that campaign management will increasingly run through AI tools that need clear permissions.

What happened

Amazon Ads announced a closed beta of its Model Context Protocol server, a standard access layer that connects AI models and agents to its advertising platform, PPC Land reported on November 13, 2025. Agents can query campaign performance, access account information, generate reports and update settings such as budgets through natural language, according to the same report.

The server supports Amazon DSP, sponsored ads and Amazon Marketing Cloud, and organizes its tools into four groups: account management, billing, campaign management and reporting, according to the same report. Administrators can restrict agents to read-only tools, the report said.

Advertisers can connect through Claude, ChatGPT, Amazon Q, Amazon Bedrock and other compatible applications, and Amazon said it does not own or operate the AI applications that connect, according to PPC Land. Access is limited during the beta and can be requested through Amazon’s developer portal.

Why it matters for brands

Campaign work is moving into AI tools. Tasks that once needed the console, spreadsheets or developers can be asked for in plain language, which speeds up analysis and routine changes.

Permissions become a control point. An agent that can change budgets can also make costly mistakes. The ability to restrict agents to read-only tools gives brands a safe starting point.

Data access widens. Brands and their partners can connect the AI tools they already use, rather than relying only on Amazon’s console.

What to do now

  1. Decide which AI tools, if any, should access your Amazon Ads account, and who approves them.
  2. Start with read-only access for reporting and analysis before allowing any changes.
  3. Keep a log of changes made by agents, and review it alongside your usual account checks.

We will look at what unBoxed 2025 and these agent tools change for advertisers in a post next week.

A0839.desc: US shoppers spent $44.2 billion online over Cyber Week 2025, up 7.7% from 2024, according to early data from Adobe.
A0839.byline: By Kwontified. Published Dec 3, 2025. 2-minute read.
A0839.body:
US shoppers spent $44.2 billion online over Cyber Week 2025, up 7.7% from 2024, according to early data from Adobe. Cyber Monday was again the biggest day, but Black Friday grew faster for the second year in a row. These figures cover all US retailers and are preliminary; brand-level Amazon results will vary.

What happened

Shoppers spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday, up 7.1%, slightly above Adobe’s projection, Adobe said in a release on December 2, 2025. Across the five days from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, online spending reached $44.2 billion, up 7.7%, according to the same release.

Black Friday set a record at $11.8 billion, up 9.1%, the weekend brought $11.8 billion, up 8.7%, and Thanksgiving reached $6.4 billion, up 5.3%, according to Adobe. Black Friday outgrew Cyber Monday for the second consecutive season as shoppers took advantage of earlier deals, Adobe said.

Discounts ran deep. On Cyber Monday, electronics discounts peaked at 31% off listed prices, toys at 28% and apparel at 25%, according to the same release. Buy now, pay later accounted for $1.03 billion of Cyber Monday spending, up 4.2%.

Why it matters for brands

Early deals pulled demand forward. Black Friday’s faster growth shows shoppers responding to deals earlier in the window, which favors brands that had stock, deals and advertising ready from the start.

Discounts did the work. Deep discounts in electronics, toys and apparel drove spending, so growth may have come at the cost of margin for many sellers.

Electronics led. Electronics were the largest Cyber Monday category, which fits shoppers who waited for holiday prices after cautious buying earlier in the year.

What to do now

  1. Compare your own Cyber Week sales by day with the market pattern, especially Black Friday against Cyber Monday.
  2. Review margin as well as revenue on deal products before planning December promotions.
  3. Treat these figures as preliminary and update your read as brand-level and Amazon-specific data arrives.

We will grade the event against our Cyber Week forecast ranges next week.

A0866.title: Amazon Ads opens its MCP server for AI agents to all API partners
A0866.alt: A white six-wheeled delivery robot with its lid open carries a cardboard parcel on a sidewalk by a lilac wall.
A0866.ttag: Amazon Ads opens its MCP server for AI agents to all API partners | Kwontified
A0866.desc: Amazon Ads moved its Model Context Protocol server, which lets AI tools query and manage advertising accounts in plain language, from closed beta to open…
A0866.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 3, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0866.body:
Amazon Ads moved its Model Context Protocol server, which lets AI tools query and manage advertising accounts in plain language, from closed beta to open beta on February 2, 2026. The server is now available to Amazon Ads API partners with active credentials. Brands working with tools or agencies that connect to it should set clear rules for what AI agents may change.

What happened

Paula Despins, Amazon Ads’ vice president of ads measurement, announced that the Amazon Ads MCP Server had entered open beta, PPC Land reported on February 2, 2026. The server and its tools are available globally to Amazon Ads partners with active API credentials, according to the same report.

The move follows a closed beta that began on November 13, 2025, which allowed AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to query and manage campaigns in plain language, PPC Land reported at the time.

The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to outside software. Amazon’s server translates requests from those assistants into actions in the Amazon Ads system, such as pulling reports or adjusting campaigns.

Why it matters for brands

Agents can now do real work. With the server open to all API partners, more agencies and software providers can let AI assistants build reports, change bids and create campaigns through conversation rather than manual steps.

Control becomes the key question. An agent that can change budgets and bids can also make costly mistakes. Brands need to know which tools connect to their accounts and what those tools are allowed to do.

The work of advertising teams shifts. Routine setup and reporting can move to agents, leaving people to set goals, review changes and measure results independently.

What to do now

  1. Ask your agency and software providers whether they connect to the Amazon Ads MCP server, and what actions their agents can take.
  2. Start with read-only access, and require human approval for budget and bid changes.
  3. Keep a log of every change an agent makes, and review it weekly against results.

A0877.byline: By Kwontified. Published Feb 26, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0877.body:
Amazon Ads launched Creative Agent in Canada on February 25, 2026, giving Canadian advertisers an AI tool that researches, writes and produces video and display ads through conversation. Brands advertising on Amazon.ca can now produce new creative far faster than before, and should set review standards before using it at scale.

What happened

Amazon Ads announced that Creative Agent is available to advertisers in Canada inside Creative Studio, where advertisers can click “chat” to work with an AI partner that conducts product and audience research, brainstorms ideas, develops storyboards and produces video and display ads, Amazon said in a February 25 announcement.

The tool is offered at no additional cost and helps advertisers produce ads in hours rather than the weeks and large budgets creative work often requires, according to the same announcement. It builds multi-scene videos and display ads, with animations, music and voiceovers, for use across Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display, Amazon DSP, Brand Stores and Streaming TV.

Creative Agent is built on foundation models available on Amazon Bedrock, including Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude, and advertisers can edit and direct the work at every stage, Amazon said. The launch coincided with Amazon Ads’ second unBoxed event in Toronto.

Why it matters for brands

Creative is no longer the bottleneck. Many brands run few video or display ads because production is slow and expensive. A tool that produces finished ads in hours lowers that barrier, especially for smaller brands.

More creative means more testing. Brands can try several concepts for the same product and keep what performs, instead of relying on a single expensive production.

Quality control still matters. AI-produced ads can drift from brand guidelines or make claims that need checking. Review standards should be in place before volume rises.

What to do now

  1. Test Creative Agent on a few products with clear brand guidelines and approved claims.
  2. Review every ad before launch for accuracy, tone and compliance with Canadian rules.
  3. Run new concepts against existing ads and keep the ones that improve results.

A0886.ttag: Bloomberg reports Amazon will move Prime Day to late June | Kwontified
A0886.desc: Amazon plans to move its Prime Day sale from July to late June, Bloomberg News reported on March 12, 2026.
A0886.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 13, 2026. 1-minute read.
A0886.body:
Amazon plans to move its Prime Day sale from July to late June, Bloomberg News reported on March 12, 2026. If the report is right, brands lose several weeks of preparation time, so deal submissions, inventory shipments and budgets should be planned now rather than on a July timeline.

What happened

Amazon is planning to move its Prime Day sale event up to late June, marking a rare shift in calendar for the decade-old shopping event, Reuters reported on March 12, citing Bloomberg News.

The shift would move Prime Day sales into Amazon’s second quarter, which typically ends on June 30, according to the Reuters report. Amazon declined to comment to Reuters.

Amazon has not announced official dates. Prime Day has traditionally run in July, and the 2025 event lasted four days.

Why it matters for brands

Preparation windows shrink. Deal submission deadlines and inventory shipment cutoffs come weeks before the event. A late-June Prime Day pulls those deadlines into May.

Inventory is the biggest risk. Stock that would have arrived at Amazon’s warehouses in time for a July event may arrive too late for June.

Budgets and calendars need to shift. Brands that plan second-quarter and third-quarter budgets separately will need to move Prime Day spending into the second quarter.

What to do now

  1. Plan Prime Day on a late-June timeline, and move deal and inventory deadlines forward by several weeks.
  2. Check whether stock for Prime Day items can reach Amazon’s warehouses by late May.
  3. Shift Prime Day advertising budgets into the second quarter, and watch for Amazon’s official announcement.

A0882.desc: Amazon announced on March 16, 2026, that its third Big Spring Sale will run from March 25 to March 31.
A0882.byline: By Kwontified. Published Mar 17, 2026. 1-minute read.
A0882.body:
Amazon announced on March 16, 2026, that its third Big Spring Sale will run from March 25 to March 31. Brands have about a week to finalize budgets, stock and advertising for the event, and those without approved deals should focus on protecting visibility rather than chasing discount shoppers.

What happened

Amazon officially announced the 2026 Big Spring Sale, which goes live at 12:01 a.m. Pacific time on March 25 and runs for a full week until March 31, 9to5Toys reported on March 16.

The dates match the 2025 event. Amazon had already advised US sellers on February 18 to prepare for its spring event and to submit deals by the deadline, EcommerceBytes reported, updating its coverage on March 16 when the dates were confirmed.

The Big Spring Sale is Amazon’s first major sale of the year. The inaugural event ran March 20 to 25, 2024.

Why it matters for brands

The window for deals has largely closed. Brands that submitted deals before Amazon’s deadline are set. Brands that missed it will compete against discounted products without a deal of their own.

Budgets need to be ready now. A week of notice leaves little time to adjust campaigns, so budgets and bids for deal items should be set before March 25.

Stock decides who benefits. Deal items that sell out early lose the rest of the week’s demand.

What to do now

  1. Raise budgets on approved deal items for March 25 to 31, and set daily caps that will last the full week.
  2. Check stock levels for deal items against the expected lift.
  3. Protect branded search and best sellers if you have no deals, rather than raising bids to chase discount shoppers.

A0907.body:
Amazon confirmed on April 29, 2026 that Prime Day will take place in June 2026, earlier than its usual July timing, but it has not yet given exact dates. Brands should plan deals, inventory and budgets on a June timeline now, rather than waiting for the dates.

What happened

Amazon officially announced that Prime Day 2026 will take place in June, 9to5Toys reported on April 29. Prime Day has typically run in July, and Amazon announced the month without giving specific dates, according to the report.

The event will cover 26 countries, including the United States, Canada, Mexico, the United Kingdom and much of Europe, with Prime members in Australia, Brazil, India and Japan able to shop Prime Day deals later in the summer, according to the same report.

The announcement confirms an earlier report. Amazon planned to move Prime Day to late June, which would shift the event’s sales into Amazon’s second quarter, Bloomberg News reported, according to a March 12 Reuters report.

Why it matters for brands

Deadlines move earlier. Deal submissions, inventory shipments and creative production all come weeks before the event. A June Prime Day pulls those deadlines into May.

Inventory is the biggest risk. Stock planned for a July event may not reach Amazon’s warehouses in time for June, and missing stock means missing the event.

Budgets shift between quarters. Brands that plan second-quarter and third-quarter budgets separately will need to move Prime Day spending into the second quarter.

The length is not yet known. The 2025 event lasted four days, and Amazon has not said how long the 2026 event will run.

What to do now

  1. Plan Prime Day on a June timeline, and confirm deal and inventory deadlines with Amazon.
  2. Check that stock for Prime Day items can reach Amazon’s warehouses in time.
  3. Move Prime Day advertising budgets into the second quarter, and watch for Amazon’s announcement of exact dates.

A0915.alt: A white six-wheeled delivery robot with its lid open carries a cardboard parcel on a sidewalk by a lilac wall.
A0915.ttag: Amazon releases a local MCP package for Selling Partner API developers | Kwontified
A0915.desc: Amazon’s Selling Partner Developer Services team released Local MCP for SP-API on May 28, 2026, a package that lets AI coding assistants search Amazon’s…
A0915.byline: By Kwontified. Published May 29, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0915.body:
Amazon’s Selling Partner Developer Services team released Local MCP for SP-API on May 28, 2026, a package that lets AI coding assistants search Amazon’s seller API documentation, generate code and build multi-step workflows. Brands that run their own Amazon data and automation should test it with developers, with tight control over credentials and approvals.

What happened

Amazon announced the package in a May 28 post on its Selling Partner API samples repository. Local MCP for SP-API is a single npm package that bundles two MCP servers, which connect AI assistants to tools and documentation for the Selling Partner API (SP-API), the interface sellers and vendors use to automate listings, orders, inventory and reports.

The first server is a development assistant. It lets an AI assistant search official SP-API documentation in natural language, browse the endpoint catalog, generate code samples in Python, Java, JavaScript, C# and PHP, review integration code for problems such as rate limiting and error handling, and guide migrations between API versions, according to the post.

The second server builds workflows. Developers describe a multi-step process in natural language, such as checking inventory and creating a replenishment shipment when stock runs low, and the tool builds and runs the workflow, the post said.

Most tools run locally without credentials, but tools that make live API calls require SP-API credentials, according to Amazon. The package works with AI tools such as Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code that support the Model Context Protocol.

Why it matters for brands

Building on Amazon data gets easier. Brands with in-house developers can use AI assistants to write and maintain SP-API integrations faster, including updates when Amazon changes its API versions.

Automation moves closer to the business. Workflow tools let teams describe processes, such as replenishment or order updates, in plain language rather than writing every step by hand.

Control matters more. Tools that can call live APIs can change listings, orders and shipments. Brands need clear rules for credentials, testing and approval before automated workflows touch live accounts.

It follows Amazon’s advertising move. Amazon Ads opened an MCP server for advertising in February 2026, PPC Land reported on February 2, 2026. Amazon now offers AI agent connections on both the advertising and selling sides.

What to do now

  1. Ask developers to test the package in a sandbox or test account before connecting live credentials.
  2. Set rules for which workflows can run automatically and which need human approval.
  3. Review existing SP-API integrations for upcoming version migrations, using the migration tools.

A0922.ttag: Amazon announces Prime Day 2026 for June 23-26 | Kwontified
A0922.desc: Amazon announced on June 2, 2026 that Prime Day will run for four days, from June 23 through June 26, with early deals already live.
A0922.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 3, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0922.body:
Amazon announced on June 2, 2026 that Prime Day will run for four days, from June 23 through June 26, with early deals already live. Brands have three weeks to lock in stock, deals and budgets for each day of the event.

What happened

Prime Day 2026 will run from June 23 through June 26, offering four days of deals for Prime members across more than 35 categories, beginning at 12:01 a.m. Pacific time on June 23, iClarified reported on June 2, citing Amazon’s announcement. Amazon said early deals are already available.

Amazon will release new deals during the event. A feature called Today’s Big Deals will add limited-time offers three times a day, at 12 a.m., 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. Pacific time, and new deals will appear as often as every five minutes during select periods, according to the report.

Amazon’s AI assistant plays a role. Prime members can use Alexa for Shopping to create a personalized Prime Day deals guide, set deal and price alerts, check price history and automatically buy eligible items when they reach a target price, the report said.

The event covers 22 countries, including the United States, Canada, Mexico, the United Kingdom and much of Europe, with Prime members in Australia, Brazil, India and Japan able to shop Prime Day deals later in the summer.

Why it matters for brands

The calendar is now fixed. Brands that planned for a range of June dates can now set stock arrival, deal and advertising schedules against exact days.

Four days need pacing. With the same four-day length as 2025, brands should set budgets for each day and keep spend for the final day.

Deal drops change the rhythm. Scheduled releases of limited-time deals three times a day may create spikes in traffic, so brands should watch daily and hourly results.

Price tracking is easier for shoppers. Price history and target-price purchases through Alexa for Shopping make it easier for shoppers to judge deals, so discounts need to be genuine.

What to do now

  1. Confirm that Prime Day stock will reach Amazon’s warehouses before June 23.
  2. Set advertising budgets for each of the four days, and protect spend for June 26.
  3. Check that deal prices are real reductions from recent prices, since shoppers can see price history.

A0935.ttag: Early read: Prime Day 2026 opened with a record $8.3 billion day | Kwontified
A0935.desc: This is a preliminary read based on public data available before final results.
A0935.byline: By Kwontified. Published Jun 29, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0935.body:
This is a preliminary read based on public data available before final results. US online spending reached $8.3 billion on the first day of Prime Day 2026, up 5.3% from the first day of 2025, and Adobe reaffirmed its forecast of $26.3 billion for the four-day event. Brands should treat these figures as early signals and wait for final results before judging their own performance.

What happened

Day one set a record. US retailers drove $8.3 billion in online spending on June 23, the first day of Prime Day 2026, up 5.3% from $7.9 billion on the first day of Prime Day 2025 and the biggest e-commerce day of 2026 so far, according to Adobe data reported by Chain Store Age on June 24, 2026.

Adobe held its forecast. Because day one tracked ahead of its projections, Adobe reaffirmed its forecast that US retailers would drive $26.3 billion in online spending across the four-day event from June 23 to 26, up 9% from a year earlier, according to the same report.

Mobile and AI rose. Mobile shopping drove a record 51.2% of first-day online sales, or $4.24 billion, and traffic from AI sources had an add-to-cart rate 33% higher than other sources, according to Adobe.

The event was earlier and focused on essentials. Amazon positioned Prime Day as a vehicle for grocery and household essentials deals, and the June dates were earlier than the July timing Amazon had used for five consecutive years, Quartz reported on June 24, 2026.

Why it matters for brands

Early numbers are not final. The first-day figure covers one of four days and all US retailers, not Amazon alone. Final results will show whether growth held through the event.

The growth rate is modest. A 5.3% first-day increase and a 9% full-event forecast are well below the 30.3% growth of 2025, when the event doubled in length. That fits an event of the same four-day length.

AI shoppers are worth watching. Higher add-to-cart rates from AI traffic suggest assistants are becoming a meaningful path to purchase during big events.

What to do now

  1. Pull your own daily results for all four days before comparing them with market figures.
  2. Compare day-by-day pacing with your plan, and note where budgets ran short or went unspent.
  3. Wait for final results before drawing conclusions about Prime Day 2026 growth.

Amazon will hold Prime Big Deal Days on October 6 and 7, 2026, and Target set its Circle Deal Days for the same two days. Sellers committed their offers before the dates were public. Brands should now set ad budgets, pricing and daily pacing for a two-day overlap with Target.

What happened

Amazon set the dates. Prime Big Deal Days will run for 48 hours from 12:01 a.m. PDT on October 6, with Prime member-exclusive deals across more than 35 categories, Amazon announced on September 14, 2026.

Deals will arrive in waves. New deals will drop three times a day under the Today’s Big Deals banner, according to Amazon. Shoppers can ask Alexa for Shopping to set deal alerts and to buy an item automatically at a target price, Amazon said.

Target matched the dates. Target Circle Deal Days will run October 6 to 7 with discounts of up to 40% for members of its free Target Circle program, and paid Target Circle 360 members get early access beginning October 5, RTTNews reported on September 15, 2026.

The overlap repeats 2025. That October, Walmart Deals ran from October 7 to 12 and Target Circle Week from October 5 to 11, alongside Amazon’s event, Retail Dive reported on September 23, 2025.

Commitments came first. Deal submissions for Prime Big Deal Days closed on September 8, according to EcomCrew’s report on Amazon’s July 7 calendar, so offers were set before the dates were public.

Inventory windows are closing. The final FBA inbound deadline for the event, using Amazon-optimized shipment splits, was September 16, according to the same report. Brands that missed it must rely on stock already in place.

Three deal drops a day change pacing. Ad budgets that run out early on each day could miss later deal windows.

Automated purchases bypass search. A purchase triggered by a target price skips sponsored results, so some event sales will not reflect ad spend.

What to do now

  1. Confirm which deals were accepted and match ad budgets to each deal window.
  2. Check prices across Amazon and Target for products featured in both events.
  3. Set daily budget caps that leave room for all three deal drops each day.

Amazon used Accelerate 2026 to give its Seller Assistant always-on workflows, open it to outside AI tools starting with Claude, and let sellers manage eBay, Shopify, TikTok Shop and Walmart sales from Seller Central. Brands should decide which tasks an agent may act on, set approval rules before switching workflows on, and weigh what connecting other channels shares with Amazon.

What happened

Seller Assistant now works without being asked. Amazon introduced Seller Assistant workflows, automations that monitor conditions and respond even when the seller is not logged in to Seller Central, Amazon announced on September 23, 2026. Sellers set guardrails and choose whether a workflow only recommends or also acts, approving actions first, with every action logged, according to Amazon.

It remembers the business. Seller Assistant now keeps a persistent memory of each seller’s pricing patterns, inventory cycles and growth goals, Amazon said. The assistant has rolled out to over 90% of Amazon’s selling partners, and sellers accept its recommendations more than 90% of the time, according to the company.

Outside AI tools can now act on Amazon accounts. A new Selling Partner plugin connects a seller’s listings, performance metrics, inventory and sales data to Amazon Quick and, in beta, Anthropic’s Claude, and can take actions as Seller Assistant does, with human approval and audit trails, Amazon said. For now it is available to sellers in Amazon’s US stores.

Seller Central now reaches rival marketplaces. On September 24, Amazon announced tools that let sellers connect eBay, Shopify, TikTok Shop and Walmart accounts and manage listings, orders and profitability inside Seller Central, rolling out gradually in the US at no extra cost, EcomCrew reported on September 24.

Why it matters for brands

Agents can now change prices and listings unattended. That helps only within guardrails a brand has thought through.

Approval rules become a control point. The choice between recommend-only and act-with-approval decides how much a brand’s team must review each day.

Outside tools gain write access. That makes access permissions a security question.

Connecting channels shares data. Linking Walmart or TikTok Shop accounts gives Amazon a view of sales on channels it does not run, which brands should weigh against convenience.

What to do now

  1. List the routine tasks you would let an agent recommend, and the few you would let it perform with approval.
  2. Set price floors, stock limits and approval owners before switching any workflow on.
  3. Review who can connect AI tools and other channels to your Seller Central account.

A0978.desc: Amazon Ads replaced its ad console and Amazon DSP with a single platform called Amazon Ads Agent and organized buying into three campaign types, with AI…
A0978.byline: By Kwontified. Published Sep 30, 2026. 2-minute read.
A0978.body:
Amazon Ads replaced its ad console and Amazon DSP with a single platform called Amazon Ads Agent and organized buying into three campaign types, with AI handling more of the targeting and placement. Brands should decide which campaigns to hand to automation, keep a manual test running alongside it, and set the measures they will judge it by before moving budget.

What happened

Amazon renamed and merged its buying tools. Amazon Ads unveiled Amazon Ads Agent, which replaces the former Ads Console and Amazon DSP experience and adds a conversational chat that lets advertisers ask questions in natural language, MediaPost reported on September 29, 2026, the day of the announcement at Amazon’s unBoxed conference.

Buying now runs through three campaign types. Advertisers choose among Sponsored Ads, Display, Video and Audio (DVA+), and Full-Funnel Campaigns, according to the report.

DVA+ asks for a goal, not a plan. Advertisers select a goal such as driving sales or traffic, add products, set a budget, and Amazon’s AI places ads across streaming TV, online video, display and audio on Amazon and the open internet, the report said.

The launch comes under scrutiny. A month earlier, the Federal Trade Commission and 22 states sued Amazon, alleging inflated advertising prices, which Amazon denied, the Associated Press reported on August 31.

Why it matters for brands

Control moves to the platform. When advertisers set goals and Amazon chooses placements, brands lose some of the levers they used to pull directly.

Comparison gets harder. Results reported across formats inside one campaign are harder to compare with earlier campaigns built channel by channel.

Smaller brands gain access. Programmatic video and audio placements that once needed a dedicated team now sit behind a simpler setup.

Pricing questions remain open. With an auction lawsuit pending, brands should watch how clearly Amazon explains what they pay.

What to do now

  1. Keep at least one manually managed campaign as a benchmark before shifting budget into automated campaign types.
  2. Define the results you will judge automation by, such as new-to-brand sales and cost per sale, before you test it.
  3. Ask your Amazon Ads team what placement and cost reporting each campaign type provides.
